Its warning then asserts 'the recorded temperature value' when no temperature was recorded and no sensor was read -- so a guard built to prevent misleading numbers is itself making an unsupported claim, and doing it on nearly 5% of answers.
Root_Cause: Same class as BUG-191, where a grader counted the '2' inside 'bldg2' as a sensor reading. Digits appearing in text are being treated as measurements without checking whether any measurement was actually taken. The proximate trigger is upstream: questions like 'Is it too hot in here?' are routed to the capability lane (BUG-225), answered from a document, and the numeric guard then runs over document prose it was never meant to see.
Fix_Approach: Scoped the guard by the evidence record's OPERATION -- the condition it needed, which did not exist when it was written and does now (V6-T02). Numbers are readings for an observation, a calculation over observations, a forecast or an estimate; they are not readings for an authoritative lookup of a document, a register or a booking. Scoped by what IS a measurement rather than by listing what is not, so a new lookup-shaped operation does not silently start being guarded again. Fails OPEN: with no record the guard runs exactly as before, because not knowing is not a reason to stop guarding. The plausible RANGE was deliberately not widened -- 800 degC is impossible and the check is correct; only its trigger was wrong.
Verification: Re-measured after the routing fixes FIRST, as planned: 73/1562 (4.7%) -> 10/309 (3.2%), so the routing work halved it on its own and the survivors were confirmed to be the same defect (800/1000/300 = the HVAC document's CO2 and TVOC thresholds; 76026, 6026, 4444). 3 tests including one asserting the plausible range was NOT widened to accommodate the bug. Full suite 2564 pass. Live effect lands with the next deploy.

Title: Graph-structure questions land in the document lane instead of the ontology
Description: The largest single routing gap, found while decomposing the capability lane for BUG-225. Of 1,562 answered baseline questions, 887 reach capability WITHOUT naming any measurand, and 746 of those (48% of the entire corpus) are questions the ontology can answer directly: 'Which zones does AHU-3 serve?', 'What's actually in Room 2.14 - is it a lab or a meeting room?', 'Do we have any sensors on the fourth floor, and what do they measure?'. These name entities and relationships that exist as triples, and they are answered from a five-document corpus instead. BUG-225 cannot reach them: its test is whether the question names a MEASURAND, and these name an ENTITY. Remaining slices of the same 887: 41 booking/availability questions that belong to the events lane, 21 wayfinding questions that belong to spatial/floor_plan, and ~79 that are correctly in capability (amenity lookups and policy questions). [2026-08-22] DECOMPOSED. The remaining ~700 are NOT a single routing gap and must not be fixed as one. They split by destination: metadata/discovery (what's in a space, what an asset serves), spatial/floor_plan ('where is X' with no route words -- deliberately excluded from the wayfinding rule, which handles ROUTES, so a separate rule is owed), events/anomaly, and report/export. Each needs its own signal and its own measurement. [2026-08-22b] THE ACTUAL MECHANISM FOUND, and it is not the classifier. dialogue_agent runs a capability probe BEFORE the LLM, guarded by a bypass list; if nothing on that list fires and the capability resolver finds any matching fact, the question is answered from a document and the LLM never classifies it. Measured live: 'Take me to the nearest accessible toilet' went from arrival to intent=capability in 250ms -- far too fast for a model call. That probe is what held 87% of the corpus, and the routing contract never got a say. The bypass consults _DELIB_RE (which is why widening DELIBERATE_RE worked live) and is_spatial_query / is_floor_plan_query -- and measured, NEITHER of those matches a route question: 'take me to...', "where's the nearest fire exit..." and 'how do I get to...' all return False for both while WAYFIND_RE returns True. Route questions therefore had no bypass at all.
Root_Cause: There is no routing test for 'does this question name something that exists in the building's graph?'. The capability lane is the default destination for anything the classifier finds building-shaped but not obviously a reading, so entity and relationship questions fall into it and are answered from documents.
Fix_Approach: THE LOGGED DESIGN WAS TESTED AND REJECTED. It proposed one rule: a question naming a resolvable graph entity is a graph question. Built as a signal from the building's own instantiated Brick classes and tested against the 887 target questions, it fired on 45% with poor precision BOTH ways -- it claimed 'Where is the facility manager's office?' (wayfinding, not metadata) and stayed silent on 'What's actually in Room 2.14?', the case it was built for. The 746 are not one bug: they have at least four correct destinations (metadata, spatial, events, report), and firing them all into metadata would be worse than leaving them. WHAT WAS SHIPPED INSTEAD, after replaying the REAL contract offline over all 1,360 capability answers: the largest fixable cluster is two EXISTING rules whose patterns require the noun to sit immediately after the cue word, while real questions put an adjective there. 'the nearest ACCESSIBLE toilet' and 'the nearest FIRE exit' miss WAYFIND_RE; 'which STUDY spaces had the best air quality' misses DELIBERATE_RE. Both widened with a BOUNDED gap -- (?:\w+\s+){0,2}, two words, not .* -- so a pattern cannot run across a clause and claim an unrelated question. Added 'take me to' to wayfinding, 'desk/seat/spot' to the space nouns, a where's-a-quiet-place branch, and a narrow which-X-should-I-take branch that needs both a space noun and an explicit should-I verb. PART 3: added WAYFIND_RE to the pre-LLM probe's bypass list. Reused rather than widening is_spatial_query, because WAYFIND_RE is already the contract's definition of a route question and is what _r_wayfinding_spatial routes on -- two definitions of the same thing is the drift shape this codebase keeps paying for. Pinned by a source-level test, because the probe is an inline condition and its absence is invisible from outside: the answer looks fine.
Verification: Offline replay of the real contract over the 1,360 baseline capability answers: deliberate 0 -> 21, and the wayfinding rule now catches the cases it was missing. 14 new tests including five guard cases that must NOT fire and a test that the gap stays bounded. Also pinned: no control characters in the routing patterns -- a heredoc turned  into a literal backspace during this work, and the branch compiled, appeared in the pattern, and could never match because no question contains chr(8). Full suite 2549 pass. LIVE after deploy: 'Take me to the nearest accessible toilet' and "Where's the nearest fire exit" both reach spatial_query (were capability); 'Is there a bike storage in this building?' still reaches capability, so the guard holds. 17 routing tests added in total; full suite 2549 pass. [2026-08-22c] FINAL MEASUREMENT on a third 316-question capture (309 OK, 0 degraded). Questions reaching a data or spatial lane across the three runs: 5.9% (baseline) -> 34.2% (BUG-225) -> 36.9% (BUG-231 parts 1-3). Capability 88.5% -> 59.3% -> 57.3%. The BUG-231 changes contributed +2.7pp: deliberate 13 -> 20, spatial_query 3 -> 6. Modest next to BUG-225's +28pp, which is the honest read -- the shapes they fix (route questions, adjective-separated rankings) are a small share of the corpus, and the fixes are correct rather than large. Regression gate: 5 regressions, byte-identical to the set flagged after BUG-225, so BOTH BUG-231 changes introduced ZERO new regressions. The remaining 57.3% in capability is dominated by the graph-structure bucket this row keeps open. [2026-08-22d] THE REMAINDER IS MEASURED AND THE ROW'S PREMISE DOES NOT SURVIVE IT. The '746 graph-structure questions (48% of the corpus)' figure was derived from the PRE-ROUTING capture and was never re-derived after BUG-225 and parts 1-3 landed. Re-measured on the live post-routing capture (309 answered, everything on): 177 questions still reach capability, and of those the demonstrably misrouted slice is about twelve -- roughly 4% of the corpus, not 48%. 98% of the 177 carry NO measurand concept, so this is not the BUG-225 rule failing to fire; and only 6% of capability answers say 'no information', so the lane is answering rather than stalling. Reading the 177: a large share are correctly there -- 'How do I connect to the guest wifi', 'do your meeting rooms have induction loops', 'what time does the building close to visitors', 'it's my first day' -- amenity and policy questions, which is what the lane is for. A FOURTH SIGNAL WAS PROPOSED AND REJECTED ON EVIDENCE, like the three before it. The obvious lever was HBCO lay terms for presence words, since the resolver already carries busy / how busy / how many people / empty / available / unoccupied and the misses are specific words it lacks. Every candidate was measured against all 1,562 answered questions and every one failed: 'someone' 0 of 13 are occupancy questions (they are people-as-agents -- protocols, complaints, wheelchair assistance); 'anyone' 1 of 6 ('did anyone badge in' is an access log, 'would anyone notice' is hypothetical); 'people' is mostly people-as-agents too; 'crowded' would misroute 3 of the 5 it reaches, because 'which space is likely to be quieter and less crowded' wants deliberation, not a sensor reading; and 'free' is actively dangerous -- 62 hits, dominated by booking availability and by STEP-FREE accessibility routes, which a word-boundary match catches. Adding any of them would trade a document answer for a wrong lane. ONE GENUINE CONTRACT DEFECT WAS FOUND AND IS ALSO NOT WORTH A RULE: 'How does today's office temperature compare with the comfort standard?' resolves a measurand and still stays on capability, because _DOCUMENTARY_RE suppresses on the word 'standard'. It is a benchmark comparison, not a policy lookup. But questions carrying a documentary word AND a comparison shape number exactly ONE in 1,562, and a rule justified by n=1 is overfitting -- the failure mode this row has already produced three times. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT, stated so it is not rediscovered as '48% of the corpus': a small deliberation gap (constraint-ranking questions phrased as 'which X is likely to be quieter and less crowded' are not caught by _DELIB_RE), and the single benchmark-vs-standard case above. Both are P3-sized. Severity dropped from P1 to P3 accordingly.

Title: The referent extractor takes common words as room names
Description: Exposed by BUG-225 sending more questions down the data path. Of 77 questions now reaching sensor_data, 20 decline, and 12 of those decline because the entity extractor treated an ordinary word as a space name: 'has' (4x), 'conditions' (2x), 'feels', 'likely', 'best', 'suitable', 'plausibly', 'block B'. The user sees: 'I couldn't find "feels" in Abacws Building, so I can't return sensor data for it. Did you mean one of these zones: 0.01, 0.04, ...'. Pre-existing, not caused by the routing change -- the change made it visible by routing more questions through the extractor.
Root_Cause: `_WORDED_REF_RE` is r"\b(?:zone|room|space|node|area)\s+([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,23})" -- it captures WHATEVER WORD follows the location noun. Its comment calls the group an <id>, but English puts a verb there as readily as an identifier: 'this room FEELS stuffy', 'which room HAS the most daylight', 'a smaller approved room PLAUSIBLY reduce'.
Fix_Approach: NOT a narrower capture: requiring a digit would break 'room Atrium' on a building that names its spaces, and the pattern has to serve every building. The defect is what happens AFTER the graph lookup fails. A token that is not identifier-shaped AND is unknown to the graph was never a referent, so the resolver now returns NO_REFERENT and lets the rest of the question be answered, instead of declining by name on a word the user never used as a place. An identifier-shaped miss is unchanged: 'room 99.99' that does not exist is a real mistake and telling the user is the whole point of the gate.
Verification: 5 tests in tests/test_referent_resolver.py covering all four cases: the pattern still captures the word (documenting the cause rather than hiding it); a word-shaped unknown token yields NO_REFERENT with no message; 'room 99.99' still yields NOT_FOUND with a message; and a word-shaped token that DOES exist ('room Atrium') still resolves, because the graph decides, not the shape. Full suite 2561 pass.

Title: Only 7.4% of narrow-table streams are current, though 100% have history
Description: A necessary qualification to TODO-224's headline. That audit established that all 2,688 timeseries UUIDs resolve to rows in a database, which is true. It counted rows, not RECENT rows. Measured now: of 1,483 narrow-table streams, only 110 (7.4%) have a reading in the last 2 days. The tables themselves are live -- most carry rows timestamped within the minute -- but the publisher feeds only a handful of UUIDs per table: noise_data holds 236 streams and exactly ONE is current; co2_data holds 66 and none are. The fresh 110 are essentially the streams seeded by TODO-224 plus the wide-table top-up. For a system whose most common question is 'what is X right now', the live number matters more than the historical one, and only the historical one was reported.
Root_Cause: data-publisher tops up the wide sensor_data table (PUBLISH_WIDE=true, an intentional dev-mode behaviour recorded in CLAUDE.md) and a small subset of narrow-table UUIDs. Nothing was wrong; nothing was measuring it either.
Fix_Approach: Part (1) DONE (freshness travels with coverage on every surface). Part (2) DECIDED BY THE USER 2026-09-03: the publisher SHOULD feed every declared stream. Varying cadence per sensor is explicitly wanted rather than tolerated - 'i dont mind having different time intervals for different sensors, even if the synthetic data is increasing, we are showing live replies on latest data'. So every point with a ref:storedAt to a writable store gets fed, at a cadence chosen per modality rather than one global 30s tick, which is both more realistic and cheaper than writing 2,156 rows every 30 seconds. Implemented together with CAVEAT-405 (shaped signal) because both live in the publisher's value loop and shipping them separately would create two data regimes and cost two replays.
Verification: Part (1) done: freshness now travels with coverage on every surface that reports it -- the batch coverage badge (total_reporting), the per-datasource card and its verdict sentence, the onboarding readiness line, and the admin console's badge, cards and onboarding wizard. No new measurement was written: building_metrics._default_reporting_provider already computed per-UUID freshness correctly for narrow AND wide shapes and was rendered in exactly one place, so it was extracted as reporting_uuids_by_store() and reused; the metrics-block count is now a wrapper over it and unchanged. THREE properties are pinned by tests/test_coverage_reports_freshness.py (9 tests): freshness is per-UUID and never per-table (noise_data's table max is 'now' with 1 of 236 streams current, so a table-level check would restate the illusion); an unmeasured store is absent rather than zero (a broken connection must not read as a dead building) -- my own first version got this wrong and seeded an empty set before the probe; and freshness does NOT decide the verdict, because bldg1's wide sensor_data is a deliberate archived snapshot that answers historical questions correctly. Part (2) -- whether the publisher SHOULD feed every declared stream -- is a dev-data decision for the user and remains open. LIVE ON bldg1 after deploy, all three surfaces. Onboarding readiness: '64 datasource(s); 2796 of 2796 declared sensor(s) have rows, 683 reporting in the last 24 h' -- 100% coverage against 24% live, which is the sentence this caveat existed to get said. Coverage badge: total_declared 2796 / total_with_data 2796 / total_reporting 683 over 19 datasources. Per-datasource, the picture is starker than the caveat claimed and confirms it: database1 (the wide table carrying the intentional dev top-up) is 683 live of 685, and EVERY narrow table is 0 live -- occupancy_data 0/280, light_data 0/242, noise_data 0/236, contact_data 0/466 -- while all of them report full historical coverage. 3 of the 19 datasources return reporting=None rather than 0, so the unmeasured-is-not-zero distinction works on live data. One wording defect found in the same probe and fixed: at reporting=0 the verdict read '0 of them reported ... the rest answer historical questions only', which implies a live subset that does not exist; zero now gets its own sentence in both the API and the console. [2026-08-23 CORRECTION — A NUMBER I REPORTED WAS WRONG] The per-datasource freshness figures published above were an artefact of BUG-240, not measurements. MySQLNarrowAdapter stores its table as the PRIVATE `_table`, while the probe asked for `adapter.table` and got None, so every narrow store took the WIDE branch -- which queries the wide table and intersects its uuid-shaped COLUMN NAMES with the narrow store's uuid VALUES. Those sets are disjoint by construction, so the answer was always zero, and I reported 'every narrow table is 0 live' as the caveat being worse than claimed. RE-MEASURED with the adapter fixed: total_reporting is 1254 of 2796 (44.8%), not 683 (24.4%). The single biggest correction is database1_floors04 at 522 of 522 live, previously counted as nothing. The narrow zeros that remain are REAL and now independently confirmed -- co2_data's newest row is 2026-08-20 09:51, so zero inside a 24-hour window is correct -- but occupancy_data 4, energy_data 4, equipment_data 2 and iaq_data 2 were being hidden. The caveat's substance stands (coverage 100% against liveness 45%); its numbers did not. || PART (2) MEASURED 2026-09-03 AND ALREADY SATISFIED: 2,733 of 2,734 declared streams have a reading inside 30 minutes - 100.0% at store level across 17 stores, against the 7.4% this row was opened with. That figure predates BUG-390 (the publish map grew from 19 hand-listed points to every registered point), the 73,932-row contiguous-history backfill, and BUG-403. So the user's decision - feed every declared stream - required no new synthetic data: the streams are already fed. Verified at COLUMN level for the wide store rather than trusting its table timestamp, which marks all 684 of its points fresh from one row: 683 of 684 are real columns and all 683 received a value in the last 20 minutes, 0 silent. The single exception is NOTE-407. Varying cadence per sensor, which the user explicitly wanted, is handled with CAVEAT-405 in the publisher's value loop.

Title: 'None exist in the time-series database' is said about sensors that do exist
Description: Seen in the post-fix capture: 'Whats the biggest single-day water use we've ever logged?' answered 'Found 3 sensors in metadata, but none exist in the time-series database.' All four water sensors DO have rows -- Water_Flow_Sensor_Main has 27,454 spanning 2026-06-08 to now. The query window returned nothing (one stream stops at 2026-07-04, CAVEAT-233), and the empty result was reported as the sensors being absent from the database.
Root_Cause: TWO defects, one visible. (1) The validation is single-store: sql_agent took `primary_storage_uri` -- the FIRST non-null entry in the uuid->storedAt map -- and validated EVERY uuid against that one adapter's column list. bldg1's water sensors span water_data and waterflow_data, so whichever table lost the coin toss had its sensors declared absent. This affects any question whose sensors live in more than one store, which is the normal case for a building with narrow per-modality tables. (2) The message then reported that check as 'none exist in the time-series database' -- a claim about the estate's configuration, and false.
Fix_Approach: registry.get_valid_uuids accepts the whole uuid->storedAt map, groups by store and validates each group against its OWN discovery, unioning the results. sql_agent passes the map. Two deliberate details: in the per-store branch there is NO fallback to an arbitrary other discovery -- borrowing another store's column list is exactly the mistake being fixed -- and a store with no discovery passes its candidates through, because an unknown store is not an empty one. The message now says what was actually checked and that unloaded readings are the likely cause.
Verification: 8 tests in tests/test_multi_store_validation.py, including a regression witness that keeps the old single-store answer visible as WRONG, and a test that a uuid genuinely missing from its own store is still reported. The arbitrary-fallback flaw was caught by one of these tests against my own first version of the fix. Full suite 2572 pass.

Title: A cached answer carries no evidence record, voiding the T02 guarantee on every repeat
Description: Found while verifying the BUG-230 fix live, when a record that should have been present was reproducibly absent. Ask any question twice: the FIRST response carries an evidence record, the SECOND does not. On a cache hit the pipeline is skipped entirely; plan_trace is reconstructed by hand in that branch and evidence_record was simply left out. With a one-hour TTL that is a large share of real traffic, and it silently voids the guarantee V6-T02 exists to make -- an answer arrives with no statement of what it rests on. It also explains why T02's acceptance probe passed: the probe asks each question once, so it never took a cache hit.
Root_Cause: The cache stores question/response/intent/media and a metadata dict; the evidence record was never put in it, and the hit branch never restored one. The same branch DOES rebuild plan_trace, so the need was understood for the trace and missed for the record.
Fix_Approach: The record travels with the answer in the existing `metadata` field (no new field, so old cache entries deserialise unchanged) and is restored on a hit with a `served_from_cache` marker. Its `retrieved_at` is deliberately NOT refreshed: that field says when the EVIDENCE was gathered, and for a cached answer it genuinely was gathered then. Moving it to now would manufacture currency the answer does not have, which is the exact failure the freshness gate exists to catch.
Verification: Reproduced live before the fix: same question twice, record present then ABSENT. 6 tests in tests/test_cache_carries_evidence.py, including one asserting the restore does NOT rewrite retrieved_at. Full suite 2581 pass. Live re-verification after deploy. NOTE the downstream effect this had: BUG-230 scopes the plausibility guard by the record's operation and fails OPEN when there is none, so on cached turns that guard kept running over document numbers -- the behaviour BUG-230 had just removed. Two fixes were interacting through a gap neither of them owned.
Refs: orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py (cache put + hit branch); orchestrator/services/response_cache.py; V6-T02; BUG-230

Title: My own TODO-223 fix emptied the storage map by renaming a projection variable
Description: SELF-INFLICTED, found while verifying BUG-234. The TODO-223 fix added GROUP BY + SAMPLE to the class-listing template so a one-to-many join could not exhaust the LIMIT. SPARQL forbids `(SAMPLE(?x) AS ?x)`, so the projections were aliased and ?storage became ?store. The consumer in _orchestrator reads bindings BY NAME -- `if "storage" in var.lower()` -- and ?store does not contain "storage". From that moment EVERY class-listing query returned an empty storage map. sql_agent logged 'Storage: N/A' for every sensor and validated them all against a fallback adapter. ?uuid -> ?tsid survived only by luck, because the uuid test also accepts "id".
Root_Cause: A name-based contract between a query template and its reader, with nothing asserting it. Renaming a projection is a silent, total break of that contract, and the symptom appears two components downstream as sensors that seem to have no data.
Fix_Approach: Aliases now carry the substrings the reader matches on: ?storageRef, ?uuidValue, ?locationName, ?unitName. The coupling is fragile by nature, so tests/test_sparql_projection_contract.py asserts it directly -- that an alias containing 'storage' exists, that one containing 'uuid' or 'id' exists, that no alias collides with its own source variable (which is what forced the rename), and that TODO-223's GROUP BY and bounded limit survive any future rename.
Verification: The corrected query run live returns storage refs for all three water sensors and shows them spanning TWO stores (water_data and waterflow_data) -- confirming BUG-234's per-store validation was correct all along and was being handed an empty map. 5 contract tests. Full suite passing.
Refs: orchestrator/agents/sparql_agent.py (class-listing template); orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py (binding reader); tests/test_sparql_projection_contract.py; TODO-223; BUG-234

Title: Every evidence gate is implemented, tested and never called
Description: Found while wiring V6-T03. orchestrator/services/evidence/gates.py implements four gates -- freshness, completeness, spatial adequacy, calibration -- each with unit tests against fixtures. None of them is invoked anywhere in the pipeline. build_evidence_record takes gate_verdicts from results['gate_verdicts'] and NO LANE WRITES THAT KEY, so the argument is always empty. Three V6 turns (T13, T16, T17) are marked done on the strength of these modules, with acceptance criteria stated about the running system: 'a stale series never returns Observed; the age and the remedy appear in the answer', 'sub-floor windows refused with the gap named', 'a room with no in-room sensor never returns a bare room-level value'. None of those can be true. Compounding it, the freshness gate could not have said anything true even if called: its input, latest_evidence_at, was never written either (V6-T03).
Root_Cause: Two halves of a feature owned by different turns, with the wiring belonging to neither. T16 built the decision function and its fixtures; T02 built the chokepoint and accepted verdicts as a parameter; nothing was responsible for connecting them, and the parameter defaulting to an empty sequence meant the gap raised no error. Same shape as the field that is documented, read and never written: an interface that degrades silently when one side is missing cannot tell you that one side is missing.
Fix_Approach: Freshness wired at the chokepoint in ADVISORY mode, which changes no answer by construction. The other three are NOT wired and that is the deliberate part: each judges a field nothing populates (coverage always None, spatial grade always NONE, calibration always 'unknown'), so wiring them would return the same failure for every answer in the system -- the appearance of caution, the substance of noise. They are recorded in a new gates_not_evaluated field naming the input each awaits, so a missing gate can no longer look like a passing one. A gates_advisory field records verdicts that failed without acting, because otherwise shadow mode leaves no trace to review.
Verification: 9 tests in tests/test_freshness_gate_wired.py. The load-bearing one asserts that an advisory failure does NOT move the status -- a gate that starts downgrading the moment it is wired is not shadow mode, and the regression gate would report the resulting wall of changes as breakage. Also pinned: a stale reading's age appears in the verdict, a historical question is not stale for being historical, a documentary answer is not judged on freshness at all, the modality comes from the building's own modality config with no hardcoded modality name, and a gate that raises cannot break the record it describes. Full suite 2,614 pass, 0 fail. LIVE VERIFICATION OWED: it lands with the next deploy, which is held until the in-flight 0.55-floor capture finishes so the two changes are not measured together. LIVE VERIFIED 2026-08-22 after a clean force-recreate. 'What is the CO2 level in the lecture theatre right now?' now returns gates_advisory ['freshness: the newest co2 reading is 3702 minutes old, beyond the 5-minute limit for a current-status answer'] while the answer text still says 'right now' -- the gate is advisory, so nothing changed, which is exactly the shadow-mode contract. Cross-checked against the databases: narrow co2_data maxes at 2026-08-20 09:51 (2.6 days) and wide sensor_data at 23:03 (the dev top-up), so 3702 minutes is correct. A fresh modality raises nothing: the floor-5 noise question returns gates_advisory []. TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN FIX, both caught by live probes rather than by the tests, both now pinned. (1) latest_evidence_at took the MAXIMUM over the whole result set, so a two-day-old CO2 reading was recorded as forty seconds old because an unrelated wide-table row shared the result set -- one live sensor certifying a dead one, the same shape as BUG-234. Fixed by per-sensor attribution (narrow rows carry a uuid column; in the wide table the uuid IS the column name) and by judging freshness on the OLDEST contributor while latest_evidence_at keeps its documented meaning of the newest. (2) That fix was INERT in production and green in its own tests: it keyed on sensor uuids while the lanes tag provenance by store ('store:co2_data'), so nothing matched and the gate fell back to the maximum again. The gate now reads the row-derived map directly, and the production provenance shape is pinned by its own test. (3) Separately, the modality never resolved -- concepts arrive as CURIEs ('brick:CO2_Level_Sensor') while the modality config declares bare local names, so every modality used the DEFAULT 15-minute limit instead of its own; CO2's is 5. All three notations now pinned. Full suite 2,619 pass, 0 fail. Lessons 39-43. | CLOSED 2026-09-05. The remaining three gates were already wired; they returned nothing for TWO independent reasons. (a) No sensor declared an archival interval or a calibration date - 0 instances of each - now supplied by scripts/generate_sensor_metrology.py for 2,728 sensors (1,929 with calibration, 194 overdue). (b) BUG-428: spatial_facts declared PREFIX ontosage: <ontosage.org/schema#>, which matches 0 triples against the real namespace 37,207, so all five of its ontosage-namespaced queries had always returned empty. Either cause alone would have kept the gates blind, and fixing only the data would have looked like the data was wrong. LIVE: completeness now computes 0.087 for a 7-day CO2 window ("only 9% of the requested window was observed") and calibration_state reads "expired" for a real sensor.
Refs: orchestrator/services/evidence/gates.py; assemble.py; V6-T13/T16/T17 (status corrected to logic_done_not_wired); V6-T55; V6-T03

Title: The capture read the wrong evidence key, so every tightening was scored as a regression
Description: /chat returns TWO evidence fields with adjacent names and different meanings: 'evidence' is the older evidence DOSSIER (present on ~3% of answers, carries no gates) and 'evidence_record' is the V6-T02 EvidenceRecord that carries gates_applied and status. capture_golden_baseline.py read data.get('evidence'). Verified across both captures: gates and answer_status were empty on 309 of 309 and 306 of 306 OK rows -- every row of every capture ever taken. The regression gate's entire discriminator is 'a worsened answer is a TIGHTENING when a gate fired and a REGRESSION when none did', so with the column unconditionally empty the second branch was always taken and NO INTENDED TIGHTENING COULD EVER BE RECOGNISED. Surfaced by the 0.55 retrieval-floor run, which the gate FAILED with 8 blocking regressions; live probes show 5 are the floor doing its job and 3 are the on-topic guard doing its job. One of them, 'which anchor points are certified for the abseil window clean', was previously answered with the building's HVAC CO2 threshold table -- BUG-218's own motivating example -- and its correction was being reported as breakage.
Root_Cause: Two adjacent keys on one payload, and a reader that degrades to a plausible empty value instead of raising. Identical in shape to BUG-236 (a projection alias renamed out from under a name-matching reader) and to observed_at in V6-T03 (a field documented, read, and never written). Third instance of the same failure mode in two days: an interface where one side's absence produces a legal-looking value.
Fix_Approach: The capture reads evidence_record. evidence_sha is computed from that record with retrieved_at / latest_evidence_at / served_from_cache excluded, because hashing a field that is literally 'now' makes every sha differ by construction and say nothing -- the BUG-184 mistake. SECOND FIX, found by the same investigation: the on-topic grounding guard (BUG-103) suppresses document answers WITHOUT declaring a gate, which is why 3 of the 8 findings were unattributable even once the record was being read. It now declares 'grounding_guard' on the same evidence partial the retrieval floor uses, and only when it removed EVERYTHING -- a partial filter leaves an answer standing and is not a suppression.
Verification: 8 tests in tests/test_capture_reads_the_record.py, including a contract test that the API still writes the key the capture reads (the coupling is invisible from either file alone) and one asserting the dossier and the record are distinct objects, since that is exactly what was confused. Live classification of all 8 blocking findings: 5 return gates_applied=['retrieval_floor']; the other 3 scored ABOVE the 0.55 floor (Q911 at 0.5749) and were the on-topic guard, now named. Raw Qdrant scores confirm the floor is the cutter for the first group: 0.5125, 0.5139, 0.5364 against a 0.55 floor, with an on-topic control question at 0.6254 still clearing it. Full suite 2,627 pass. OWED: a re-capture with the fixed harness, so the gate verdict is computed rather than reconstructed question by question. VERIFIED 2026-08-23 on a clean re-capture (baseline_20260823_075206, 296 OK / 20 timeout, container unchanged throughout, no source edit inside the window). gates populated on 43 of 296 rows -- grounding_guard 22, retrieval_floor 21 -- where every previous capture recorded ZERO. The regression gate then returned **PASS, 0 regressions, 8 tightened** against the same 8 questions it had called blocking regressions the run before, attributed 5 to retrieval_floor and 3 to grounding_guard. That is the gate's discriminator working end to end for the first time in the project.
Refs: scripts/capture_golden_baseline.py; baseline_regression_gate.py; CAVEAT-226; BUG-103; BUG-218; TODO-222

Title: A capture column was declared and extracted but never written, so it read as empty everywhere
Description: Self-inflicted, while fixing BUG-238. I added gates_advisory to the capture's FIELDS list and to the _ask() return value, and forgot the dict the main loop passes to csv.DictWriter.writerow. DictWriter fills a missing key with '' and raises nothing, so a full 316-question run produced an empty column. The gate impact report read that as 'no gate recorded an advisory failure' -- the most reassuring output it can produce. A cache-flushed re-ask of 10 sensor questions showed 5 DO produce a freshness advisory ('the newest co2 reading is 27048 minutes old, beyond the 5-minute limit'), so the true figure was not zero.
Root_Cause: Third instance in three days of one shape: a field present on one side of an interface, absent on the other, degrading to a legal-looking value instead of an error. BUG-236 was a renamed projection alias; BUG-238 was the wrong payload key; this is an unwritten column. csv.DictWriter's restval is the same hazard as dict.get() with a default.
Fix_Approach: Write the field. More usefully, a test now asserts that EVERY name declared in FIELDS appears in the row dict, so the next added column cannot be silently dropped -- the specific bug is uninteresting, the class of it is not.
Verification: 9 tests in tests/test_capture_reads_the_record.py including the declared-vs-written guard. A cache-flushed 27-question capture now records advisory verdicts on 2 rows where the same run recorded 0 before the fix. NOTE the regression-gate verdict is UNAFFECTED: the `gates` column was written correctly, only `gates_advisory` was lost, so the PASS/8-tightened result stands. What is owed is a capture with the fix if the advisory half of the impact report is wanted at full-bank scale.

Title: Narrow adapters hid their table behind a private name, so every narrow store was probed as wide
Description: MySQLNarrowAdapter keeps its table in `self._table`. Two callers ask `getattr(adapter, 'table', None)` to decide whether a store is narrow (uuid, datetime, value) or wide (uuid-as-column): building_metrics._default_reporting_provider, which is the CAVEAT-233 freshness probe, and scripts/propose_archival_intervals.py. Both received None and took the wide branch, which intersects the WIDE table's uuid-shaped column names with the narrow store's uuid values -- disjoint sets, so the result was a confident zero for every narrow store. Found because the cadence script reported all 16 stores as 'wide shape' when 15 of them are demonstrably narrow. Also found in the same read: building_metrics hardcoded the table name `sensor_data`, a building literal in core code that contract rule 3 forbids and that the V6-T63 static literal scanner did not catch.
Root_Cause: An interface expressed as a duck-typed getattr against a name the implementation never made public. Nothing raised, because getattr with a default is indistinguishable from a legitimate 'this adapter has no single table' -- which is exactly what the wide adapter means by it. Fourth instance this week of an absent value that is legal rather than loud.
Fix_Approach: A public `table` property on MySQLNarrowAdapter, so the fix lands once at the adapter instead of at each caller and the next caller cannot trip on the private name. building_metrics' wide branch now resolves its table from schema DISCOVERY -- the table whose columns are uuid-shaped -- and reports UNKNOWN rather than zero when discovery yields nothing, because an undiscovered table and a silent building are different facts.
Verification: Live on bldg1 after deploy. Freshness went from 683 to 1254 of 2796 reporting, with database1_floors04 corrected from 0 to 522 of 522. The remaining narrow zeros were confirmed against MySQL directly (co2_data max 2026-08-20 09:51, so 0 in 24h is right), which is the check that distinguishes a fixed probe from a differently-broken one. The cadence script, which returned 'wide shape' for all 16 stores before, now measures 15 of them and proposes intervals for 2,031 streams. Suite passes.

Title: `uuids` is documented as a reserved bus key and nothing writes it
Description: CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/agent-patterns.md both list `uuids` as a reserved key 'set by the sparql node'. It is not: the SQL node keeps `uuids` as a LOCAL variable and puts `sensor_metadata` on the bus, keyed by uuid. Three readers believed the documentation. _sources_from added no per-sensor sources at all, so an answer's sources were only store-level provenance tags and every per-source field added this week -- observed_at (V6-T03) and spatial_adequacy (V6-T13) -- had nothing to attach to. _grade_spatial_adequacy returned at its first guard on every question, so a correctly wired spatial gate produced no verdict on a live probe.
Root_Cause: The same reserved-key list that already caused this once. It documented `sparql_results` and `sql_data`, names that appear nowhere in the pipeline, the evidence assembler was written from the list rather than the code, and the two most important data lanes could never be identified. The warning about that episode sits in agent-patterns.md directly above this entry, and `uuids` survived it -- a corrected document is not the same as a verified one.
Fix_Approach: One helper, evidence.assemble.contributing_uuids(results), reading sensor_metadata and still honouring `uuids` in case a lane ever writes it, so this does not become a second place to keep in step. Both documents corrected in the same change, because a reserved-key list that is wrong is worse than none -- someone codes from it again.
Verification: Live: a room question now returns 3 sources where it previously returned store tags only, with observed_at and spatial grades attached, and the spatial gate emits a real verdict ('a served zone links these spaces, but the link is not validated'). Suite 2,639 pass. OWED: the whole reserved-key list should be checked against the code that writes it, not spot-fixed twice.

Title: A report ID's digits were judged as a sensor reading
Description: Found by the V6-T23 live probe. Reporting a noisy radiator returned 'your maintenance request has been logged as REP-571188' followed by 'WARNING The recorded sound value (571188, 571188) is outside the range this quantity normally takes'. plausibility._NUMBER_RE's lookbehind rejects a preceding word character but NOT a hyphen, so the numeric tail of every PREFIX-123456 identifier is a candidate reading — and a report acknowledgement is largely made of one.
Root_Cause: Digits in text are assumed to be measurements unless something proves otherwise; the assumption should run the other way. Third of a family: BUG-191 counted the '2' inside 'bldg2' as a sensor reading and scored refusals as passes; BUG-230 read a document's threshold table as live values.
Fix_Approach: _IDENTIFIER_PREFIX_RE at _is_reading — the one place that already decides what a number IS, so the clock/date exclusions and this one cannot drift apart. Covers letter-hyphen, '#', 'no.' and 'ref'.
Verification: 7 tests in tests/test_identifier_digits.py, including a control asserting a genuinely impossible reading is STILL caught — the first draft of that file passed everything while testing nothing, because it used the measurand key 'noise' when the registered key is 'sound' and an unknown key returns [] for every input. That trap is now documented in the file. LIVE: the same report now returns a clean acknowledgement with no warning, and still binds space=...#Room5.16. Suite 2,697 pass.

Title: The freshness gate judged wayfinding answers, which have no measurand to be stale
Description: Found by the first real gate-impact report. 6 of 41 freshness advisories were on spatial_query and floor_plan answers: 'Where is the nearest water refill station', 'how do I get to the seminar room', 'which corridors are wide enough'. Those have operation=OBSERVATION but read no sensor, so the verdict came out as 'no  observation is available for this space' with an EMPTY modality — the double space was the tell. Geometry is observed and does not perish; a corridor's width is not stale.
Root_Cause: _is_current_status_question tested operation and time range but not whether a MEASURAND was resolved. spatial_result maps to OBSERVATION, so geometry answers qualified as current-status sensor claims.
Fix_Approach: Freshness declines to judge an answer with no resolved measurand. The modality resolver was already there for the per-modality age limit; it is now also the eligibility test.
Verification: A test asserts a spatial answer raises no freshness verdict; the existing fixtures were given an explicit concept, since they had been exercising a path the system no longer takes. Suite 2,730 pass. IMPACT: had this gate been enforced on the strength of the uncorrected report, wayfinding answers would have been refused for insufficient freshness — the report's own numbers were the thing that caught it, which is what the shadow-mode discipline is for.

Title: Work-order questions never reached the events lane; the capability probe answered first
Description: 'How many work orders are open?' returned the building's WORKING HOURS document. The routing contract sends all four probe phrasings to the events lane and was never consulted: the pre-LLM capability probe in dialogue_agent matched a document on the word 'open' and answered from prose. Third member of BUG-231's family, after wayfinding and deliberation questions.
Root_Cause: The probe's bypass list guards floor-plan, spatial, wayfinding and deliberation shapes but not event-store ones, so any booking/work-order/footfall question could be pre-empted by any document sharing a single word with it.
Fix_Approach: Bypass on the routing contract's own EVENTS_RE. Reused rather than re-written for the same reason WAYFIND_RE was: two definitions of 'is this an event question' is the drift this codebase keeps paying for.
Verification: LIVE: intent capability -> events, and the answer now comes from the events store. Two tests: one pins the bypass, one pins that the contract itself still routes these questions, so a regression in either is distinguishable. Suite 2,770 pass.

Title: The report-intake singleton got its database from one caller only, so other readers saw an empty store
Description: get_report_intake_service() is handed a PostgresManager only by the report-intake node. The events lane's joined ticket view called it and received a service with postgres=None, read zero reports, and printed no reconciliation -- on a building holding 154 of them. The join appeared to work and silently did nothing.
Root_Cause: A singleton whose dependency arrives from whichever caller happens to run first. A read that returns [] because of initialisation order is indistinguishable from a building with genuinely no reports.
Fix_Approach: The singleton acquires the manager lazily from the app module when no caller supplied one, so correctness no longer depends on call order.
Verification: LIVE: the work-order answer now carries '154 issue(s): 154 reported by people and 0 raised as work orders'. Pinned by a test on the factory.

Title: The orchestrator reports unhealthy for four minutes on every cold boot
Description: docker ps shows ontosage-orchestrator (unhealthy) while /health returns 200 with every service ok. The healthcheck's start_period is 60s but the app needs ~4m15s to become ready (DWG pipeline, GraphDB warm-up), so it logs a failing streak of 7 and flips to healthy afterwards. Not a fault, but a false signal on every boot trains people to ignore health flags -- which is the entire point of having them.
Root_Cause: start_period was set for a faster boot than this building produces; bldg1's six floors of DWG parsing dominate startup.
Fix_Approach: Raise start_period to cover real cold-boot time (~360s). NOT DONE in this session: it lives in the orchestrator Dockerfile and changing it forces an image rebuild mid-task, so it is logged rather than slipped in.
Verification: start_period raised 60s -> 360s in all three compose files. The app does not serve a request until FastAPI's lifespan completes, and lifespan runs the DWG pipeline and waits on GraphDB: measured ~4m15s, against a 60s start_period plus 5x30s of retries, so the container reported (unhealthy) for ~3.5 minutes of every boot while /health returned 200 with every service ok. NOT DONE: moving warm-up off the lifespan critical path so the app serves early and reports its own readiness. That is the better fix and a larger change; the false signal is gone either way.

Title: Plant/BMS point questions were answered from documents; the capability probe had no bypass for them
Description: With plant points connected and readable, 3 of 5 plant questions were answered from prose: 'is the supply fan running on floor 5?' returned a maintenance-log excerpt, 'what is the filter differential pressure on AHU_F5?' returned the building-statistics block, and 'what is the damper position of VAV_Floor5_West?' returned an HVAC manual page. FOURTH member of BUG-231's family after wayfinding, deliberation and event-store questions.
Root_Cause: The pre-LLM capability probe bypasses on SemanticRouter.is_data_query, which recognises a data question by sensor id, zone id, or a room/floor locator plus a measurement word. An equipment id (AHU_F5, VAV_Floor5_West) matches NONE of those patterns, so a plant question never looked like a data question.
Fix_Approach: A plant_point_query rule in the ONE routing contract, plus the matching bypass. Recognition needs BOTH a plant measurand and an equipment reference, except for measurands nothing in a room has (damper, filter dP, supply fan) which stand alone. The measurand vocabulary is DERIVED from the equipment-scoped modalities in saturation_modalities.yaml, so a building declaring a seventh plant modality is recognised with no code change.
Verification: LIVE: all five probe questions now classify sensor_data (were capability/discovery). 12 routing assertions cover both directions -- the costlier one being that room questions ('how warm is it in 5.16?') must NOT enter the plant lane, since answering a room from a duct sensor is a wrong answer that looks right.

Title: Confident denial of a connected sensor: 'there is no sensor that reports the supply fan status on Floor 5'
Description: After routing was fixed, 'is the supply fan running on floor 5?' reached the data lane and answered: 'There is no sensor in the provided ontology that reports the running status of the supply fan on Floor 5.' AHU_F5_Fan_Status existed, was typed brick:Fan_Status, carried ref:hasTimeseriesId and had 1,344 rows in a registered store. The model then helpfully suggested the user 'look for any points that include fan or status in their label' -- which is exactly what it had just been given and missed.
Root_Cause: The SPARQL agent's context comes from vector retrieval over the graph. _retrieve_context('is the supply fan running on floor 5') returned 6,385 characters containing NO fan point -- floor-5 room sensors outranked it. The same retriever returns the fan points correctly for the phrasing 'supply fan status air handling unit', so the index was current and the RANKING was the failure. A denial sourced from a similarity window reads exactly like a denial sourced from the graph.
Fix_Approach: Resolve the plant Brick class DETERMINISTICALLY from the modality config before keyword inference (_infer_plant_class), so instance discovery runs against the right class instead of hoping similarity ranks it. Design contract #2 already says SPARQL first and retrieval as fallback; for a class derivable from config there is no reason to let similarity decide. Longest-phrase-wins so 'supply air temperature' cannot lose to 'supply air flow'.
Verification: All five plant measurands resolve to the correct Brick class offline; room questions ('what is the air temperature in room 5.01', 'what is the co2 in 5.01') resolve to None and are untouched. Live re-probe recorded in the V6 tracker.

Title: bldg1 declares twelve AHU individuals for six physical air handlers, under three naming schemes
Description: brick:AHU has 14 instances: AHU_Floor0-5, AHU_F0-F5, and AHU-F5 / AHU-F3. Labels show them to be the same six units ('Air Handling Unit Floor 5', 'Air Handling Unit - Floor 5'). Both AHU_FN and AHU_FloorN participate in brick:feeds, so any answer naming the equipment serving a space can list two AHUs where the building has one. Separately, AHU-F5 and AHU-F3 feed NOTHING, and they are where the feed framework attached its existing AHU runtime points -- so those points are unreachable from any space by the equipment->zone->room path.
Root_Cause: Three generations of TTL authoring (original model, a later extension, and the feed framework's auto-registration) each minted their own identity for the same equipment, with no owl:sameAs or reconciliation between them.
Fix_Approach: REPORTED, NOT MERGED. scripts/provision_plant_points.py prints a duplicate-identity report and provisions onto every feeder rather than pattern-matching a 'real' one -- selecting by name would put a building literal into building-agnostic code, and merging on label similarity is the proximity-inference mistake that produced BUG-189. The generated series is seeded from the NORMALISED UNIT NAME, so two individuals describing one physical AHU produce identical series and the duplication surfaces as redundancy rather than as a fabricated disagreement between two readings of one duct. Resolving the identities is a TTL fix and needs the user's decision on which survives. [2026-08-27] MERGED, on the user's decision (a). The investigation found the real shape: AHU_Floor0-5 were NEVER DECLARED anywhere. Thirty points said brick:isPointOf against subjects in no TTL, and a reasoner typed the dangling references as equipment from the property's range -- that is where fourteen instances for six units came from. scripts/merge_duplicate_ahu_identities.py drops the 30 phantom points and their 30 configuration periods, re-points the AHU runtime sensor at AHU_F5 so it is reachable from floor 5, carries the AHU-F3/AHU-F5 comments onto the real individuals before deleting them (that text is information the building has), and leaves database rows and building.yaml's actuation allowlist untouched.
Verification: Six identities remain, one scheme, idempotent on re-run, all files reparse. THREE MORE instances of the same defect were found by generalising the check: seven phantom VAV_Floor5_* with fourteen points (declared from their own points' labels and location -- no feeds or isFedBy invented, because floor 5 has one AHU and that guess is exactly the proximity inference behind BUG-189); two pumps located at bldg:Building where this building is bldg:AbacwsBuilding; and bldg2's chilled-water meter naming an undeclared bldg:chiller. The phantom VAVs had also cascaded: 12 of 14 points carried NO location, because the provisioner takes a point's floor from its equipment. validate_dangling_references now runs at swap on every building. 12 tests; suite 3,322 pass.

Title: Uploading a TTL that also lives in input/ duplicates it into two named graphs on the next boot
Description: input/bldg1_plant_points.ttl was loaded through the admin upload API to avoid a four-minute restart. On the next restart ttl_uploader discovered the same file (it matches bldg1_*.ttl) and loaded it AGAIN into its own graph. Result: 592 triples in both 'abacws#bldg1_plant_points' and 'urn:ontosage:ttl:bldg1_plant_points.ttl', and every plant point returned twice through any blank-node join -- the reference fan-out shape that made CAVEAT-039 a live wrong-answer defect.
Root_Cause: Two independent load paths key their named graph differently, so neither can see that the other already holds the file. The SHA check in ttl_uploader compares against its OWN graph only.
Fix_Approach: Immediate: dropped the manually-created graph, keeping the uploader's (a fresh deployment gets that one automatically, so it is the reproducible copy). Durable fix NOT DONE: ttl_uploader should detect an existing graph holding the same content under a different name, or the admin upload should use the uploader's naming convention for files that live in input/. Logged rather than slipped in mid-task.
Verification: Durable fix landed, both halves. (1) The admin upload REFUSES a graph URI whose local name matches a file in input/, and names the graph to use instead -- a refusal that does not say what to do next just moves the problem. (2) audit_shadowed_graphs() runs inside run_idempotent_uploads on every boot and WARNS when one file is loaded into both its canonical graph and a hand-named one; it reports rather than drops, because unattended startup is the wrong place to decide which copy is real. 14 tests including the exact graph name from the incident, GraphDB being down, and one pinning that the audit is actually called.

Title: An unregistered storedAt key silently returns the DEFAULT adapter, querying the wrong table shape
Description: Plant points declared ref:storedAt bldg:plant_data. The key was absent from building.yaml's storage.databases filter, so no adapter was built for it, and AdapterRegistry.get() fell through to the default -- the WIDE mysql adapter, which reads a uuid as a COLUMN NAME. The failure surfaced six layers away as "Unknown column '2532e981-...' in 'field list'", and the user saw "no current value is provided" for a point holding 1,344 rows.
Root_Cause: A named key that resolves to a DIFFERENT store is a wiring error, but the fallback chain treats it identically to an unnamed legacy storedAt. Registration requires TWO files (building.yaml decides which adapters are BUILT, database_registry.yaml decides HOW) and nothing warned that only one had been done.
Fix_Approach: Registered plant_data in both files. Also: get() now logs a WARNING naming the missing key and the registered set when a NAMED key misses. It still falls back -- an unnamed storedAt genuinely wants the default -- but the wiring error is no longer silent.
Verification: LIVE: all four plant questions now return readings -- supply air 15.5 degC, fan 100% on, filter dP 152.6 Pa, damper 56% (avg 62.5%). Boot log confirms plant_data in the active adapter set.

Title: Every why-question the classifier labelled 'capability' skipped the diagnosis lane entirely
Description: "Why is room 5.01 stuffy?" never reached the V5-T20 diagnosis lane. Two independent interceptors took it first: the pre-LLM capability probe answered it from documents in 1.3s, and when it got past that, the concept-stage rule capability_measurand_is_data converted it to sensor_data -- which returns the CO2 mean and then GUESSES at the cause ("ventilation is insufficient"), while the AHU fan state and VAV damper position that would have answered it sat connected.
Root_Cause: Rules stop at the first claim. capability_measurand_is_data (concept stage) runs after why_diagnosis (parse stage) but claimed questions the parse stage never saw, because the capability probe short-circuited before classification. Neither interceptor knew about why-questions.
Fix_Approach: Two narrow guards: the capability probe bypasses is_why_question (fifth member of BUG-231's family), and capability_measurand_is_data declines to claim why-questions so why_diagnosis gets them. Deliberately narrow -- BUG-225's rule exists because the capability lane absorbed 88% of measurement questions, and only why-questions move.
Verification: LIVE: 'Why is room 5.01 stuffy?' and 'Why is 5.16 so warm?' both classify diagnosis (were capability). Tests assert both directions -- why-questions reach diagnosis, and ordinary measurand questions ('What is the CO2 in room 5.01?') still reach the data lane so BUG-225 does not reopen.

Title: The diagnosis lane could never resolve a room, and answered every room question at building scope
Description: resolve_referent stripped '.' from the QUESTION token ('5.01' -> '501') but not from the LABEL it compared against ('Room 5.01'). The match could never succeed for any label form, so every room-scoped why-question fell through to the building branch and was answered from a mean across 233 rooms -- with nothing in the answer indicating the room had not been found. A wrong-scope answer that reads exactly like a right one.
Root_Cause: Two normalisations of the same thing, written separately and never compared. Invisible because the fallback is a legal answer rather than an error -- and because almost nothing reached this lane (see the routing bug above), so it was never exercised.
Fix_Approach: One _squash() helper applied to BOTH sides, so they cannot drift apart again.
Verification: LIVE: now answers 'for Room 5.01 - Research Laboratory' and 'Room 5.16 - Seminar / Conference Room' (both previously 'the building'). Tests cover four label spellings plus a negative case that a question naming 5.01 does not match Room 5.02.

Title: The numeric guard suppressed honest 'no readings' answers because a room name looks like a number
Description: "I have no co2 readings for Room 5.01 over the last 24 hours" was replaced with "a number in the text could not be traced back to the underlying data". The guard compares every number in the prose against the payload's own fields, and the early-return no-data payload carried only success + formatted_response -- so '5.01', the ROOM NAME, was unbacked. The mechanism built to protect honesty destroyed an honest answer.
Root_Cause: An identifier is numerically indistinguishable from a measurement. Same shape as BUG-242, where report id REP-571188 was judged as a sensor reading. The success path already carried referent/window; only the early return did not.
Fix_Approach: The no-data payload now carries kind/modality/referent/window/window_label, matching the success path. The guard's own mechanism then backs the room name.
Verification: LIVE: both why-probes now return the honest sentence naming the room instead of the suppression text.

Title: CORRECTED: the co2 case was NOT a selection defect; the real blocker was the wide store being unreadable by the deliberative stack
Description: ORIGINAL CLAIM (WRONG): 'the capability schema picks a stale SATURATE sensor when the room also has a fresh real one', citing Room 5.01's co2. INVESTIGATION SHOWED the real CO2 sensor is DELIBERATELY excluded from the `co2` modality by label_excludes: ['installed-node'] and routed to a separate `co2_index` modality, because the hardware reports an index (50-80) and the provisioned sensor reports ppm. That split is CAVEAT-207, owner-confirmed 2026-08-20, and it is correct: mixing the scales made every room clamp to one utility and made two lanes disagree. So for co2 there was no fresh alternative to choose, and 'I have no co2 readings over the last 24 hours' was an HONEST and CORRECT answer about genuinely stale synthetic data.
Root_Cause: Two real defects sat behind the symptom, neither of them the one first logged. (1) MySQLAdapter -- the WIDE adapter -- had NO build_timeseries_query at all. fetch_series resolves it with getattr() and skips a missing one with a log line, so the whole deliberative stack (diagnosis, ranking, prediction) silently read ZERO rows for every sensor whose ref:storedAt points at a wide table -- on a retrofitted building, all of the physically-installed hardware. (2) The coverage audit's zone hop only modelled a zone CONTAINING rooms; a building nesting a per-room zone INSIDE the room had every real sensor invisible to the room matrix.
Fix_Approach: Both fixed, plus the freshness rule that was worth having anyway: when a room holds two same-modality sensors the auditor now prefers one that is actually reporting (None means 'not measured' and restores exact previous behaviour, never 'nothing is fresh'), and candidates are deduped by sensor IRI so the class fan-out stops inflating the count.
Verification: LIVE: 'Why is room 5.01 so warm?' now returns a real diagnosis -- mean 23.0 from the WIDE store, building median 23.0, 2 anomaly episodes -- with the leading explanation "AHU_F5's supply fan ran for only 39.6% of the window". Before, the same question returned 'I have no temperature readings'. Coverage: temperature fresh 180 -> 204 of 233 rooms; co2 present 66 -> 73. Room 5.01's co2 remains honestly 'no readings' -- the synthetic co2_data top-up stopped on 2026-08-20 (see the data-freshness row).

Title: A pressure reading was reported in psi for a point declared in Pascals
Description: "What is the filter differential pressure on AHU_F5?" answered "about 152.5 psi". The point is in Pascals. psi and Pa differ by a factor of 6,895, so this is not a formatting slip -- it is a wrong answer that reads as a confident one, and a plausible filter-dP number in psi would be a catastrophically clogged filter.
Root_Cause: The plant TTL declared units as brick:hasUnit with a BARE STRING ("Pa"). This building declares units with qudt:hasUnit and a QUDT IRI -- 875 triples against 101 -- so the unit was present, correct, and in a shape nothing downstream reads. With no unit in its context the model supplied one. THIRD convention invented by the same generator in one session (brick:isPartOf where the pipeline walks brick:hasLocation was the second): a triple that is present, correct and invisible.
Fix_Approach: The provisioner now emits qudt:hasUnit with the QUDT IRI (DEG_C, PA, L-PER-SEC, PERCENT, UNITLESS), matching the building's dominant convention.
Verification: LIVE: the fabricated 'psi' is gone -- the answer now says 'the exact unit isn't specified' rather than inventing one. Honest degradation, which is the outcome that matters: a wrong unit is a wrong answer, an unstated one is not.

Title: A reading's unit is in the graph but does not reach the answer
Description: With qudt:hasUnit <unit:PA> and brick:hasUnit "Pa" BOTH on the point, the filter differential pressure still answers '152 - 154 units (the exact unit isn't specified)'. The unit is declared twice, in two conventions, and neither reaches the narration.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. The entity template projects ?unit via OPTIONAL { ?sensor brick:hasUnit ?unit }, so either the point-specific path taken for plant questions uses a different projection, or the unit is dropped between sparql_result and the response prompt. Distinguishing those needs a trace this session did not run.
Fix_Approach: NOT DONE. Logged rather than guessed at. Lower severity than it looks because the failure is now HONEST -- the answer states the unit is unspecified instead of inventing one (see the bug above) -- so this costs completeness, not correctness. [2026-08-27] PARTIAL. Two upstream gaps found and fixed (see BUG-333): the QUDT convention was bound by no template at all, and the unit table covered 8 of the config's 35 modalities. But the metadata builder, probed with the exact reported shape, ALREADY returned 'Pa' before those fixes -- kind='pressure' hits the hardcoded table -- and the narration prompt already injects '(unit: Pa)' when the metadata carries it. So the reported symptom is NOT explained by what was fixed. Left OPEN rather than closed on a plausible-looking change. Next step needs the live stack: re-ask the question and read whether sensor_metadata is populated at all on that lane -- it is only built when analytics_required is true, and a lane that narrates sql_result directly may never see it. [2026-08-27] CAUSE FOUND, and it was not the metadata path. sql_agent._format_results built its summary prompt from the raw rows alone -- uuid, value, timestamp -- so the model was never shown the unit or the label. 'The exact unit isn't specified' was an HONEST answer to a prompt that had omitted it. The caller had sensor_metadata in state the whole time and simply never passed it. Now threaded through fetch_data_for_uuids into the prompt, with an explicit instruction for BOTH cases: state the unit, or say it is not recorded, never invent one -- an instruction covering only the present case leaves the model to choose for the absent one.
Verification: LIVE VERIFIED 2026-09-10 (V12-02). This row previously closed as FIXED_UNVERIFIED because the narration is an LLM call and only a live re-ask could prove it end to end; that re-ask has now happened and the earlier unverified note is superseded. Q 'What is the filter differential pressure on AHU_F5?' -> 'about 0.43 Pa ... ranged from 0.426 Pa to 0.445 Pa, with an average of roughly 0.434 Pa'. The unit reaches the answer. Offline: 7 tests including one that the ORCHESTRATOR passes the unit through, because a parameter accepted and never handed over is the same bug one layer in. TWO OBSERVATIONS that belong to other rows, not to this one: Sources lists 'Unknown Source', and 0.43 Pa is implausibly low for a filter differential pressure (typically tens to hundreds of Pa) without the plausibility band challenging it.

Title: The wide MySQL adapter had no build_timeseries_query, making every real sensor invisible to the deliberative stack
Description: MySQLAdapter -- the adapter for the WIDE store, where each sensor is a COLUMN -- was the only adapter in the codebase without a build_timeseries_query. fetch_series resolves the builder with getattr() and skips a missing one with a log line, so diagnosis, ranking and prediction read ZERO readings for every sensor stored there. It surfaced as 'I have no temperature readings for Room 5.16 over the last 24 hours' about a sensor holding 581,572 values current to that minute -- indistinguishable from an uninstrumented room.
Root_Cause: An optional-by-getattr interface. The narrow adapter implemented it, so the feature worked for every synthetic store and failed for the real one -- the half nobody demonstrates, because the synthetic data is what the tests use.
Fix_Approach: Implemented the wide equivalent: one SELECT per uuid UNIONed, which also gives per-uuid limiting for free (the property the narrow builder needed a window function for). Columns are validated against the schema cache, now warmed in connect() -- the builder is SYNC by the adapter contract and cannot await, and one unknown column aborts the whole UNION, taking every healthy sensor in the batch with it.
Verification: LIVE: the builder returns correct (timestamp, uuid, value) rows -- 19.12, 18.69, 27.64 degC -- and an unknown uuid is dropped from the batch rather than aborting it. Downstream, diagnosis now produces real answers for wide-store rooms.

Title: plant_state was written for one SPARQL executor shape and handed another; the mismatch became a false 'no equipment' claim
Description: Two SPARQL executor conventions are live: ontology_manager.run_sparql_select returns {'ok', 'rows'}, deliberation.live.sparql_exec returns raw SPARQL-JSON. plant_state was written against the first and unit-tested against it; the diagnosis lane passes the second. The call raised inside a broad `except`, and the caller received an empty context that rendered as 'No equipment is declared as serving this space, so plant state cannot be consulted' -- fluent, plausible and FALSE about a room served by an AHU and a VAV with seven connected points.
Root_Cause: MY OWN instance of the failure this session kept finding: an interface whose absent side degrades to a legal value. The broad except was written to protect the answer from a plant-lookup failure and instead converted a wiring error into a confident false statement. Every unit test passed throughout.
Fix_Approach: A rows_of() normaliser that reads BOTH shapes, and bounds moved into the query text so one call works for executors that do and do not accept a limit keyword. Six tests, including the one whose absence let this ship: for_space exercised against a raw SPARQL-JSON executor.
Verification: LIVE through /chat: 'Why is room 5.01 so warm?' now cites "AHU_F5's supply fan ran for only 39.6% of the window" as explanation 1, with plant_equipment ['AHU_F5', 'VAV_Floor5_West'], plant_points 7 and damper_mean 30.6 in the payload.

Title: The coverage audit modelled only one of the two zone-nesting directions
Description: discover_points joined a sensor to a room through `?zone brick:hasPart ?space` -- a zone CONTAINING rooms. The opposite and equally valid shape, a per-room zone nested INSIDE the room, was not covered. A building modelled that way had every physically-installed sensor attached to a zone and therefore invisible to the room matrix, leaving only sensors provisioned directly onto rooms as candidates.
Root_Cause: One of two legitimate Brick nesting idioms was implemented.
Fix_Approach: Added the inverse hop with both ends guarded against Floor, so a room's sensor never grants floor-wide coverage. Also deduped candidates by sensor IRI -- the class fan-out was reporting '2 candidates' for rooms holding one sensor, the same inflation that made 7 plant points read as 9.
Verification: co2 coverage 66 -> 73 of 233 rooms; multi-candidate counts fell from 233 to 47 as the fan-out was removed. Room-level check: 28 distinct sensors now visible in one room that previously exposed only its provisioned ones.

Title: Several synthetic narrow tables stopped being topped up; two are empty while still registered
Description: Measured across every narrow store: co2_data last written 2026-08-20 (4d), contact_data 2026-08-13 (10d), humidity_data / temperature_data / submeter_data / waterflow_data 2026-08-22 (2d). pm25_data and parking_data hold ZERO rows while being registered as datasources, so any question routed to them can only ever answer 'no data' -- design contract #8 has a triple in the graph and no rows behind it.
Root_Cause: The SATURATE generator was run once per modality rather than on a schedule; only the stores the live data-publisher writes stay current.
Fix_Approach: NOT DONE -- this is a data top-up decision for the user, not a code fix, and the affected modalities are explicitly labelled synthetic. scripts/refresh_narrow_table.py exists for it. Worth noting the honest behaviour meanwhile: the diagnosis lane now says 'I have no co2 readings over the last 24 hours', which is true.
Verification: Superseded by the 2026-08-26 measurement: all eight stale tables topped up and idempotent on re-run; parking_data holds 5,268 rows, not zero. pm25_data remains empty by design. See the newer row for the durable fix (generator vs manual script).

Title: Per-person energy attribution was ANSWERED with a fabricated figure
Description: "How much energy did I use this month?" was answered **22.06 kWh** -- the sum of all six floor meters, presented as one person's consumption. "Which employee uses the most electricity?" answered "Energy Meter Floor4 is currently consuming the most", silently substituting a METER for a PERSON. No meter in this building measures an individual, so both figures were fabrications with real numbers attached.
Root_Cause: The privacy inference classifier covered presence, tracking and private content but had no class for attributing a metered aggregate to an individual, so these questions fell straight through to the analytics lane -- which did what it always does and summed the meters it could find.
Fix_Approach: A fourth inference class, individual_attribution, guarded by a PER-CAPITA check that runs first: 'energy per capita' divides a total by a headcount, identifies nobody, and refusing it would deny a standard sustainability metric while protecting no one. The refusal explains what a meter CAN measure and names the questions that remain answerable, rather than only saying no.
Verification: LIVE: both questions now classify privacy_refusal and answer "Energy can't be attributed to an individual here...". 13 assertions cover both directions, including that per-capita and floor/building questions stay answerable.

Title: Metered-consumption questions were answered from documents; sixth member of BUG-231's family
Description: "How much energy did the building use last week?" returned "I don't have that specific information on record" while six floor meters held the data, and "How much electricity does the lab on floor 5 use?" returned the ROOM BOOKINGS document. Both were classified capability by the pre-LLM probe. An energy question answered from prose never reaches a lane that can state a figure -- so it can state no BOUNDARY either, which is what this whole turn is for.
Root_Cause: No consumption rule in the routing contract and no bypass in the capability probe. is_data_query needs a room/floor locator plus a measurement word, and "the building" is neither.
Fix_Approach: A consumption_query rule in the ONE contract plus the matching bypass. It defers to the existing inventory guard so "how many energy meters are there?" stays a census, and it declines any question the privacy classifier claims, so an attribution question is refused rather than routed to analytics.
Verification: LIVE: all three figure questions now reach analytics and carry a boundary line. The building total is now summed across all SIX floor meters -- an earlier run summed only five, which the boundary line makes visible where the bare number hid it.

Title: A factual caveat appended before persona formatting was paraphrased away by it
Description: The meter-boundary line was appended to the answer before the persona formatter ran. The formatter rewrites the prose, and the caveat simply vanished -- the code ran, the line was produced, and no error was raised anywhere.
Root_Cause: An LLM formatting pass sits between answer composition and delivery. Anything added before it is a SUGGESTION to the model, not a guarantee to the reader.
Fix_Approach: Append after formatting. General rule worth keeping: a caveat that an LLM may reword is a caveat that can disappear, so anything whose exact wording carries a guarantee belongs after the last generative step.
Verification: LIVE: the boundary line now appears on all three figure answers. Pinned by a test asserting the append happens textually after the persona-formatting call.

Title: A whole-site water meter is asserted isPartOf Floor0, conflating placement with metering scope
Description: brick:Building_Water_Meter -- a class that means 'meters the building's water' -- is asserted brick:isPartOf Floor0. Almost certainly correct as PLACEMENT (the hardware is on the ground floor) and wrong as BOUNDARY. Read as a boundary, the site's water total would be published as floor 0's consumption.
Root_Cause: brick:isPartOf / brick:hasLocation say where a meter SITS. Neither says what it measures, and nothing in the model distinguished the two.
Fix_Approach: Handled in code rather than by editing the building's data: the topology provisioner ranks the BRICK CLASS above placement, so a Building_*_Meter serves the building whatever floor it is bolted to, and placement-derived boundaries are written with ontosage:boundarySource 'placement' and NO allocation method. The answer then says 'inferred from where the meter sits, not a declared metering boundary'.
Verification: Re-checked with the reader audit before closing, because five capabilities in this codebase shipped correct and uninvoked. evidence/meter_boundary.py exists, ranks brick_class above placement, and IS called -- _orchestrator.py:4056 attaches the boundary line in the response node. 50 tests in tests/test_meter_boundary.py pass.

Title: The inventory guard reports 'how much electricity does the lab use?' as a countable-meta question
Description: _is_countable_meta returns True for "How much electricity does the lab on floor 5 use?" -- a quantity question, not a device census. Any rule that defers to that guard would drop the question.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed; the guard belongs to the inventory rule and owns that distinction.
Fix_Approach: WORKED AROUND, not changed: consumption_question settles 'how much <mass noun>' before consulting the guard, because a quantity of electricity can never be a count of devices. Narrowing the shared guard itself would risk the counting behaviour it owns, and one decision with two owners is the drift this codebase keeps paying for.
Verification: Rule moved from the workaround into the guard that owns it. _is_countable_meta now returns False for 'how much <metered resource>' when no countable device is named, so 'How much electricity does the lab on floor 5 use?' is no longer a device census -- while 'How much energy do the meters use?' still counts, because it names a device. consumption_question keeps its check but now AGREES with the guard instead of pre-empting it. 18 tests, and the counting behaviour is pinned first because that is what the narrowing could have broken.

Title: The regression gate counted a transport timeout as a dropped answer, so background flakiness read as a blocking regression
