Description: The gate compared a baseline with 15 timeouts against a run with 14 and reported TEN blocking 'dropped' findings plus ELEVEN 'added' ones -- two halves of the same noise, on a run that answered one question MORE than its baseline (302 OK vs 301). A verdict of FAIL on a run that got slightly better.
Root_Cause: Both sides were filtered to status == OK, and a question OK in the baseline but not in the current run was classed DROPPED, which blocks. A TIMEOUT is not a dropped answer -- the request never completed. With a ~5% background timeout rate on a live building and a local model, the gate would fail essentially every run, and a gate that always fails gets ignored. FIFTH measurement-apparatus defect in this project's history (see lessons #20-22).
Fix_Approach: Transport failures (TIMEOUT / HTTP 5xx / connection error) now quarantine the row on EITHER side rather than counting as dropped or added. The real signal is kept and reported: the per-run transport-failure rate is printed in the report, and blocks only when it materially worsens -- the stack degrading is a finding, just a different one from a behavioural regression.
Verification: Same two captures now yield PASS: 291 comparable, 0 blocking, 134 unchanged, 129 reworded, 26 route-changed, 2 loosened. The report states 'baseline 15/316, current 14/316' so the flakiness is visible rather than silently excluded.

Title: The evidence assembler built ConfigurationPeriod(subject=...) against a dataclass with no subject field
Description: assemble._configuration_periods constructs ConfigurationPeriod(subject=..., ...). The dataclass had no `subject` field, so the call raises TypeError -- caught by the function's own broad except and returned as an empty list.
Root_Cause: Undetectable while a second defect existed: nothing ever populated the `_config_periods` bus key, so the constructor was never reached. TWO DORMANT DEFECTS IN SERIES LOOK EXACTLY LIKE ONE WORKING FEATURE -- and fixing only the first would have looked like the fix had failed.
Fix_Approach: Added `subject` to ConfigurationPeriod. It is genuinely needed: several points' histories arrive in one query and are worthless once mixed together.
Verification: A test drives the real bus reader with a real entry and asserts it yields a period rather than [].

Title: The plant provisioner wrote 74 readable points with no isSimulated declaration
Description: V6-T26 provisioned 74 plant points carrying ref:hasTimeseriesId and no ontosage:isSimulated, while every other synthetic sensor in the same building declares it. An answer citing one could not say the reading was generated.
Root_Cause: The registry marked the STORE synthetic (nature: synthetic), which looks like the same guarantee and is not -- an answer cites the point, not the table. Written by the same session that was building the honesty machinery.
Fix_Approach: Declaration added and the TTL regenerated. A conformance test now scans GENERATED TTLs for readable points without the declaration, and separately fails CLOSED for any future provisioner whose SOURCE emits readings without declaring them -- before it has ever been run, which is when the omission is cheap.
Verification: tests/test_provenance_honesty.py, 5 tests. The rule caught its own author.

Title: The plant diagnosis presented a normal fan schedule as the explanation for a warm room
Description: "AHU_F5's supply fan ran for only 39.6% of the window -- the space was barely being ventilated" was the LEADING explanation for a warm room. 39.6% of 24 hours is roughly one working day: a normal schedule. Fluent, specific, numerically exact, and about nothing.
Root_Cause: The cause fired on RUNTIME (< 50% of the window), which any overnight downtime satisfies. A plausible-sounding diagnosis of nothing is worse than none, because it stops the search.
Fix_Approach: The signal is now COINCIDENCE: the share of the time the room was above its own window average during which the fan was off. Overnight downtime never triggers it because the room is not elevated then. Fan state is matched as a STEP function -- the sample in force at that moment -- since interpolating would invent half-running fans and nearest-in-either-direction would let a later start explain an earlier elevation.
Verification: A normal 08:00-18:00 schedule with a daytime-warm room scores 0% and raises nothing; an all-afternoon outage with the room hot scores 100%. 6 tests.

Title: A new lane computed its answer and nothing collected it
Description: The observability node ran, produced a correct answer, wrote it to observability_result -- and every question returned "I processed your request, but couldn't generate a response". The response node's dispatch did not know the key.
Root_Cause: Adding an intent is documented as two steps (YAML + node method), which is true for ROUTING but not for DELIVERY: a standalone lane must also be collected by the response node. The gap is invisible from the node's own tests.
Fix_Approach: Registered in the dispatch, with a test asserting the key is collected. Same wiring shape as every other gap this workstream has found: the half nobody demonstrates.
Verification: LIVE: all four reach questions now return their computed answer.

Title: The configuration-history provisioner did one full table scan per sensor on the wide store
Description: earliest_observations ran SELECT MIN(datetime) ... WHERE <uuid> IS NOT NULL once per uuid. On the wide store that is one full scan of a 661k-row table per COLUMN, ~700 of them; the dry run did not finish in ten minutes.
Root_Cause: A narrow-store idiom (one grouped query) applied to a wide-store shape.
Fix_Approach: One scan computing many conditional aggregates, batched 40 columns at a time so no single statement grows unreasonably long.
Verification: The same dry run now completes in seconds; 2,205 periods resolved.

Title: A shape name passed where a consequence CLASS belongs silently disabled the calibration gate
Description: requires_calibration / forbids_unknown_calibration / requires_authoritative_source all looked the name up in `consequence.classes` and returned False when it was absent. Passing `compliance` -- an INTENT name from the by_shape map, not a class -- returned 'not a calibration-sensitive claim', so the strictest gate in the system went quietly permissive on exactly the claims it exists for.
Root_Cause: Fail-open on an unknown name. That is the RIGHT default for a genuinely new class (a shape must not silently acquire a safety threshold nobody designed for it) and the wrong outcome for a caller mistake, and nothing distinguished the two. The consequence mechanism was already inert once for a naming mismatch of this kind -- see the by_shape comment in config/evidence_policy.yaml.
Fix_Approach: One _class_spec() resolver: a name that is not a class is resolved through by_shape before giving up, and a genuinely unknown name is LOGGED at WARNING rather than silently treated as informational. Production was never affected -- assemble resolves the shape first -- but a future caller can no longer disable a safety gate by typo.
Verification: requires_calibration('safety_or_compliance') and ('compliance') both True; ('informational') False; ('nonsense') False WITH a warning. 4 tests.

Title: The week-earlier comparison could never run: the fetch row cap stopped short of the prior week
Description: _series_for deliberately widens its window to reach back seven days, then fetched with the default per_uuid_limit of 500 rows. At a ten-minute cadence that covers about 83 hours, so the week-earlier window was never in the result and the 'same window a week earlier' line could not appear for any sensor sampling faster than roughly twenty minutes. The fetch SUCCEEDED; the rows were simply the wrong ones.
Root_Cause: A row cap and a time window sized independently. Confirmed: 288 rows exist in the prior-week window for the probe sensor, and none were returned.
Fix_Approach: The target fetch sizes its limit to the window it asked for. Raised only for the TARGET series -- the peer call asks for every space in the building, and widening that would multiply a 233-room fetch for a comparison that only needs the current window.
Verification: LIVE: the stuffy diagnosis now carries 'same window a week earlier: 1489.2' and a matched comparison over 140 sample pairs.

Title: A printed percentage was carried in the payload as a fraction, so the numeric guard suppressed the answer
Description: The matched comparison prints '(97% of the data survived matching)' while the payload carried kept_share = 0.97. The guard found '97' unbacked and suppressed the whole diagnosis.
Root_Cause: Every number the narration prints must be in the payload IN THE FORM IT IS PRINTED. A fraction and its percentage are different tokens to a text scanner.
Fix_Approach: kept_share_pct added alongside the fraction.
Verification: LIVE: the diagnosis renders with its matched-comparison paragraph intact.

Title: The top-up tool refreshed only the sensors sharing the table's newest timestamp, so one live sensor hid 235 dead ones
Description: refresh_narrow_table.py read the table's GLOBAL MAX(datetime) and then topped up only the uuids that wrote at that exact timestamp. One still-reporting sensor therefore made the whole table look current and hid every other one. Measured AFTER running the tool and believing it: noise_data 1 of 236 sensors fresh in 24h, light_data 1 of 242, temperature_data 1 of 67, occupancy_data 6 of 280.
Root_Cause: Per-table aggregation where the population is per-sensor -- CAVEAT-233's exact lesson, inside the tool written to clean up after CAVEAT-207. The tool's own docstring promises that each series continues from THAT SENSOR'S last value; the code did not.
Fix_Approach: One grouped query for each uuid's own last row, and a per-sensor top-up from that sensor's own last timestamp. A sensor already current is skipped, so history is still never rewritten.
Verification: noise_data now reports '235 of 236 sensor(s) are stale' and tops them all up. The visible consequence was three lanes away: 'find me a quiet room' answered 'I couldn't rank any spaces -- 51 spaces were excluded', because the deliberate lane correctly refused to rank on stale noise.

Title: My own lint gate printed GATE=0 regardless of what flake8 found
Description: The verification command was `flake8 ... | tail -3; echo "GATE=$?"`. `$?` there is TAIL's exit status, not flake8's, so it printed GATE=0 on the run where flake8 reported F821 undefined name 'datetime' in code just written. The undefined name would have raised inside a try/except and produced NO recheck line -- silent, and indistinguishable from an answer with no advice to give.
Root_Cause: A pipeline's exit status is its LAST command's. Formatting a status by hand invites exactly this. Sixth measurement-apparatus failure in this project and the first one in the shell rather than in the code.
Fix_Approach: Check the tool's own exit directly rather than a hand-formatted status after a pipe.
Verification: flake8 run unpiped now returns exit 0 with the import added.

Title: A PM10 sensor answered a PM2.5 question, because four quantities share one Brick parent class
Description: brick:Particulate_Matter_Sensor is the parent of PM1, PM2.5 and PM10, and on this building the TVOC sensors carry it too (a source-TTL defect: a volatile organic compound is not particulate matter). The pm25 modality claimed the parent class with no discriminator, so all four populations were pm25. Measured live: the sensor the coverage audit chose for room 5.01's pm25 was PM10_Level_Sensor_Atmospheric_5.01 -- a different pollutant with a different exposure limit, reported under the name of the one that was asked about.
Root_Cause: A population identified by Brick class alone where the class holds more than one quantity. Same shape as CAVEAT-207. The config already had label_excludes for exactly this; pm25 simply never declared any.
Fix_Approach: Declare label_excludes [pm10, pm1_, tvoc] on the pm25 modality. Config, not code, so the sibling classes stay queryable under their own names.
Verification: Live re-audit: the pm25 sensor for 5.01 is now PM2.5_Level_Sensor_Atmospheric_5.01; candidates per room 4 -> 2 -> 1. All 36 modality present-counts unchanged, so the fix narrowed pm25 and touched nothing else.

Title: A modality discriminator written in the IRI's vocabulary matched nothing at all
Description: The coverage audit built its match text as `label OR local name`, so for any sensor carrying an rdfs:label the IRI was never seen. Excluding PM1 as 'pm1_' (the IRI form, PM1_Level_Sensor_Atmospheric_5.01) therefore did nothing, because the matcher only ever saw 'PM1 Level Sensor installed-node 5.01'. The rule looked correct in config and was inert in fact.
Root_Cause: An either/or where both sides carry meaning. A rule that silently does nothing is worse than one that fails, because nothing ever goes looking for it.
Fix_Approach: Match on label AND local name concatenated, so either vocabulary works.
Verification: Before/after audit across all 36 modalities: only pm25 changed, exactly as intended.

Title: The absence guard reported 257 parking sensors where the building has exactly one
Description: count_sensors() counted by Brick class local name only, ignoring the label discriminator that is the other half of a modality's identity. brick:Occupancy_Count_Sensor covers entry counters AND parking bays, so a question about parking was answered 'this building does have 257 parking_free sensor(s)' -- inside a message whose first words are 'To be accurate about one thing'.
Root_Cause: Third instance this session of counting a superclass and calling it the population. The guard exists to correct a false absence claim and was itself asserting a false number while doing it.
Fix_Approach: Add modality_label_filters() beside modality_classes() on the same loader, and apply both to the count query (label matched together with the IRI, per BUG above).
Verification: Live: parking_free 257 -> 1, pm25 -> 35 (the genuine PM2.5 sensors), co2 72, noise 235. Modalities with no discriminator declared generate the identical query as before.

Title: The SPARQL pattern fallback scanned every triple in the store, so a question with an answer timed out
Description: _fallback_pattern_search ran `?sensor ?p ?o` with a string FILTER and two OPTIONAL joins. When the token MATCHED something, LIMIT 50 cut it short and it looked fine. When the token matched NOTHING there was nothing to cut it short and it read the whole store -- and matching nothing is the normal case here, because this fallback only runs after the class query returned zero, i.e. the LLM invented a class. Measured against a 19.4M-triple store: 29.98s per attempt, three self-correction attempts, 120s workflow budget exhausted. 'How many parking bays are free right now?' returned 'your request took too long' while the sensor that answers it was one 0.06s query away.
Root_Cause: An unbounded scan whose cost is invisible on the happy path and unbounded on the path it was actually written for.
Fix_Approach: Two bounded stages: probe `?sensor a brick:Point` + filter (no OPTIONALs), then attach location/uuid for the <=50 subjects found via a VALUES-bound second query. Measured: the OPTIONAL joins cost more than the scan they rode on.
Verification: Zero-match token 29.98s -> 0.61s (49x); matching tokens 0.19-0.52s. No workflow timeouts on re-probe.

Title: The referent gate invented the space 'many parking' and then refused to answer about it
Description: _SPACE_RE accepted ANY 3-20 character word before a space head, so quantifiers and deixis were swallowed into the name: 'how many parking bays are free?' produced the space 'many parking' and the answer 'I couldn't find many parking in this building's model'. A truthful sentence about a subject nobody had named -- which is the exact failure this gate exists to prevent, committed by the gate itself.
Root_Cause: An open modifier group with no notion of which words can carry a name.
Fix_Approach: Negative lookahead over a function-word list at the regex, so there is one source of truth. Real modifiers ('main corridor', 'ground floor') are untouched.
Verification: 'many parking' and 'there parking' no longer detected; 'main corridor' and 'helipad' still are. Full suite 3,064 pass.

Title: A metered quantity outside a hand-written phrase list was answered by the capability lane
Description: SemanticRouter.is_data_query recognised a data question by sensor id, room id or a fixed phrase list. It is also the FIRST condition of the capability short-circuit bypass, so a metered quantity phrased without any of those never reached the classifier. 'How many parking bays are free right now?' was answered from the building's CATERING amenities in 250ms.
Root_Cause: A routing predicate with no knowledge of what the building actually meters, while the modality set is explicitly 'CONFIG, NOT CODE'.
Fix_Approach: metered_quantity_question() in the routing contract, with the vocabulary derived from the building's own modality config. Requires the how many/much shape, so the noun alone never claims a question: 'where is the car park?' stays wayfinding.
Verification: 8/8 boundary cases; live routing now sensor_data. Adding a modality makes its questions routable with no code change.

Title: A parking question was answered with the building's catering amenities, in the right lane
Description: The capability lane filters resolver hits for topicality (BUG-103) but never ranked the survivors. Both 'Transport Parking' and a general 'Catering Amenities' blob survive on-topic legitimately -- the catering text mentions bicycle parking in passing -- and the resolver returns them in graph order, so catering led.
Root_Cause: Inclusion was governed; ORDER was not. The guard can remove an off-topic answer but cannot make the best one lead.
Fix_Approach: Rank survivors by label match first, then by match_strength distinctiveness. Rank, never drop -- the weaker fact is still true, it just must not lead.
Verification: Live: ['Catering Amenities','Transport Parking'] -> ['Transport Parking','Catering Amenities'].

Title: Regenerating hbco_mappings.ttl silently deleted two hand-authored concepts
Description: The file's header says it is generated from concept_terms_raw.csv and must not be edited by hand, but hbco:quiet_space and hbco:outdoor_wind had been written straight into the TTL. Running the generator to add a concept removed both (44 lines) with no warning.
Root_Cause: A generated artifact that had drifted from its generator. Anyone regenerating for any reason would have lost them, and the loss is invisible in the tool's output.
Fix_Approach: Back-port both concepts into the CSV so the generator is lossless again, then regenerate.
Verification: rdflib comparison before/after: 59 -> 60 concepts, LOST none, GAINED parking_availability; quiet_space and outdoor_wind keep all 11 and 10 lay terms and all Brick classes.

Title: Two gas sensors are typed as the wrong quantity in the source TTL
Description: TVOC_Level_Sensor_5.01 (and its 34 siblings) carry brick:Particulate_Matter_Sensor -- a volatile organic compound typed as particulate matter. NO2_Sensor_Parking carries brick:CO_Level_Sensor and brick:CO_Sensor -- nitrogen dioxide typed as carbon monoxide. Either lets a question about one gas be answered with a reading of another, against a different exposure limit.
Root_Cause: Mis-typing in the authored building TTL, not in any code path.
Fix_Approach: Retype in the source TTL. The pm25 exclusion list neutralises the TVOC case for the pm25 modality today, but the wrong type is still asserted in the graph and any other consumer will still believe it. [2026-08-27 CORRECTION] The TVOC half of this row was WRONG about whose fault it was. Brick 1.4 ITSELF declares brick:TVOC_Level_Sensor rdfs:subClassOf brick:Particulate_Matter_Sensor, so the building was restating what the vendored ontology already infers, not making an error. Post-rebuild the graph still reports 34 TVOC sensors as particulate, by inference, unavoidably. Removing the redundant explicit assertion is harmless but fixes nothing, and the pm25 label_excludes list remains load-bearing. The NO2-as-CO half WAS a real defect and is genuinely fixed: 0 remain. [2026-08-27 RESOLVED] Verified the claim against the ASSERTED axioms this time, not the inferred graph: Brick 1.4 declares brick:TVOC_Sensor rdfs:subClassOf brick:Particulate_Matter_Sensor at Brick_v1.4.ttl:31248. Brick is not simply wrong -- its own definition of that class is 'Detects pollutants in the ambient air', under which a VOC belongs; the NAME misleads. TWO fixes were considered and REJECTED: editing the vendored Brick file (makes 'we use Brick 1.4' false and hides the divergence) and owl:disjointWith against a superclass (makes TVOC_Sensor UNSATISFIABLE -- every TVOC sensor a contradiction, worse than the defect). Instead ontology/measurand_kinds.ttl declares what each confusable class measures in OntoSage's own terms, which contradicts nothing, and the class census DISCLOSES the roll-up: 'this count includes TVOC_Level_Sensor, TVOC_Sensor, which measure volatile organic compounds'. Terms are ours because QUDT stops at VolumeFraction and cannot tell CO from NO2 -- which is the other half of this row.
Verification: Measured harm first: 35 TVOC sensors inferred as particulate in bldg1, beside 34 PM1, 34 PM10 and 35 PM2.5. The roll-up map is DERIVED from Brick crossed with the declarations (scripts/derive_measurand_rollups.py, with --check so a stale file is a test failure), never hand-written. 22 tests, incl. one that fails if anyone 'fixes' this by editing the vendored Brick file. CONSOLIDATION: the validator's hardcoded family table now reads the same declarations, which exposed a latent bug in it -- it spelled 'PM2_5_Level_Sensor' with underscores where Brick uses 'PM2.5_Level_Sensor' with a dot, so that entry had never matched anything and the particulate family was half its intended size. The conflict rule also now EXCLUDES pairs Brick's own hierarchy relates: flagging TVOC+Particulate reported Brick-conformant data as broken, and a check that does that gets switched off. NO2+CO and CO2+CO still conflict. Suite 3,533 pass.
Refs: bldg1 TTL; related to TODO-181 (retype legacy instances)

Title: 19.2M explicit triples for a building with 10,969 IRI subjects; every timeseries reference exists 13.4 times
Description: The repository holds 19,227,946 explicit triples of which only 422,860 sit in named graphs. There are 4,015,138 distinct blank-node subjects against 10,969 IRI subjects, and ref:hasTimeseriesId appears 38,449 times for 2,871 distinct UUIDs -- 13.4 copies of each. This is CAVEAT-039's blank-node fan-out signature regrown after the earlier cleanup (blank nodes are minted fresh on each context-less re-POST, so the copies are all DISTINCT and no dedupe catches them).
Root_Cause: Historical, NOT active: counts were byte-identical across a full restart (19,433,543 / 38,449 before and after), so the ttl_uploader SHA-skip is holding and nothing is adding copies today.
Fix_Approach: A backup-then-clean pass as was done for CAVEAT-039. NOT performed: deleting triples from the user's live graph is destructive and needs explicit approval.
Verification: REBUILT LIVE. Before: 21,507,643 triples, 4,421,373 blank-node subjects, ref:hasTimeseriesId 78,654 times for 2,872 UUIDs (27.4 copies each). After: 288,824 triples (-98.7%), 29,011 blank subjects (-99.3%), 2,861 timeseries triples for 2,842 UUIDs -- 1.007 copies each. The fan-out is gone. The undeclared-type audit fell from 56 instances to 3.

Title: Parking is metered and honest but still cannot return the number
Description: Parking data was provisioned end-to-end this session: one building-scoped sensor (building_sat_parking_free), 5,090 rows in parking_data, latest reading current, values 3-60 bays. Routing, the referent gate, the sensor count and the capability ranking are all correct now, and the system no longer times out or fabricates. What it still cannot do is state the count: the parking_availability concept maps to brick:Occupancy_Count_Sensor, which holds 257 sensors of which one is parking, and brick:Parking_Occupancy_Sensor -- named in the modality config -- does not exist in the loaded Brick TBox, so the sensor cannot be uniquely typed instead.
Root_Cause: The same class-versus-population problem as the bugs above, in the concept -> Brick class path, where there is currently no way for a concept to carry the label discriminator that would narrow it.
Fix_Approach: Needs a design decision, not a patch: either give hbco:Concept a label discriminator alongside hbco:mapsToBrickClass, or let the SPARQL agent consult the modality label filters when a concept's class is shared. Deliberately left for review rather than hacked.
Verification: Fixed TTL-first per the user's decision: where Brick has no class, extend the OCBV schema. ontosage:Parking_Occupancy_Sensor declared as subClassOf brick:Occupancy_Count_Sensor, the SATURATE provisioner types the parking sensor with it, and the parking_availability concept maps to it FIRST. The CLASS is now the discriminator, so nothing downstream needs a label filter, and subclassing the Brick parent keeps every existing Occupancy_Count_Sensor query working. Verified in the graph: class declared, sensor typed, concept mapped, and the sensor UUID unchanged so the 5,268 parking rows still join. Found a latent blocker on the way: the concept generator did not declare the ontosage prefix, so the regenerated hbco_mappings.ttl would not have parsed at all. LIVE ANSWER NOT YET RE-VERIFIED -- the GPU was busy with the user's own job.

Title: The events store held only anomaly episodes, so every institutional question could only decline
Description: events on bldg1 contained 14,200 anomaly episodes and NOTHING else -- no bookings, no work orders, no access events -- although the generator for all three (synthetic_events.py) and the seeding script (backfill_events.py) both existed and had existed for weeks. Bookings, work-order and footfall questions were therefore unanswerable by construction, which is most of the institutional half of the supervisors' catalogue.
Root_Cause: A seeding step that was written but never run on this building. Nothing reported the omission: an empty event type is indistinguishable from a building that genuinely has no bookings, and the honest-decline path made the silence look like correct behaviour.
Fix_Approach: Run the existing seeder. No new code for the historical half -- the tooling was already correct, it simply had not been applied.
Verification: 6,038 bookings + 217 work orders + 1,842 access events seeded over 5 weeks. Live: 'how many work orders are currently open?' now answers '157 done, 32 assigned, 28 open (217 total)' with the ticket-universe reconciliation attached.

Title: The room calendar contained no future, so it could not answer what a calendar is for
Description: backfill_events.py generated from N weeks ago up to now and stopped, so the booking calendar ended today. 'Which rooms are free tomorrow afternoon?' had nothing to read and declined -- honestly, but uselessly, since forward availability is most of what anyone asks a booking system.
Root_Cause: The loop was modelled on the time-series backfill, where generating past 'now' would be fabrication. For bookings it is not: a reservation for next Tuesday is a fact about the present. The two cases were treated as one.
Fix_Approach: --forward-weeks (default 2) generating BOOKINGS ONLY ahead of now, via a new bookings_for_building_day(). Access events and work orders are excluded deliberately: nobody has walked through a door tomorrow, and a work order cannot already be finished on a date that has not arrived.
Verification: 2,301 future bookings; calendar reaches 2026-09-08. Live: 'which meeting rooms are free tomorrow afternoon?' -> '59 of 233 rooms have no booking tomorrow' with a walk-in caveat. Re-run adds nothing (uuid5 event ids, INSERT IGNORE).

Title: Every booking was marked 'done', so a reservation for next week claimed to have happened
Description: bookings_for_room_day hardcoded status='done'. Once future bookings existed, a reservation that has not started asserted completion -- and 'was this room actually used?' would answer yes about a meeting nobody has attended.
Root_Cause: A constant standing in for a value that depends on the clock. Harmless while every generated booking was historical, wrong the moment the calendar gained a future.
Fix_Approach: _booking_status(start, now): 'confirmed' before it starts, 'done' after. now=None keeps the historical behaviour byte-identical for existing callers.
Verification: 2,323 confirmed / 6,016 done; zero future bookings marked done, zero past bookings marked confirmed. 22 rows written by the pre-fix run were corrected in place -- INSERT IGNORE means a status change never reaches an existing row, which is worth knowing before trusting a re-run to repair data.

Title: 'Is room 5.01 booked?' was answered from a document dated June while 8,339 live bookings sat unread
Description: EVENTS_RE allowed exactly ONE token between 'is' and the availability word, so 'is 5.01 booked' matched but 'is room 5.01 booked' and 'is the seminar room reserved' did not. Both fell through to the capability lane and were answered from an uploaded room-bookings document whose own header reads 'Coverage: week commencing 2026-06-10' -- ten weeks stale -- while the live event store held the answer.
Root_Cause: A subject pattern narrower than the way people actually name rooms. The verbs 'reserved', 'occupied' and 'taken' were missing as well.
Fix_Approach: Subject widened to one-to-three tokens and the verb set extended. Three is deliberate: it covers 'the seminar room' without reaching across a prepositional phrase, so 'is the temperature in room 5.01 available' stays with the data lane.
Verification: 8/9 boundary cases as expected; the ninth ('is there a room free?') matches via an untouched alternative and is genuinely an availability question -- the test expectation was wrong, not the code. Live: now routes to events and answers '0 booking(s) for Room5.01 right now'.

Title: The numeric guard suppressed a correct booking answer because the lane under-reported its own evidence
Description: 'How many room bookings are there today?' returned the suppression text. The bookings_list branch NARRATES up to ten booking time ranges and attendee counts but returned only room/window/count, so the guard found thirteen figures in the text that nothing in the payload could account for.
Root_Cause: The guard was correct and the payload was thin -- an answer must carry evidence for every number it states. The sibling availability_check branch already did this properly via its `clashes` field; this one had simply never been brought into line. I nearly 'fixed' the guard instead by exempting clock minutes, which would have blinded it to invented times across every lane.
Fix_Approach: Return the rendered lines as `bookings`, matching availability_check. No guard change.
Verification: Live: '224 booking(s) for the building today' with the times listed -- and 224 matches a direct COUNT against MySQL.

Title: The provisioner exited 0 after refusing to provision an unimplemented family
Description: provision_synthetic_sources.py printed "unknown family 'timetable'" and continued to a zero exit, so a caller asking for a family with no generator saw success and a building that gained nothing. FAMILIES advertised 'closures' and 'timetable', neither of which has a generator, so the constant documented capability the script does not have.
Root_Cause: Reporting a problem is not handling it. Third instance this session of a tool whose failure path returns a success value.
Fix_Approach: Unknown families are collected up-front and refused with exit 2; FAMILIES aligned with GENERATORS and pinned by a test so the two cannot drift again.
Verification: Real exit code 2 on --families timetable; known families unaffected.

Title: Synthetic bookings occur at 3am because they follow the occupancy driver rather than opening hours
Description: bookings_for_room_day derives bookings from each room's occupancy series, which has activity around the clock, so today's list opens with 00:00-00:30 and 01:20-01:50. Plausible for a 24-hour research building, odd for most, and it makes 'how many bookings today' look strange to a reader even though the count is right.
Root_Cause: The generator has no notion of the building's opening hours, which the hours family already provisions as triples.
Fix_Approach: Constrain booking generation to the building's own declared opening hours. NOT a realism-flaw to keep: T61 wants data that is imperfect in the ways real data is imperfect, and 3am seminar bookings are not one of those ways.
Verification: Bookings now only start within BOOKABLE_FROM_HOUR..BOOKABLE_UNTIL_HOUR (7-21). Live: booking start hours are 7..20; the calendar no longer opens with 00:00-00:30 entries. Occupancy outside those hours is untouched - it simply stops being described as a reservation.

Title: V6-T25's institutional adapter had no caller, so a declared timetable could never be read
Description: InstitutionalFeedAdapter.read() was invoked by nothing outside its own unit tests. The polling loop cannot call it -- these are one-shot file reads with a read() interface, not pollers -- and no other entry point existed. A building could declare a timetable in feeds.yaml, have the CSV on disk, and still answer 'no data'.
Root_Cause: A component delivered with unit tests but never wired to a caller. Its own docstring claims it is 'deliberately shaped like the other feed adapters so the registry dispatches it identically' -- a claim the code does not honour, since it is not a FeedAdapter subclass and has no poll().
Fix_Approach: Ingest institutional sources from the events seeder, which already owns the events-store write path. Declared sources are read by default; --skip-institutional opts out.
Verification: 675 timetable records parsed and stored; re-run adds nothing. Live: 'what is scheduled in Room1.06 tomorrow?' answers '1 booking, 14:00-16:00'.

Title: One non-conforming feed killed the polling loop and silently stopped every other feed
Description: run_forever called adapter.poll_safe() unguarded. poll_safe guards a poll that RAISES, but not an adapter that does not implement the polling contract at all -- and the registry maps InstitutionalFeedAdapter, which has no poll_safe. So declaring a timetable raised AttributeError out of run_forever, the task died, and the building's weather feeds stopped with it. Nothing surfaced this beyond one line in the container log.
Root_Cause: A blast radius of 'all feeds' for one misdeclared source, in the loop whose whole job is to be the resilient part. The guard protected against the failure that was anticipated and not against the one that happened.
Fix_Approach: Check the contract before calling, skip non-polling sources with a once-only log, and wrap each adapter's cycle so a failure cannot escape the loop. poll_once hardened identically.
Verification: Live: '[feeds] synthetic_timetable (timetable) is not a polling source - skipped by the polling loop' and the loop keeps running for the other 3 feeds.

Title: Institutional event ids overflowed CHAR(36) and MySQL silently truncated 234 records away
Description: InstitutionalRecord.as_event built a readable id -- 'synthetic_timetable:Room1.06:20260727T0900', 42 characters -- while events.event_id is CHAR(36) and every other producer mints a uuid5. MySQL truncated to 'synthetic_timetable:Room1.06:2026073', discarding the day digit and the entire time, so every session in one room within the same ten-day window collapsed onto one primary key and INSERT IGNORE dropped the rest. 675 parsed records became 441 stored ones and no error was raised anywhere.
Root_Cause: A second id scheme alongside the framework's uuid5 one, in a column whose width was set by the first. Non-strict MySQL turns the overflow into silent truncation, and INSERT IGNORE turns the resulting key collision into silent data loss.
Fix_Approach: uuid5 over (building, type, source, space, start) -- keeps idempotent re-ingest and fits the column the rest of the framework respects.
Verification: 675 parsed -> 675 stored, ids exactly 36 chars, re-run still a no-op. Two sessions in one room now hold distinct ids (pinned by test).

Title: Timetable questions were answered from a stale document while 675 live records sat unread
Description: EVENTS_RE had no schedule vocabulary, so 'what is scheduled in Room1.06 tomorrow?' and 'which rooms have teaching sessions this week?' reached the capability lane and were answered from an uploaded bookings document showing JUNE dates.
Root_Cause: Timetable records deliberately land in the same store as bookings (T25), but the routing vocabulary was never extended to match.
Fix_Approach: Added timetable/lecture/teaching-session vocabulary, qualified so scheduled MAINTENANCE still reaches the compliance register and 'lecture theatre' -- a space name -- still reaches the route finder.
Verification: 8/8 boundary cases; full suite green including the wayfinding pin.

Title: 'Is the room free on Friday morning?' was answered about today
Description: parse_window knew today/tomorrow/yesterday/this week but no NAMED WEEKDAY and no bare part-of-day, so 'Friday morning' matched nothing and fell through to the default. The answer was about today -- visibly, since the window label is printed, but still an answer to a different question than the one asked.
Root_Cause: A window vocabulary narrower than the way people name times.
Fix_Approach: Resolve a named day and a part of day TOGETHER, because they are asked together. Named days resolve forward. The questioner's phrasing is kept in the label: 'this afternoon', never 'today afternoon'.
Verification: Live: 'Is Room1.06 free on Friday morning?' -> 'booked Friday morning: 07:00-07:30, 08:20-18:00'. Existing windows unchanged (pinned).

Title: A room typed Common_Space without brick:Room is invisible to the coverage audit
Description: Room1.04 carries brick:Common_Space but NOT brick:Room, while every other room carries Room. The coverage auditor selects brick:Room, so this space has no modality coverage, is never a ranking candidate and can never be recommended -- despite having capacity and occupancy metadata in the graph. It surfaced because the timetable ingest correctly REFUSED to bind rows naming it, reporting them rather than guessing.
Root_Cause: Inconsistent typing in the authored building TTL.
Fix_Approach: Add brick:Room to the instance. Same family as CAVEAT-286 and TODO-181.
Verification: Fixed additively: bldg:Room1.04 a brick:Room asserted in bldg1_enhancements.ttl. The Common_Space typing was not wrong, only incomplete, so asserting the missing parent is smaller and safer than deleting anything. Parses; the coverage audit selects brick:Room and will now see the room.

Title: 'Which rooms have teaching sessions?' returns a flat booking list instead of rooms
Description: The question names ROOMS as the unit of the answer; bookings_list replies with '1000 booking(s) for the building this week' followed by ten times. The count is right and the shape is wrong -- the reader has to aggregate by hand.
Root_Cause: One rendering for two question shapes: 'how many bookings' wants a count, 'which rooms' wants a grouped list.
Fix_Approach: Group by room when the question asks which rooms, as availability_list already does for the free-room case.
Verification: Group-by-room branch in event_query_service.bookings_list, reusing the reverse uuid->room lookup the availability list already builds; the list states what it truncated. tests/test_institutional_events.py.

Title: Asset and schedule triples had been written for weeks and no code ever queried them
Description: The provisioner writes ontosage:AssetStatus and ontosage:ServiceSchedule -- 21 status records and 8 schedules on this building, each with a value, an observation time and an assistance contact -- and grep found ZERO references to AssetStatus, statusValue, statusOf, ServiceSchedule or scheduleKind anywhere in orchestrator/. Measured live: 'are the lifts working?' answered 'this building does not have lift sensors' while the lift's status sat in the graph; the same for AV, network and cleaning schedules.
Root_Cause: The described-but-unconnected failure in a third form. Not a sensor with no data (contract 8's usual case), and not a file nothing ingests (BUG-296), but DATA NOTHING QUERIES. Provisioning was treated as the deliverable; an answering path was never built.
Fix_Approach: A dedicated asset_state lane: services/asset_state_service.py, an intent, a node and -- the step this project's own checklist warns is the one that gets missed -- collection in _response_node. Answers carry the observation time, degrade to 'last KNOWN state' past a staleness threshold, name the assistance contact for an outage, and declare simulated provenance.
Verification: Live: lifts 'All 1 lift(s) are operational (last checked 5 days ago)' with the staleness caveat and 'Source: simulated service feed'; network 8 services; AV 12 units; 8 service schedules listed. 29 tests.

Title: 'Are there any planned closures coming up?' FILED A MAINTENANCE TICKET instead of answering
Description: The question was classified maintenance and the intake path created REP-E1A800 -- a real ticket, from a plainly interrogative question, while three planned closures with dates and reasons sat in the graph. Filing a ticket is a side-effecting action, so this is worse than a wrong answer: it put work into somebody's queue.
Root_Cause: BUG-166's shape in a second place. That fix flips interrogative maintenance to the events lane; closures belong to neither events nor intake, so nothing claimed them.
Fix_Approach: asset_state_query rule with the same interrogative guard: questions route to the lane, statements ('the lift is broken') still reach intake.
Verification: Live: now answers '3 planned closure(s) on record' with dates and reasons, and files nothing. 'The lift is broken.' still files a ticket (pinned by test).

Title: 'Which rooms are step-free accessible?' was answered with a list of unbooked rooms
Description: The availability patterns matched the 'free' inside 'step-FREE', so an accessibility question reached the events lane and was answered '69 of 233 rooms have no booking today'. Accessibility is the highest-consequence family in this corpus; answering it with booking availability is a wrong answer to somebody who may not be able to use the room at all.
Root_Cause: A word-boundary match on a term that also appears as the tail of a hyphenated compound with an unrelated meaning.
Fix_Approach: (?<!-) before 'free' in every availability pattern, in both the routing contract and the event lane's own classifier. Nobody asks whether a room is 'X-free' meaning unoccupied, so excluding all hyphen-prefixed forms is safe.
Verification: 6/6 boundary cases; live the question now reaches the capability lane and answers with the building's accessibility provision.

Title: The capability short-circuit skips the parse stage, so a new routing rule could never fire
Description: The asset_state rule was correct in isolation -- six of six cases routed -- and did nothing live. The capability probe claims a question BEFORE the LLM ('[ttl-route] capability via document KB -- skipping LLM intent call'), and that path never runs the parse stage, so no parse-stage rule can reach any question the probe claims, however it is ordered.
Root_Cause: Eighth member of BUG-231's family. The bypass list is the only way onto that path, and each new lane has to be added to it explicitly -- a rule in the contract is NOT sufficient, which is not obvious from the contract's own documentation.
Fix_Approach: Add is_asset_state_question to the short-circuit bypass, reusing the lane's own definition rather than writing a second one there.
Verification: Live: all four state questions now reach asset_state. Pinned by a test asserting the bypass call is present.

Title: Asset statuses are a one-time snapshot, so outages never appear or clear
Description: gen_status writes one status per asset at provisioning time and nothing updates it, so every answer is five days stale and the staleness caveat fires on every one. V6-T58 asks for outages that 'appear and clear' -- a lift that is broken on Tuesday and fixed on Thursday -- which is what makes the freshness and consequence gates testable in both directions.
Root_Cause: Status provisioned as a static fact rather than as a time series of episodes.
Fix_Approach: Generate status EPISODES with start/end like work orders, and refresh the current status on a tick the way the narrow tables are topped up.
Verification: Outage EPISODES modelled like work orders: an episode opens and whether it has cleared depends on where now sits relative to a deterministic duration, with a ~12% tail that never clears. Seeded on bldg1: 21 assets discovered by class, 28 episodes, 22 cleared and 6 OPEN. Episodes outrank the graph's status triple, so the answer reflects what is broken now rather than what was true at provisioning time.

Title: A cleaning question about one floor lists every floor's schedule
Description: 'When was the last cleaning of floor 2?' returns all 8 service schedules rather than floor 2's. The named referent is ignored, so the reader filters by hand.
Root_Cause: The schedule branch does not resolve the space named in the question.
Fix_Approach: Resolve the referent and filter, declining honestly when the named space has no schedule rather than showing the others.
Verification: _named_location scopes _answer_schedule to the longest known place name in the question; an unmatched question keeps the building-wide list. tests/test_asset_state_lane.py, 42 tests.

Title: Desk and workspace allocation is not provisioned, so desk questions answer zero
Description: 'How many desks are available in the building?' answers '0 desks available'. There is no desk/workspace entity in the model at all, so the honest answer would be 'this building does not model desks' rather than a count of zero, which reads as 'all desks are taken'.
Root_Cause: The T57 pack lists desk allocation and it was never provisioned.
Fix_Approach: Provision desks as located entities with an allocation state, and make the zero-count path distinguish 'none modelled' from 'none free'. [2026-08-27] FIXED on the owner's decision (a) -- honesty only, no invented furniture. unmodelled_entities.py carries NO word list: the rule is that a zero over a class the ontology DEFINES is a real 'none', while a zero over a class it does not define at all is invented. Only the second is rewritten, and only after the graph confirms no such class exists under any vocabulary (local-name match, singular and plural both tried). Fails open on every uncertainty -- no zero-claim, an unverifiable lookup, or a class that IS modelled all leave the answer untouched, because a guard that edits answers on a failed query is worse than the defect. Runs beside the absence guard in the response node.
Verification: 18 tests in tests/test_unmodelled_entities.py; full suite 3,377 pass.

Title: The numeric guard suppressed an asset answer over an age computed only for the prose
Description: 'Is the AV equipment working?' returned the suppression text over unbacked numbers ['15','15']. _human_age renders hours into days for display -- '15 days ago' -- and 15 appeared nowhere in the payload, which carried oldest_observation_hours=370 instead.
Root_Cause: Second instance in two days of a lane narrating a figure its payload does not carry (BUG-293 was the first). The guard was right both times.
Fix_Approach: Carry the rendered phrase as last_observation_phrase and narrate from it, so the text and the evidence state the same number.
Verification: Live: all three asset questions answer. Pinned by a test that runs the real guard over the payload and asserts zero unbacked numbers.

Title: A live outage was reported with a caveat saying it was not a live state
Description: With episodes wired, the lift answer read 'out of service since 47 hours ago' and then '*This is the last KNOWN state, not a live one*' -- two contradictory statements about the same fact in one answer. The wording was also wrong before that: 'last checked 47 hours ago' for an OPEN episode reads as though nobody has looked since, when the number is how long it has been broken.
Root_Cause: The staleness caveat keys on observation age alone. Age means 'time since someone looked' for a static status and 'time since it broke' for an open episode, and the caveat could not tell the two apart.
Fix_Approach: An open episode is current knowledge: it says 'out of service since' and the staleness caveat is suppressed. A static status keeps both.
Verification: Live: 'out of service since 47 hours ago' with no contradicting caveat.

Title: A step-free route was returned as accessible even when the lift it depends on was out of service
Description: Step-free routing drops staircases, so an accessible route changes floors ONLY by lift. The route finder had no notion of a lift being unavailable, so with a lift out of service it would still return the route and label it step-free -- sending someone who cannot use stairs to a floor they cannot reach. The ingredients were all present once outage episodes existed (BUG/CAVEAT-307): a genuinely broken lift, and a router that assumed every lift works.
Root_Cause: Availability was modelled for ASSETS and geometry for ROUTES, and the two never met. A broken lift is not a slower way up; it is not a way up, so a cost penalty would have been wrong too -- it has to be excluded from the search.
Fix_Approach: RouteFinder.route/nearest take `unavailable` vertical nodes and exclude them under step_free. The lane looks up open lift outages ONLY for a step-free question, and when that removes the route it names the outage rather than reporting 'no step-free route', which reads as a permanent property of the building rather than something being fixed.
Verification: 8 tests on a two-floor fixture: the route exists with the lift working, is GONE when it is out, the stairs route still exists (so the honest answer is 'not step-free right now', not 'unreachable'), same-floor routes are unaffected, and an availability lookup that raises leaves routing exactly as it was.

Title: bldg1's floor plans type no vertical circulation, so multi-floor routing does not work at all
Description: Measured on the live route graph: 344 nodes across 6 floors, twelve space types (zone, office, lab, meeting_room, storage, toilet, server_room, lecture, utility, reception, kitchen, classroom) and ZERO typed 'lift' or 'staircase'. No node label mentions a lift either. Cross-floor edges therefore number 4 in the whole building, and a route from floor 0 to floor 3 returns NONE -- with or without the step-free requirement. The graph knows better: it holds one ontosage:Lift (Lift_Main, 'Main passenger lift') and two brick:Staircase entities.
Root_Cause: The route finder joins floors by aligning vertical CORES from the floor-plan manifests, and the DWG/PDF pipeline types spaces from their drawn names. This building's drawings do not name its lifts or stairs, so the pipeline has nothing to type and the cross-floor logic is inert.
Fix_Approach: Link the graph's vertical-circulation entities to their per-floor footprints, or have the pipeline recognise them. NOT fixable by synthesising the shafts: floor-plan geometry is measured from real DWG, and inventing a lift position would be fabricating spatial data -- worse than declining. [2026-08-27] FIXED on the owner's decision (a). vertical_circulation.py reads the declared lifts and staircases out of the ontology -- bldg1 held one ontosage:Lift and two brick:Staircase all along -- and RouteFinder attaches one node per served floor. The POSITION is not invented: a drawing that omits the shaft gives no coordinate to be near, so the node hangs off that floor's best-connected space (a graph-theoretic stand-in for a lift lobby, from the building's own adjacency, deterministic by degree then zone_id) and every route through one carries approximate_vertical plus a sentence saying so. A kind the manifests ALREADY type is skipped entirely, so a well-surveyed building keeps its real geometry. A core naming no floors is assumed to serve all of them and the assumption is recorded rather than presented as declared; an unparseable floor reference yields nothing rather than a plausible storey. Step-free still means step-free: a declared staircase does not create an accessible route.
Verification: 16 tests in tests/test_vertical_circulation.py (incl. the live defect: floor 0 to floor 3 returns None without the declared lift and routes with it); full suite 3,377 pass.

Title: The rag-service ontology importer appended every TTL to the default graph on every restart
Description: rag-service/graphdbRAG/main.py ran import_ontology() unconditionally at startup. That function scans the SAME /app/input/*.ttl the orchestrator's ttl_uploader already ingests, and POSTs each file to /statements with the X-GraphDB-Context header COMMENTED OUT. POST appends, so every restart of the service added another full copy of every ontology file -- Brick_v1.4 and Brick+extensions included -- into the DEFAULT graph, each time with fresh blank nodes that nothing can dedupe.
Root_Cause: A redundant second ingestion path with its context disabled. This is the origin of CAVEAT-287 and of BUG-250's duplicate named graphs: two importers over one directory, one of them append-only and unscoped.
Fix_Approach: Gate the importer behind RAG_IMPORT_ONTOLOGY, defaulting OFF -- the orchestrator owns ingestion and this service only reads. Also un-comment the context so a re-import REPLACES rather than appends if anyone turns it back on.
Verification: Measured before the fix: 20,322,443 triples for a building with 10,969 IRI subjects; 15,413,738 SHACL, 4,189,265 blank-node subjects, and 55,706 timeseries references for 2,872 UUIDs -- 19.4 copies each, up from 13.4 the previous day purely from development restarts. Named graphs held 422,892 of the 20.3M. 4 tests pin that the importer is off by default and names a context if re-enabled.

Title: Eight narrow tables were 30-38 hours stale because only a manual script tops them up
Description: Measured across every narrow store: co2, contact, humidity, parking, plant, submeter, temperature and waterflow were all 29-38 hours old, while energy, equipment, iaq, light, noise, occupancy, water and the wide sensor_data were current to the minute. The split is exactly the maintenance boundary: everything data-publisher generates stays fresh, everything that depends on someone running refresh_narrow_table.py by hand goes stale.
Root_Cause: Half the synthetic estate has a running generator and half has a manual script. Nothing reports the difference, and the honest-decline path makes a stale modality look like a building that simply cannot measure that thing.
Fix_Approach: Topped all eight up. The DURABLE fix is a decision for the user: either add these modalities to data-publisher, or schedule the refresh. Until then staleness recurs within about a day of no attention.
Verification: All eight now 0.2h old and a re-run reports 'already current' (idempotent). Supersedes BUG-261's claim that parking_data holds zero rows -- it holds 5,268. pm25_data is still empty and correctly so: the 35 real PM2.5 sensors resolve via database1, and pm25_data is only a SATURATE provisioning target.

Title: CLEAR DEFAULT is NOT safe here - the safety check is confounded by inference
Description: With the leak stopped, the obvious next step was to clear the default graph, since all legitimate ingestion goes into named graphs. Measuring first: brick:Room counts 233 ANYWHERE and 0 inside named graphs. Those typings are either inferred or default-graph-only, and GraphDB does not attribute inferred triples to a named graph -- so the measurement cannot distinguish 'safe to clear' from 'clearing destroys every room typing and blinds the coverage audit'.
Root_Cause: A GRAPH ?g {} test silently excludes inferred triples, so it under-reports what would survive a clear. The check looked conclusive and was not.
Fix_Approach: Do NOT run CLEAR DEFAULT on this evidence. The safe route is a rebuild: back up, drop the repository, re-ingest through ttl_uploader (deterministic and named-graph scoped), then verify entity counts against the pre-drop numbers. Much less urgent now that the leak is fixed -- the bloat is stable, not growing. [2026-08-27] Resolved by not needing the confounded check at all. Instead of asking 'is CLEAR DEFAULT safe', the question asked was 'is every IRI subject in the live graph reproducible from input/' -- a set difference over 5,850 building-namespace subjects, which inference cannot confound because it compares SUBJECTS, not type counts.
Verification: 146 subjects would have been lost. Every one classified BEFORE the drop: 68 AHU phantoms, 50 legacy 4-triple sensor stubs with no label or timeseries, 5 simulated potability statements, 4 feed points FeedRegistry recreates at boot, and bldg:Building (repointed to AbacwsBuilding). ZERO unexplained. Two genuine at-risk finds were recovered to files first -- see BUG-335.

Title: link_to_work_order() has no caller, so the two ticket universes can never join
Description: user_reports.work_order_id exists, ReportIntakeService.link_to_work_order() exists and tickets.py reads the column -- and NOTHING calls the linker. So every reconciliation reports '163 reported by people and 217 raised as work orders, with none linked to each other yet', and 'is my report being dealt with?' is unanswerable by construction. Fourth instance today of a capability that exists with no invoker (institutional adapter, AssetStatus triples, ServiceSchedule triples, this).
Root_Cause: The link is correctly designed as explicit-never-inferred, but nothing was ever built to record it.
Fix_Approach: NEEDS A PRODUCT DECISION, not a patch: should filing a fault report automatically raise an estate work order, or is that a triage step a human performs? I drafted the automatic version and BACKED IT OUT -- the storage adapters expose execute_query(sql) only, validate queries as read-only, and would have refused the INSERT while my except-clause swallowed the failure. That would have shipped a silent no-op, which is the defect class this session has been removing. [2026-08-27] Owner chose the inference rule: same space + overlapping window + compatible category, recorded as an inferred link with its basis. That contradicts tickets.py's opening argument ('the link is explicit, never inferred'), so the two are reconciled rather than one overriding the other: propose_links() produces SUGGESTIONS carrying their own basis, and merge() stays explicit-only. An inferred merge would double-count in a way that looks authoritative -- worse than the undercount it replaces -- and two tickets in one room on one day are still not necessarily one issue. progress_note() gives three distinct answers: a recorded link is a fact, a candidate is a lead, and nothing is nothing. Wired into the joined ticket lane, which is where the 'none linked to each other yet' line was printed.
Verification: 21 tests. Same space only (not nearby -- proximity inference produced BUG-189); work order must POSTDATE the report and fall inside 72h; two DIFFERENT known trades in one room are two issues; an unreadable trade is not evidence either way and does not block; an ambiguous title naming two trades reads as unknown rather than being bucketed; a recorded link always beats a guess and a work order already claimed is off the table, so one work order is never offered to two people. Suite 3,343 pass. Fixed a brittle neighbouring test while here: it asserted on a fixed 2,600-character slice of the file and failed on length rather than behaviour.

Title: The whole OCBV vocabulary was unreachable from the SPARQL lane (no prefix declared)
Description: EXTENDED_PREFIXES declared brick, rdfs, ref, qudt and a dozen others -- and neither ontosage: nor hbco:. Every query the agent generated referencing an OCBV term was therefore a SPARQL SYNTAX ERROR, so amenities, knowledge topics, lifts, AV equipment, network services, asset status, service schedules and the new parking sensor class were all unusable from the query lane.
Root_Cause: The OCBV layer was added to the ontology and to several services, but the query agent's prefix block was never extended with it. Nothing failed loudly: a syntax error surfaces as an empty result or an exception that a fallback swallows.
Fix_Approach: Declare ontosage: and hbco: in the standard prefix block.
Verification: Live: 'how many parking bays are free right now?' now resolves ontosage:Parking_Occupancy_Sensor and reads the actual sensor. 5 prefixes pinned by test.

Title: A concept naming a class and its parent resolved to the PARENT, answering 294 for a bay count
Description: concept_resolver._brick_local shortened only brickschema.org IRIs and passed everything else through, so an OCBV class arrived as a BARE FULL IRI. Two things broke silently: the agent's class choice takes brick_classes[0] from a SET (so order is arbitrary) and its specificity check looks for a CURIE prefix that could never match; and a bare IRI embedded in generated SPARQL is a syntax error anyway, because an IRI needs angle brackets where a CURIE does not. Visible symptom: 'how many parking spaces are free?' answered 294 -- the building's SPACE COUNT, from a COUNT over the 40-instance generic class -- while one parking sensor with 5,268 rows sat behind the specific class. A real number, from a real query, to a different question, so the numeric guard had no reason to object.
Root_Cause: A shortener written for one vocabulary, used for all of them, in a codebase that had since grown a second vocabulary by design.
Fix_Approach: Shorten every known vocabulary to a CURIE, and choose the most specific class as a PURE function: an ontosage: class exists precisely because Brick lacked one and is declared a subclass of the nearest Brick parent, so where both appear the extension is by construction the child.
Verification: Live: the class resolves to ontosage:Parking_Occupancy_Sensor and the answer reads the sensor. 15 tests, including both candidate orderings -- the set ordering meant the parent won roughly half the time.

Title: A graph-querying 'fix' never once ran: its exception was swallowed at DEBUG level
Description: The first version of the most-specific-class check asked the graph. It ALWAYS fell back: _execute_query raised '[Errno -2] Name or service not known' from its Fuseki fallback path, the except swallowed it with logger.debug, and the function returned candidates[0]. I 'verified' it three times -- twice it looked correct purely because the right answer happened to be first in the list.
Root_Cause: An exception handler that logs below the running level turns a total failure into a plausible default. Seventh measurement-apparatus failure in this project.
Fix_Approach: Raised the log level to see the real error, then removed the need for it entirely: the check is now a pure function with no network call and therefore no silent fallback. Pinned by a test asserting it is not a coroutine.
Verification: Both candidate orders return the extension class in a pure unit test.

Title: A 'right now' bay count is answered with a windowed MEAN, and the model invents a threshold
Description: 'How many parking bays are free right now?' now reads the correct sensor and answers '41.63 free parking bays'. Two problems: a bay count is an integer and 'right now' wants the LATEST value, not a mean over a window -- 41.63 bays cannot exist. And the narration added 'comfortably above the typical threshold of 30-35 free bays for this facility', a threshold that appears nowhere in the data or the ontology.
Root_Cause: The analytics lane aggregates by default, and the invented threshold is the familiar failure of a model filling in domain colour around a real number.
Fix_Approach: A present-tense question on a count modality should take the latest reading and render it as an integer. The invented threshold is the more serious half and belongs to the standards-claims gate (V6-T34): a comparison needs a cited band.
Verification: Resolved as a side effect of the class fix. 'How many parking bays are free right now?' now answers 'about 42 parking bays free right now (the most recent reading is 41.6)' -- it leads with the LATEST value as an integer and reports the mean as context rather than as the answer, and the invented '30-35 typical threshold' did not recur once the correct sensor class was in play.

Title: 'How many parking SPACES are free?' still answers 294 while the bay phrasing answers correctly
Description: With the class fixed, 'how many parking BAYS are free right now?' reads the sensor, but 'how many parking SPACES are free?' still answers 294. Both resolve the same concept and the same class, so the divergence is downstream -- the second phrasing reaches a COUNT over spaces rather than a reading.
Root_Cause: Not yet isolated. 'spaces' is also the word this system uses for ROOMS, so the question is genuinely ambiguous to a counting lane.
Fix_Approach: Trace which lane produces the count once the class is correct; likely the countable-metadata rule claiming 'how many ... spaces'.
Verification: Root cause found: a TEMPLATE, not the LLM. _template_sparql fires a generic space-count on any query containing a zone word (zone/room/space) that asks for a count -- so 'how many parking SPACES are free?' matched on the word 'spaces' and returned COUNT(DISTINCT ?space) = 294, the building's room count. The template now yields when a concept has already resolved a specific class: a generic space count is the right answer to 'how many rooms are there?' and the wrong answer to any question the building's own vocabulary recognises as being about something measurable. Verified live: no longer answers 294. Verified NOT over-suppressed -- no concept resolves for plain room/zone counts, so those still use the template (pinned by test).

Title: V6-T45 is marked done and every term it declares has zero readers
Description: Module P of the OCBV schema -- 'Amenity service status and potability' -- declares PotabilityStatement, amenityStatus, appliesToOutlet, potabilityAuthority, potabilityIssuedOn and potabilityValue. ALL SIX have zero references anywhere in orchestrator/ or scripts/. The word 'potability' does not appear in the codebase at all. The task is marked done.
Root_Cause: Fifth instance of the same pattern found today: a capability delivered as vocabulary or data with nothing that reads it back. The others were the institutional feed adapter, the AssetStatus triples, the ServiceSchedule triples and link_to_work_order(). Each passes its own tests, each presents from outside as an honest decline, and each was marked complete.
Fix_Approach: Either wire it -- a potability/amenity-status question needs a lane the way asset state got one -- or reopen T45. Found by the audit lessons.md #87 proposed: for each kind of data the system stores, grep for the code that reads it back. [2026-08-27] WIRED, in two steps. amenityStatus/statusOf were joined and read on 2026-08-26 (a broken fountain is now excluded). The remaining four terms are now read too: the resolver binds potabilityValue, potabilityAuthority and potabilityIssuedOn and renders the claim WITH the owner and date the schema calls required -- surfacing the value alone would have reproduced the unattributable health claim the module exists to prevent. An unattributed statement reports as unverified; a missing date is stated; UNKNOWN is rendered as 'nobody has assessed it', which the schema names as a legitimate answer and which is not the same as unsafe. PotabilityStatement itself stays unreferenced BY DESIGN -- it is a KnowledgeTopic subclass so the resolver finds it through inference (lessons.md #91). appliesToOutlet is authoring vocabulary, read by the same inference path.
Verification: 10 tests in tests/test_potability_statement.py covering all four render paths, the query, and the amenity->fact hop -- the branch that surfaces a topic was entered only when answerText or a contact was present, so a statement carrying nothing but potability fields would have fallen through to the physical-amenity rendering and dropped the claim. Full suite 3,285 pass. NOT DONE, deliberately: no potability statement is authored for bldg1. bldg1 is a REAL building, and provisioning a synthetic 'the water is safe to drink' claim about one is the harm this module guards against, whatever provenance flag rides with it. The vocabulary is readable; the claim is the building owner's to publish.

Title: The forecast-skill registry vocabulary has no readers either
Description: ontosage:ForecastSkill declares backtestMAE, backtestMAPE, ciCoverage and horizonHours. None of the four appears anywhere in orchestrator/ or scripts/. The V5 PREDICT pillar reports CI95 coverage from its own artifact, so the measured result is real -- but the GRAPH vocabulary for publishing forecast skill alongside the building is unused.
Root_Cause: Vocabulary declared ahead of the code that would populate or read it.
Fix_Approach: Lower priority than Module P because the pillar's numbers do not depend on it. Either publish skill into the graph and read it there, or drop the vocabulary so the schema stops advertising something the system does not do. [2026-08-27] Owner chose (a): publish measured skill and read it there. scripts/publish_forecast_skill.py TRANSCRIBES the grader's registry (volumes/<id>/artifacts/forecast_skill.json) into ForecastSkill triples -- it computes nothing, and carries graded_at through as skillMeasuredAt so a stale cell reads as stale. 18 cells published for bldg2, 162 triples. forecast_skill.py reads them back and the observability lane answers 'how accurate are your forecasts?' from the graph, which is exactly what the schema said the vocabulary was for.
Verification: 17 tests. Coverage below nominal is flagged as optimistic rather than softened; an unmeasured modality is reported as unmeasured, never as bad; the fit count rides with the coverage figure because 0.83 over six fits is a different claim from 0.83 over six hundred. Routing needed BOTH halves: a new rule ahead of forecast_to_trend AND a guard inside it, because this contract applies every matching rule and the LAST one wins -- the new rule fired first and was overwritten, answering 'how good are your predictions for CO2?' with a CO2 forecast. Pinned-order test updated in the same commit.

Title: An out-of-service amenity was recommended exactly as though it worked
Description: ontosage:amenityStatus links an amenity to its AssetStatus record, and the schema states plainly why: 'an amenity whose status is out_of_service must be EXCLUDED from recommendations rather than listed with a caveat: somebody who walks to a broken fountain has been given a wrong answer, however well hedged.' Nothing read the property -- the capability resolver's amenity query never joined it -- so a broken drinking fountain was offered as a drinking fountain.
Root_Cause: Fifth instance of a capability shipped without an invoker, found by the audit lessons.md #87 proposed. V6-T45 was marked done with all six of its declared terms unread.
Fix_Approach: Join amenityStatus -> statusValue in the resolver query, carry it on the amenity, and EXCLUDE non-operational amenities from the answer. When everything that matched is out of service the answer says so rather than returning nothing: 'no drinking fountains here' sends someone away, 'the ones here are not working' tells them what is wrong. An ABSENT status means usable -- most buildings publish none, and defaulting the other way would empty every answer.
Verification: 12 tests including the all-broken case and the absent-status default, plus one asserting the query actually contains the join -- the property was declared for a year and never read, so the join is the thing worth pinning.

Title: The model benchmark printed '0 / 0' for probes it never ran, which reads as a pass
Description: With --invariance-only the fabrication and privacy probes are skipped entirely, and the report's headline 'Guarantees' table still printed '**0** / 0' for every arm. Zero out of zero renders identically to a clean sweep, under a heading that says the guarantees are the point of the benchmark. Anyone reading the artifact -- including me, an hour later -- would quote it as 'fabricated = 0 on every model'.
Root_Cause: A denominator of zero rendered as though it were a measurement. Exactly BUG-191's mistake one layer up: there a grader scored a refusal as a pass because a digit appeared in it; here a table scores an unrun probe as a pass because a zero appeared in it. Eighth measurement-apparatus defect in this project.
Fix_Approach: Render '_not run_' when the denominator is zero, and add an explicit warning block when a run measured no guarantees at all. The already-generated artifact was corrected in place rather than left to be quoted.
Verification: Report regenerated shape checked; the existing artifact now says _not run_.

Title: Plan invariance is not established even within ONE model: 3 of 8 plans reproduce on a repeat run
Description: T49's acceptance criterion is 'deliberative fingerprints identical across models'. Measured on three local arms: cross-model invariance is 2/8 identical, 3/8 divergent, 3/8 downgraded (a weaker model fell back to a reflex 1-step plan). But the NOISE FLOOR -- the same model, gpt-oss:20b, run twice -- is only 3/8 identical. Cross-model agreement (2/8) is therefore AT OR BELOW run-to-run variance, and none of the observed differences can be attributed to the model at all.
Root_Cause: CAVEAT-160 at scale: the CQ-IR compile step wobbles at temperature 0, so the 'deterministic plan' is deterministic only given that the same compile is produced -- which it often is not. BUG-184 established that plan_fingerprint is the right anchor and the harness does compare it; the wobble is upstream of the fingerprint, in what gets compiled.
Fix_Approach: FIXED on both causes BUG-184 separated, and they needed different fixes. (a) LANE DOWNGRADES, 2 of the 3 mismatches and the larger contributor: all ten benchmark questions match DELIBERATE_RE, so the pattern was never the gap -- the two rules that route to the lane gated on DISJOINT intent sets (weak+recommend, and analytics+sensor_data) and anything the classifier put elsewhere fell between them. Naming a floor pulls a question toward floor_plan; 'where can I sit near the cafe' toward spatial_query. _SUPERLATIVE_TAKEOVER_INTENTS now covers floor_plan, spatial_query, compare and trend as well. Safe because DELIBERATE_RE must still match, and it needs a superlative or an explicit should-I shape. (b) COMPILE DIVERGENCE: the raw compiler response is cached in Redis, keyed on the normalised question + modality set + prompt hash + PROVIDER + MODEL. The raw TEXT is stored rather than the parsed CQIR, because everything after the LLM call is deterministic validation against a closed vocabulary -- replaying the text reproduces the plan exactly and a stored plan cannot drift from the parser that made it.
Verification: 35 tests. THE TRAP, pinned by its own test: keyed on the question alone this cache would hand model B the plan model A compiled, and the multi-model benchmark would report perfect invariance for the very property it exists to measure -- a cache that fabricates the result is worse than the wobble it fixes. CQIR_COMPILE_CACHE=false turns it off for the noise-floor arm, because 'what the compiler does' (cache off) and 'what a user experiences on a repeat' (cache on) are different numbers and reporting the second as the first is how a fix becomes a fiction. Also fixed a side-effect: offline compiler tests were reaching for an absent Redis, 68s -> 6.3s. Suite 3,683 pass parked. CAVEAT-160 is the same root cause and is covered by (b) for repeats.

Title: A 'which rooms' question was answered with a flat list of times
Description: 'Which rooms have teaching sessions this week?' returned '1000 booking(s) for the building this week' followed by ten start-end times. The count was right and the unit of the answer was wrong: the question names ROOMS as the thing to enumerate, and the reader was left to aggregate a thousand sessions by hand.
Root_Cause: One flat rendering served two different questions. bookings_list never asked what the questioner wanted counted.
Fix_Approach: Detect the rooms-as-unit phrasing and group by room, reusing the reverse uuid->room lookup the availability list already builds rather than adding a second one. The list states what it truncated instead of stopping silently.
Verification: Duplicate of CAVEAT-302 -- logged as a new row by mistake; the fix is recorded there.

Title: A schedule question about one place was answered with the whole building's schedule
Description: 'When does the cafe open?' returned the opening hours of every amenity that publishes a ServiceSchedule. Not fabricated, but the named place's answer was buried among places nobody asked about.
Root_Cause: _answer_schedule never read the place named in the question.
Fix_Approach: A module-level _named_location matches the longest known amenity name appearing in the question (whitespace- and underscore-insensitive) and scopes the answer to it; an unmatched question keeps the building-wide list.
Verification: Duplicate of CAVEAT-308 -- logged as a new row by mistake; the fix is recorded there.

Title: The feeds validator kept its own list of feed types and rejected a working timetable feed
Description: bldg1/feeds.yaml declares 'type: timetable', which the feed registry dispatches through InstitutionalFeedAdapter. validate_feeds_yaml held a separate _FEED_TYPES set that had never been told, so it reported the feed as an unknown type AND as missing brick_class and storage -- two keys an institutional source does not have by design, because it produces events rather than a Brick point with rows. Surfaced by a new test that simply ran the full building validation.
Root_Cause: Two copies of one list. The registry's _ADAPTER_CLASSES is the authority on what is dispatchable; the validator restated it and drifted behind.
Fix_Approach: Read the accepted types from the registry map, and require brick_class/storage only for feeds that become points. A telemetry feed missing them still fails, and an unknown type is still rejected -- both pinned by tests.
Verification: tests/test_measurand_typing.py, 4 tests; full suite 3,222 pass.

Title: Every control action was recorded and nothing could read one back
Description: SimDriver.set_point() has written a row to Postgres actuation_log for every approved setpoint change since T23 -- who asked, which point, what value, why, when -- and bldg1 ships with actuation.driver: sim and three writable points, so the path is LIVE on the shipped building. No code in the repository ever issued a SELECT against that table. 'What did you change today?' and 'who approved that?' were unanswerable about actions the system had itself recorded.
Root_Cause: SIXTH instance of a capability present, correct, tested and uninvoked. The previous five were in the graph layer; this one is relational, which is why the earlier audit did not see it.
