Description: After the 64.7-minute full probe run, /health stopped answering from the host (three attempts: 25 s, 60 s and 60 s, all connection-timeout) AND from inside the container itself (docker exec curl to 127.0.0.1:8000, 25 s timeout). Docker reported the container 'Up (healthy)' throughout - a stale healthcheck result. Meanwhile the container logs showed the rules engine and feed pollers executing normally on the same second, so the process was alive and the event loop was NOT blocked in general. A later attempt returned http=200 in 0.105 s with no intervention. An authenticated script failed outright at /auth/login on a 30 s read timeout during the window.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. The strongest candidate is the feed/rules polling loops: the log burst at the failure window shows many sequential MySQL queries and GraphDB POSTs interleaved with outbound calls to api.open-meteo.com, one of which returned HTTP 503. An external call with a generous timeout on the same loop that serves HTTP would stall request handling while leaving already-scheduled background tasks visibly progressing - which matches exactly what was observed. Unconfirmed.
Fix_Approach: Not yet fixed. Do not raise client timeouts - that hides it. Establish whether feed polling shares the request event loop and whether rest_poll bounds its external calls; the python-style rule 'never block the event loop' is the relevant contract. The Docker healthcheck also reported healthy through a total outage, so it is not currently evidence of anything.
Verification: Measured 2026-09-10 around 00:30 UTC. Unreachable internally and externally; recovered unaided within minutes. Related to but distinct from CAVEAT-500, which is per-question latency variance rather than a total outage.
Refs: orchestrator/services/feeds/rest_poll.py; orchestrator/services/rules_engine.py; orchestrator/main.py (healthcheck); CAVEAT-500; V12-19; REV-B15; Gate B operational controls

Title: The actuation probe case asserts only the lane while its note claims it asserts a decline
Description: The case 'Open the windows on floor 3.' carries expect_intent=control and forbid_intent=capability and NOTHING about the answer, while its own note reads 'An actuation request must reach the control lane and be declined there, with a reason.' It therefore passes whether the request is declined OR executed. Measured 2026-09-10: 'Fix the temperature in here' reaches the same control lane and returns 'Command queued for approval (ID 688bc706). Target: urn:bldg1:AHU-F5-SP', because that point is one of three in building.yaml points_writable. The windows decline only because no window point is writable - not because actuation declines. Two requests, the same lane, opposite outcomes, and the case cannot tell them apart. SECOND OBSERVATION, same answer: the queued command reads 'Target: urn:bldg1:AHU-F5-SP -> ' with an EMPTY value. 'Fix the temperature in here' names no setpoint, and the lane queued an approval request anyway rather than asking what value was wanted. Impact is bounded today only because driver=sim writes to a log; under any real driver an approver would be shown a command whose effect is undefined. Fix together with the case assertions: an actuation request with no resolvable value must ask, not queue.
Root_Cause: The case was written to fix a ROUTING defect (actuation reaching the capability KB) and asserts the routing fix. Its note then described the intended end behaviour, which nothing checks. This is the review's W4-4 requirement applied to an existing case: 'assert the final output, not only the route'. It is also how the first draft of docs/V12_SUPPORTED_SCOPE.md came to state that actuation was out of scope and declined by design - the scope was written from a comment rather than from the system.
Fix_Approach: Not yet fixed. Two cases, one per side of the writable boundary: a non-writable target must decline WITH its reason, and a writable target must queue for approval naming the point and the expiry, never execute silently. Correct the misleading note in the same change. Belongs with V12-01's output-assertion work.
Verification: Measured live 2026-09-10 while re-asking BUG-157 for V12-02. driver=sim, so an approved command writes to the Postgres actuation_log and nothing physical moves; control:write is still required to approve.

Title: A question about past alarms CREATES a monitoring alert, with a meaningless threshold
Description: 'Have there been any alarms this week?' routes to intent=alert and returns 'Alert created (ID: 5054c67d). I will notify you when sensor > 0.0. Use list my alerts to manage your alerts.' A retrospective question was executed as a standing request for future monitoring: the user asked what happened and got a subscription. The threshold is also meaningless - no sensor is named and any positive reading satisfies it.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. The alert lane appears to claim the words alarm/alert without checking the TENSE or mood of the request. CLAUDE.md's routing-precedence rules already draw exactly this distinction elsewhere - comfort QUESTIONS go to analytics rather than complaint; fault STATEMENTS are reports while questions are not - so the contract exists and this lane does not honour it.
Fix_Approach: Not yet fixed. A retrospective question must reach the register holding past alarms, or honestly say that class is empty. Creating state in response to a question is worse than declining: it is a side effect the user did not ask for. Belongs with V12-23, the routing repairs still open.
Verification: Found by V12-02's live re-ask of TODO-490 on 2026-09-10. 48.9s, status OK.

Title: 'Who accessed the server room?' returns 196 unfiltered building bookings
Description: The question routes to intent=events and returns '196 booking(s) for the building today' as a time-slot list with attendee counts. Three faults in one answer: the wrong register (room BOOKINGS, not access events), no filter to the named room, and a person-level 'who' question answered with occupancy data. AccessEvent is never mentioned, present or absent.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. Candidates: the events lane matches 'access' to its bookings register by a shared word, which is the BUG-489 shape - a held register matched by a generic word outranking an absent one matched precisely - and the room referent is dropped rather than used as a filter.

Description: In the CO2 report for Room 5.01, Recommendation 1 of 3 reads 'Extend Data Capture - Increase the row limit or adjust query parameters to capture the complete dataset for a more comprehensive assessment.' The cap disclosure and the recommendation generator need separating - a limitation is context for reading the numbers, not an item on the reader's to-do list.

Title: The live admin password is in pushed git history and has been on GitHub since 2026-07-08
Description: tasks/REVIEW_AND_EXTEND_PROMPT.md line 135 contains the real ADMIN_PASSWORD in an example curl - an exact match for the value in .env. It was committed in 3756e8a 'chore: dev requirements + planning/task notes' (2026-07-08) and removed from tracking in 1a8ec2e 'chore(repo): untrack tasks/' (2026-08-12). Untracking does not remove a blob: 3756e8a is an ancestor of HEAD and is contained by ontosage/development, ontosage/main, origin/main and origin/HEAD on https://github.com/suhasdevmane/OntoSage.git. The credential has therefore been on the remote for roughly two months. Scope checked and BOUNDED: of 14 non-trivial secret values in .env, only ADMIN_PASSWORD is a chosen value exposed this way; the other matches (GRAPHDB_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD, API_KEY, API_PGPASSWORD, PG_THINGSBOARD_PASSWORD) are UNCHANGED DEFAULTS, and STRICT_SECRETS=false is set deliberately for local dev, which CLAUDE.md sanctions. Those are hygiene, not exposure.
Root_Cause: A working note written for a human included a runnable login example with the real password pasted in, and tasks/ was tracked at the time. Untracking the directory a month later made it invisible to every present-tense check without removing it from history.
Fix_Approach: USER DECISION 2026-09-10, taken after the exposure was put to them in full: the repository is PRIVATE and has never been shared, nothing is deployed anywhere, and ADMIN_PASSWORD will be rotated as part of the production plan rather than now. No history rewrite - the cost (filter-repo plus a coordinated force-push across every clone) is not justified while the only readers are the owner. Passwords stay as they are in each per-building .env, all of which are gitignored. This is a considered acceptance of a bounded risk, not an oversight: the exposure window is one private repository with one reader. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD, so the class cannot recur: scripts/check_staged_secrets.py plus a TRACKED .githooks/pre-commit, enabled with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. WHAT REOPENS THIS: making the repository public, sharing it with anyone, or any deployment. At that point rotation is not optional and the history question returns.
Verification: Guard delivered and LIVE-FIRE TESTED 2026-09-10, both directions. A file carrying the real ADMIN_PASSWORD was staged and `git commit` was REFUSED with HEAD unchanged at ccdce42; a clean file committed normally and was then reset. Self-test passes four checks (planted secret blocks, clean stays clean, credential FILENAME blocks, a $VAR reference is not flagged). Seven unit tests in tests/test_the_secret_scan_would_have_caught_it.py pin the behaviours rather than the import, because the literal guard once reported clean over two directories while fifteen real literals sat outside its scope. Scanning all 1,806 tracked files: ZERO live credentials, 82 INFO patterns (non-blocking heuristics). The scanner reports ERROR on an exact match against a real .env value and INFO on a generic pattern - its first version blocked on eight findings of which none were real, including the $ADMIN_PASSWORD reference that was the remedy, and a guard that cries wolf gets --no-verify.

Title: The grounding verifier counted SQL rows one level too shallow, so it has never seen a real result
Description: verifier_agent._count_sql_rows read sql_result['data']. The sql node writes its rows at sql_result['results']['data']. So the counter returned 0 on EVERY turn where SQL actually returned data, and the verifier fell through to its else branch: source='none', grounded=False, confidence=0.20 - for answers built from thousands of real rows. This is BUG-477 one layer up: the report agent read the same dict one level too shallow and, in its own words, 'has never once seen the data either caller fetched'. The same mistake sat in the component whose entire job is deciding whether an answer is grounded. It is why BUG-475's fabricated report carried sql_rows=0 beside a log line reading 'Query returned 1000 rows'. SECOND DEFECT in the same record: the else branch also fires for every lane the verifier does not read - floor_plan, register, events, deliberate, asset_state, observability, diagnosis - reporting 'I checked and found no support' when the truth is 'I was not looking'. Those are different facts (review p. 8).
Root_Cause: Two independent faults that compounded into one reassuring-looking flag. (1) A wrapper-depth mismatch between the sql lane's output shape and the verifier's reader, invisible because the verifier fails toward 'ungrounded' and nothing consumed that verdict. (2) No distinction between 'assessed and unsupported' and 'outside what this verifier reads'. Both stayed invisible for as long as `grounded` decided nothing; V12-03 made it decide publication, and the defect surfaced immediately.
Fix_Approach: _count_sql_rows now reads the nested shape, the unwrapped shape and a bare list under 'results' - all three, not one, because narrowing to a single accepted shape is how a working caller gets broken silently. An `applicable` field is added to the verification record, computed from an explicit _ASSESSABLE_INTENTS set, and the publication gate refuses to act unless it is True.
Verification: Found by a LIVE regression check, not by tests: the first deployment of the V12-03 publication gate withheld a report that had 1,000 real rows behind it, on the same question that had answered correctly an hour earlier. The unit tests could not have caught it - they supply the verification record by hand, so they exercised the gate's logic and never the verifier's. Four new tests pin the row counter at all three shapes and the assessable-lane list. LIVE RE-CHECK STILL OWED on the rebuilt process.

Title: The planner's results never reach the bus, so nothing downstream can see a planner-routed turn
Description: PlannerAgent._execute_step writes every result it produces - sparql_result, sql_result, analytics_result, anomaly_result, report_result, export_result, capability_result, floor_plan_result, spatial_result - into a LOCAL `context` dict. `grep` for a merge into state.intermediate_results returns nothing: _planner_node writes only `planner_result`. So every consumer that reads the bus sees an EMPTY bus for any turn routed through the planner, which includes the whole `report` intent. Measured live 2026-09-10: a report built from real rows verified as sensors=0, sql_rows=0, report_rows=0. The verifier was not reading stale data; it was reading nothing. The same blindness applies to the evidence record and to anything else keyed off the reserved bus names.
Root_Cause: The planner was built to orchestrate sub-agents and hand back one composed answer, so it kept its intermediate products locally. That was invisible for as long as nothing downstream needed them. It became load-bearing when the verifier, the evidence record and then V12-03's publication gate all keyed off the bus.
Fix_Approach: FIXED under V12-14 and LIVE VERIFIED 2026-09-11. It was deliberately not attempted in the same pass that found it, because merging the planner's context onto the bus touches the reserved-key contract, the per-turn stale-clearing list (BUG-392) and the evidence record together, and doing that at the end of a long session is how a fix for one thing takes another with it. Belongs with V12-14, which is exactly 'audit every reserved bus key against what actually writes it'. INTERIM: `report` and `export` are removed from the verifier's _ASSESSABLE_INTENTS so the publication gate stops withholding good reports. CONSEQUENCE, stated rather than hidden: R1 - publication enforcement - REMAINS OPEN for the report lane, which is the lane BUG-475 happened in.
Verification: Found while live-checking V12-03. The gate withheld a report that had 1,000 real rows behind it; three successive hypotheses about why were each refuted by measurement - first the row-counter depth (real, BUG-508, fixed: analytics went sql_rows=0 -> 6960), then the assessable-lane split (real, fixed), and only then the empty bus. The log line that settled it: '[verifier] grounded=False, confidence=0.20, source=none, sensors=0, sql_rows=0, report_rows=0' on a turn whose adapter logs show dozens of successful queries. || LIVE VERIFIED 2026-09-11: a report turn logged '[planner] published to bus: sparql_result, sql_result, analytics_result, report_result' and the verifier on the SAME turn read 'grounded=True, confidence=0.88, source=analytics, sensors=2, sql_rows=1000' - against sensors=0, sql_rows=0 the day before. The whole chain planner -> bus -> verifier -> publication gate now works, and a good report publishes rather than being withheld.
Refs: orchestrator/agents/planner_agent.py _execute_step (lines ~501-554); orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py _planner_node:6286; orchestrator/agents/verifier_agent.py _ASSESSABLE_INTENTS; BUG-508; BUG-475; V12-14; V12-03; REV-R1

Title: The plan trace keyed three of its five stages off names nothing writes, so the data pipeline recorded itself as not having run
Description: _TRACE_STAGE_MARKERS in _orchestrator.py, whose own comment calls it 'the shared-state contract in CLAUDE.md', paired ('sparql','sparql_results'), ('sql','sql_data') and ('analytics','analytics_output'). None of those three keys exists; the real ones are sparql_result, sql_result and analytics_result. The tuple feeds the plan_trace step fallback - steps = executed_stages or [name for name, key in _TRACE_STAGE_MARKERS if results.get(key) is not None] - so whenever that fallback ran, the three principal data stages could never appear and a turn that ran the whole data pipeline recorded itself as having run almost none of it. Only forecast and visualization could ever show. THIRD INSTANCE, found when the suite ran: tests/test_plan_trace.py's own fixture built its state with 'sparql_results' and 'sql_data' - the SAME two non-existent keys. So the test passed against the broken markers and certified a trace the real pipeline could never produce. The test was written from the same wrong list as the code it tested, which is exactly why neither caught the other.
Root_Cause: The same two wrong strings that .claude/rules/agent-patterns.md already records: 'it documented sparql_results and sql_data, strings that appear nowhere in the pipeline'. That file was corrected on 2026-08-22 and assemble.py, its other reader, was fixed. THIS CONSUMER WAS NOT. Correcting prose does not correct the code written from it, and nothing derived this tuple from anything or checked it, so it sat wrong for a further three weeks. analytics_output was a third instance of the same error that the earlier correction did not even notice.
Fix_Approach: The three names corrected in place, with the history written beside them so the next reader knows this list has been wrong twice. The durable part is tests/test_reserved_keys_have_writers.py, which parses the source with ast for every key assigned into intermediate_results and fails when a DOCUMENTED reserved key has no writer - it found analytics_output on its first run. agent-patterns.md and CLAUDE.md both corrected to name analytics_result. The test fixture corrected to the real keys, plus a COUNTER-TEST asserting that sparql_results / sql_data / analytics_output produce no stages - so the fixture cannot drift back to invented names without failing.
Verification: Found by the V12-14 audit test on its first execution, not by review. 7 tests pass, including one that the key extractor reads LIST ITEMS rather than prose - its first version re-reported analytics_output the moment the fix explained why the name was wrong, which would have trained the next person to delete the check instead of the key. LIVE RE-CHECK OF plan_trace STILL OWED: no live model this session. || LIVE VERIFIED 2026-09-11: plan_trace.steps came back ['sparql', 'sql', 'analytics'] on both a report turn and an analytics turn. Before the fix those three stages could NEVER appear, because the markers named sparql_results / sql_data / analytics_output, none of which any lane writes. The owed live re-check is discharged.

Title: DocumentBuilder.render promised a dict and could fall off the end; the BUG-476 guard could not see it
Description: render() is annotated -> Dict[str, Any] and its try body ended with three bare `if output_format == ...: return ...` statements and no else. If output_format were none of html/pdf/docx it fell through and returned None. LATENT, NOT LIVE: a guard forty lines earlier rejects anything outside that tuple, so the fall-through is unreachable today. That is protection by DISTANCE - add a format to the guard's tuple, forget a branch below, and render() returns None silently while callers read it defensively. That is BUG-476's exact shape, where _standardize_results fell off the end and the pipeline read None as an empty answer for as long as it had existed.
Root_Cause: The BUG-476 guard could not see it. _falls_off_the_end ended with `return not isinstance(last, (ast.While, ast.For, ast.If, ast.With, ast.AsyncWith, ast.Match))`, which treats ANY trailing `if` as terminating - so a function ending in a bare `if ...: return` was invisible to the very check written to catch functions that fall off the end. The same routine's Try arm asked whether ANY tail returned, when one returning handler does not stop another falling through. And the sweep scanned orchestrator/ only, leaving shared/ - 3,920 lines including the config every service reads - unscanned.
Fix_Approach: Explicit terminal branch in render() so the promise is self-contained rather than dependent on a distant guard. The durable part is the ANALYSER: _falls_off_the_end replaced with a recursive _terminates() handling If (requires a non-empty else, both branches terminating), Try (all handlers, plus a returning finally), With, Match (all cases) and While (only `while True` with no break). Sweep scope widened to shared/. Six unit tests pin the analyser itself, because the sweep only reports a number and neither of its two errors was visible from that number.
Verification: Corrected analyser over orchestrator/ + shared/: 1,642 + 67 annotated functions, ONE offender - this one - and shared/ clean. The two apparent hits in shared/config.py (get_llm_config, get_embedding_config) were false positives from a cruder heuristic I wrote first; both are exhaustive if/elif/else and a test now pins that shape as terminating so the guard cannot start crying wolf. 12 tests pass in tests/test_standardized_results_are_actually_returned.py.

Title: Every compound unit literal was reduced to its denominator: 'L/s' displayed as 's'
Description: modality_units.qudt_unit_display used _class_local, which splits on '/' unconditionally - correct for a class IRI, catastrophic for a unit. Measured: 'L/s' -> 's', 'm3/h' -> 'h', 'mg/m3' -> 'm3', 'kg/m3' -> 'm3', 'L/min' -> 'min'. Every rate became a time and every mass concentration became a volume. The function's OWN docstring says a bare literal is expected input - it exists because buildings write brick:hasUnit "Pa" as often as the IRI - so mangling literals defeats its purpose. Not hypothetical: 13 live Flow_Sensor points on bldg1 declare "L/s", so the estate's supply-air flow sensors reported their unit as seconds.
Root_Cause: One helper shared between two jobs with opposite rules. A class IRI's local name is after the last separator; a unit literal's slash is division. _class_local was written for the first and reused for the second.
Fix_Approach: A separate _unit_local() that only treats a separator as a delimiter when the token is genuinely an IRI ('://' or '#') or a CURIE (':' with no '/'). _class_local is untouched, so class resolution is unaffected.
Verification: Before: L/s->s, m3/h->h, mg/m3->m3, L/min->min. After: all unchanged, while http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/PA->Pa and unit:PA->Pa still resolve and unit_for_sensor still maps brick:CO2_Level_Sensor->ppm. 6 parametrised cases in tests/test_unit_conversion_contract.py plus an assertion that 's' is NOT a flow unit. Found while building V12-10, by measuring the live graph before writing the contract.

Title: One Brick class carries several incompatible units, and one point carries two units at once
Description: Measured on bldg1's live graph 2026-09-10: Occupancy_Count_Sensor has NUM on 6 points and PERCENT on 2; Air_Quality_Sensor has PPM (2), PPB (1) and MicroGM-PER-M3 (1); Particulate_Matter_Sensor has MicroGM-PER-M3 and PPB; Flow_Sensor has L-PER-MIN, M3 and the literal "L/s" (13); Sound_Level_Sensor has DeciB and DEC. Noise_Sensor_Floor5 carries BOTH DeciB and DEC - one point, two contradictory unit declarations, where DEC is a dimensionless decade and DeciB is a decibel. Any aggregate over one of these classes spans quantities that cannot be combined: a count with a percentage, a mass concentration with a volume ratio.
Root_Cause: Units accumulated from several TTL sources with no cross-check, and nothing consumed them semantically, so a disagreement had no way to surface. This is a DATA question for the building owner, not a code defect.
Fix_Approach: Not a code fix. The contract added in V12-10 (orchestrator/services/units.py) now REFUSES to aggregate across these rather than producing a meaningless number, and names the reason. Resolving the declarations themselves - particularly the two units on Noise_Sensor_Floor5 - needs the owner. Wiring the refusal into the analytics lane is V12-09's aggregation contract. || OWNER DECISION 2026-09-11 on the related CAVEAT-514 settles part of this too: everything stored in database1 is treated as real, so no unit question there turns on provenance. The mixed-unit classes remain a data question for the owner and the units contract still refuses to aggregate across them.
Verification: SPARQL over brick:hasUnit grouped by class, 2026-09-10; full IRIs inspected to rule out display artefacts, which is how the separate BUG-512 was found.

Title: bldg1's wide table mixes loaded and generated rows — by decision, both are treated as real
Description: Measured 2026-09-11 against the live wide table. sensor_data holds 697,329 rows spanning 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-11. Of those, 576,557 (82.7%) are at or before 2025-03-09 - the real snapshot the owner loaded - and 120,772 (17.3%) are after it, generated by data-publisher with PUBLISH_WIDE=true. Both origins live in ONE table, by design and user-confirmed. The consequence is not the ratio, it is the DATE: the measured period ended eighteen months ago, so every question about 'right now', 'today', 'yesterday' or 'this week' is answered entirely from generated rows. Historical questions about early 2025 are answered from real ones. Nothing in an answer distinguishes the two, and before V12-04 nothing could - provenance was resolved per TABLE, and provenance_for_table('sensor_data') returns None because provenance is read from datasources.yaml, which has zero entries for the wide table, while database_registry.yaml is the file that routes to it.
Root_Cause: Not a defect - a development arrangement the owner chose so real-time questions stay testable. It becomes a correctness problem only when an answer presents a generated reading as a measurement, which is R4.
Fix_Approach: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-11, and it supersedes the boundary this row originally proposed. The owner's position: this database stands in for the real one and will be repointed at real credentials later; the 680 `bldg:`-prefixed sensors stored in database1 are real instruments and their readings are to be treated as real throughout, whether a given row was loaded or generated during development. The split is a development artefact, not something an answer should reason about. SO: `measured_through` was REMOVED from database_registry.yaml, with the reasoning left in place above the gap so nobody re-adds it. Provenance for this store is settled per POINT - all 685 (680 sensors + 5 feeds) declare ontosage:isSimulated false in bldg1_measured_origin.ttl. The boundary MECHANISM stays in observation_provenance.py, pinned by its own test, because another building may have a store that genuinely changed character on a date. WHAT THIS DOES NOT WEAKEN: the 1,408 SATURATE-provisioned points are still simulated and still excluded from an operational ranking. That is R4's real target and it keys off the point, not the date.
Verification: Counts reconciled with the owner exactly: 685 points reference database1, of which 680 are `bldg:` building sensors and 5 are feed_* entries - three live rest_poll feeds from api.open-meteo.com (genuinely external measurements) plus ahu_runtime_floor5 and lift_vibration_floor0. All five reference database1 and are real under the same rule. Row counts as originally measured: 697,329 total, 576,557 loaded, 120,772 generated - recorded for the history, no longer acted upon. After the change: a reading taken today from a declared-measured point resolves MEASURED; a SATURATE point resolves SIMULATED.
Refs: input/database_registry.yaml measured_through; orchestrator/services/provenance.py; docs/V12_SUPPORTED_SCOPE.md; V12-04; V12-26; REV-R4

Title: The deliberation lane has been ranking real rooms on SATURATE-simulated readings and calling it a recommendation
Description: R4, caught live the moment V12-04's admissibility pass was wired in. Asked 'Which space on Floor 3 has the best conditions for focused work this afternoon?', the lane previously answered: 'Best match: Room 3.27 - Meeting Room (score 0.5413), illuminance 360.838, noise 52.233, occupancy 18.414'. Every one of those figures came from SATURATE-provisioned points: Room3.27_sat_noise, Room3.27_sat_illuminance and Room3.27_sat_occupancy all declare ontosage:isSimulated true. The rooms are real; the readings never were. Measured across the floor: 253 instrumented points declare simulated, 150 declare nothing, and ZERO declare measured - the lane has never had measured comfort data for Floor 3. The dossier did carry a 'simulated' column, which is exactly the failure mode the review names: the caveat only works if someone reads it, and the headline said 'Best match'. With the admissibility pass live the same question now excludes all 48 candidates for provenance.
Root_Cause: scorer.py had no notion of provenance at all - zero occurrences of simulated, provenance, admissible or eligible across 392 lines - so origin could be displayed but never acted on. SATURATE exists to fill coverage gaps VISIBLY, and it did its job; nothing downstream was ever taught that filling a gap is not the same as measuring it.
Fix_Approach: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-12. The detection is built, tested and live; this building declines to ACT on it, deliberately. input/building.yaml declares provenance.evidence_policy: all_connected_readings - every attached reading is authoritative and an answer does not distinguish simulated from measured. Reasoning: floors 0-4 are placeholders STANDING IN for instruments to be connected later, so excluding them would answer 'I cannot tell you about floor 3' about a floor whose data is present and correct for what it represents. The origin is documented once in README.md rather than repeated in every answer. measured_only is the other setting and turns the exclusion on; it is what a supervised pilot or any deployment where someone ACTS on an answer should set. RECORD THIS ACCURATELY: R4 is ACCEPTED, not resolved. A ranking on floors 0-4 rests on placeholder readings and is not evidence about the physical building; floor 5, with 37 rooms of real instruments, is where a ranking rests on measurements.
Verification: Detection verified live BOTH ways on 2026-09-12. With measured_only: '[scorer] mode=operational ranked 0, excluded 48 (48 for provenance)' on a floor-3 question. With all_connected_readings (the declared policy): the same question returns 'Best match: Room 3.46 - Academic Office, score 0.5401' in 53 s, ranking on the floor's own readings as intended. 27 tests cover the policy and the exclusion machinery.

Title: The secret scanner skipped a file it could not decode and still reported clean
Description: scripts/check_staged_secrets.py ran subprocess with text=True, which decodes using the LOCALE encoding - cp1252 on this machine. A staged file carrying byte 0x9d at offset 848,151 raised UnicodeDecodeError mid-scan; the traceback printed and the scan then reported 'no live credential in 24 file(s)'. The file was never examined and the result said clean. That is precisely the failure the script's own `return 2` path and its docstring exist to prevent - 'never 0 for I could not check, because a guard that reports green from a starved input is worse than no guard' - and it was in the guard itself.
Root_Cause: text=True is the obvious way to get string output from subprocess and silently binds the result to whatever codepage the console happens to use. On a repository containing any non-cp1252 byte - a TTL with an en dash, a YAML with a degree sign - it raises.
Fix_Approach: subprocess.run(..., encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'). `replace` rather than `ignore`: a replacement character stays visible in the output, whereas dropping bytes silently could split a credential across the gap and hide it.
Verification: Before: 24 files scanned with a traceback. After: 25 files scanned, no traceback, still clean. Found while dry-running the scan before a commit, not by a test - the self-test builds its input in memory and never exercises the git read path, which is the gap that let this through.

Title: ARBITER resolved 'yesterday' and 'today' to the SAME rolling 24-hour window, in UTC
Description: deliberation/compiler.py `_PAST_WINDOW_HOURS` mapped BOTH r'yesterday' and r'today' to 24.0 hours, and deliberation/fetch.py turned that number into `(datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(hours=window_hours))` with the END BOUND PASSED AS None. So a deliberation about yesterday was computed over a window running from 24 hours ago to the present -- half of it today -- and the two most common time words in the 6,117-question corpus named the identical interval. The UTC clock adds a second displacement: the stores hold LOCAL stamps, so under a summer-time offset the window was shifted by an hour and silently omitted the most recent hour, which is exactly the part a NOW-basis ranking weights most ('mean of the newest sixth of the window').
Root_Cause: BUG-480 fixed this for the dialogue lane in September by adding calendar_day_bounds(). That was a POINT REPAIR on one lane. The ARBITER compiler and sql_agent each kept their own answer to 'when is yesterday' and both were the pre-BUG-480 answer. A table of DURATIONS cannot express a DATE, so there was no correct number to put in it; the entry existed because BUG-183 needed 'yesterday' to stop raising an unparseable_time signal, and a duration was the only shape the table had.
Fix_Approach: V12-08. The resolution moved to orchestrator/services/requested_interval.py -- ONE module, imported by dialogue_agent (which re-exports for its existing callers), sql_agent and the ARBITER compiler, so 'resolve once' is an import rather than a convention. TimeSpec gained resolved_start/resolved_end; `_fold_named_calendar_day` runs unconditionally and overrides the compile (the question is authoritative, the compile is one reading of it -- the same rule dialogue_agent applies), skipping FORECAST. 'yesterday', 'today' and 'so far today' were REMOVED from the hours table, and only one fold may claim a phrase. fetch_series takes start/end and uses them verbatim, with BOTH bounds; its duration fallback reads the building's clock via local_now(). plan_executor passes the resolved interval through. The interval is in plan_fingerprint, so two questions naming different days no longer certify as the same plan.
Verification: AMENDED 2026-09-15: the core defect stands and its fix stands — 'yesterday' and 'today' both compiled to 24.0 hours, and fetch.py passed no upper bound. The description's claim that utcnow() was ALSO wrong was false (stores are UTC, see BUG-538 WITHDRAWN); the duration fallback is back on store_now(). A second defect in the original BUG-480 fix is now corrected too: local-day bounds were applied directly to UTC-stamped rows, shifting 'yesterday' by the zone offset — calendar_day_bounds now converts the local day's bounds to UTC (to_store). || tests/test_the_requested_interval_is_resolved_once.py -- 27 tests. A07: frozen clock, yesterday and today resolve to different intervals, bounds match an expectation built from `date` arithmetic in the test rather than from the production resolver, and the two days retrieve DIFFERENT date-encoded readings through fetch_series. A08: 00:30 midnight case, and both Europe/London DST transitions (the 25-hour day of 2026-10-25 and the 23-hour day of 2027-03-28), each asserted NOT to equal the 24-hour subtraction. Guard: no formatter constructs a window (no timedelta in four formatting modules) and no module anywhere maps a named day to a number of hours -- both rules verified to FAIL on the pre-fix shapes. LIVE RE-ASK OWED.

Title: A room booked in the next hour could be reported free: the booking window was built from utcnow()
Description: plan_executor._event_availability built the overlap window as `now = datetime.utcnow()` and queried `[now, now + free_crit.hours]`. Bookings are stored as local wall-clock times, so under a summer-time offset the window was displaced by an hour: a room booked in the next hour read as free, and a room whose booking ended an hour ago read as busy. The detail string printed to the user ('booked 14:00-16:00') came from the row, so the times shown were real -- the hour compared against them was not this one.
Root_Cause: Same class as BUG-517: a UTC clock read compared against local stamps. Found by the V12-08 audit rather than by a failing test, because every figure involved is internally consistent.
Fix_Approach: now = building_local_now(schema.building_id).
Verification: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-15: the premise was a measurement error. The stores are UTC (BUG-403): mysql_adapter pins every session to +00:00; sensor_data is a TIMESTAMP column, which MySQL converts to the SESSION zone on read, so a measurement through a SYSTEM-zone (BST) session made it LOOK local. Read on a +00:00 session at 00:34 UTC the newest rows were sensor_data 00:34, co2_data/occupancy_data 00:33, sensor_data_synth 00:32; events are generated from utcnow(). The original utcnow() booking overlap was CORRECT; the 2026-09-12 'fix' to building-local time introduced the one-hour displacement it described. Reverted to store_now().

Title: Freshness advice reported every reading an hour younger than it was, and the PDP an age it did not have
Description: Three sites in workflow/_orchestrator.py compared `datetime.utcnow()` against LOCAL stamps: the PROTECT chokepoint's data_age_minutes (`utcnow() - start_date`), the recommendation recheck line's observation times, and advice.describe(now=...). Under a summer-time offset each understated elapsed time by the zone offset. For the recheck line that is the unsafe direction -- a stale reading presents itself as current, in the one sentence whose whole job is to bound how long the answer stays true. For the PDP it is the safe direction (data reads as fresher, so a finer tier applies) but still wrong.
Root_Cause: The same UTC-vs-local confusion as BUG-517, in the response path.
Fix_Approach: All three now call building_local_now(state.building_id).
Verification: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-15: the premise was a measurement error. The stores are UTC (BUG-403): mysql_adapter pins every session to +00:00; sensor_data is a TIMESTAMP column, which MySQL converts to the SESSION zone on read, so a measurement through a SYSTEM-zone (BST) session made it LOOK local. Read on a +00:00 session at 00:34 UTC the newest rows were sensor_data 00:34, co2_data/occupancy_data 00:33, sensor_data_synth 00:32; events are generated from utcnow(). utcnow() for data age and recheck freshness was CORRECT against UTC observation stamps; the 2026-09-12 change made readings look an hour OLDER. Reverted to store_now().

Title: Every report named its OLDEST reading as the latest
Description: report_agent._summarize_readings took `latest` as `vals[-1]` -- the last element of a list built in ROW order. The SQL lane orders `timestamp DESC`, so the last row is the oldest. Measured on a three-row fixture reading 1000 / 900 / 400 newest-first: the summary reported latest=400.0 against a true 1000.0. Positional 'latest' is correct only when rows arrive ascending, and this lane's never do.
Root_Cause: Position used as a proxy for recency, with no timestamp comparison anywhere.
Fix_Approach: services/reading_quality.py resolves `latest` by comparing timestamps, and carries `latest_at` so the claim is checkable. A test asserts ascending, descending and shuffled input all produce identical statistics.
Verification: tests/test_counts_and_aggregates_mean_what_they_say.py (A10 block).

Title: A narrow-table report averaged CO2 ppm with temperature degC into one number
Description: A narrow-table result carries every modality in one column named `value`. `_summarize_readings` grouped BY COLUMN, so on rows of 900 ppm CO2 and 21.5 degC it reported `avg=590.5, min=21.5, max=900.0` under the field name 'value' -- and `_extract_highlights` printed that as a report bullet. Every input was real; the output is not a quantity. Only the wide table's one-column-per-sensor shape hid this, and bldg1 uses both.
Root_Cause: The summary keyed on the column name, which IS the sensor in a wide table and is the modality-agnostic string 'value' in a narrow one. No unit was consulted at any point: services/units.py shipped with V12-04 with an aggregation_decision() built for exactly this and nothing imported it.
Fix_Approach: Narrow results are grouped by uuid and labelled from sensor_metadata (threaded through _build_sections from the bus). A cross-sensor aggregate is produced only when units.aggregation_decision permits it, and the REFUSAL is recorded and rendered rather than applied silently.
Verification: tests/test_counts_and_aggregates_mean_what_they_say.py -- asserts 590.5 appears nowhere, the two modalities summarise separately, and the refusal reaches a highlight line. LIVE RE-ASK OWED on a narrow-table report.

Title: Rows dropped by the numeric filter were never counted, so a reading count could not be audited
Description: `vals = [r[f] for r in records if isinstance(r.get(f), (int, float))]` silently discarded nulls, strings and duplicates. A report saying '1,000 readings' could not be told apart from '1,000 of 1,340 readings'. Same disease as BUG-479 one layer down: the filter did not fail, it under-reported.
Root_Cause: No accounting between the rows fetched and the rows summarised.
Fix_Approach: reading_quality.screen() returns accepted rows AND a QualitySummary with a per-reason exclusion count (not a number / duplicate / no usable timestamp), plus an out_of_order flag which is recorded rather than treated as an exclusion. The counts reach the summary dict and the highlight line.
Verification: tests/test_counts_and_aggregates_mean_what_they_say.py (A12 block).

Title: The census overlap probe costs one extra SPARQL query per inventory answer
Description: overlap_notes() runs a second query over the surviving census classes to measure which are strict subsets of which. It is bounded (at most 25 classes, one GROUP BY scan) and returns [] on any failure so the census still answers -- but it is a real added round trip on a path that previously made one.
Root_Cause: Containment cannot be decided from the census result alone: the (count, lo, hi) fingerprint gives a necessary but not sufficient condition, and asserting overlap on that would sometimes be false. Brick subclass structure would answer it without a query, but whether two classes overlap in THIS building is a fact about its ABox -- 139 supply-air and 140 zone-air sensors share nothing.
Fix_Approach: Accepted. Measure the added latency on a live inventory question before optimising.
Verification: Superseded by BUG-535: the probe is disabled. The unmeasured cost was a 14-minute GraphDB stall.

Title: A co-reference rewrite could swap the room the user had just named, and the gate could not tell
Description: rewrite_to_standalone accepted any LLM rewrite that was non-empty, under 500 chars and not identical to the input. Nothing checked it was about the same place the user named. The rewrite then becomes the query EVERY downstream stage sees -- classification, entity extraction, SPARQL and the referent EXISTENCE GATE. So a rewrite turning 'what about room 3.27?' into a question about 5.01 is not caught later: it is laundered, because 5.01 exists and the gate passes.
Root_Cause: The rewrite is an LLM call over six messages of history with no deterministic post-check. The three guards it had are all about SHAPE (empty / too long / unchanged), none about FAITHFULNESS.
Fix_Approach: services/context_switch.rewrite_is_safe() compares the place named in the user's message against the place named in the rewrite, using the SAME detectors the existence gate uses so the two cannot disagree. A rewrite that changes or LOSES a referent the user typed is rejected and the original is kept. It only fires when the user named a place: a follow-up naming none is the case the rewrite exists for.
Verification: tests/test_a_changed_subject_clears_what_it_invalidates.py -- 33 tests, negatives outnumbering positives. LIVE RE-ASK OWED on a two-turn room switch.

Title: Carried-forward analytics were injected into a turn about a different room
Description: main.py loaded forecast_result/analytics_result from the previous turn and applied them with an unconditional `state.intermediate_results.update(carry_forward)`. Ask about room 5.01, then 'what about room 3.27? plot it', and the plot is built from 5.01's analytics under a question naming 3.27 -- every figure real, attributed to the wrong room.
Root_Cause: Carry-forward was designed for 'now plot that', which names no place, and the place-naming case was never separated from it.
Fix_Approach: context_switch.prune_inherited() drops only PLACE_BOUND_KEYS, and only when BOTH questions name a place and the places differ. Preferences and other non-place state survive, and an ordinary follow-up keeps everything -- clearing defensively would trade a rare wrong answer for a constant one.
Verification: Same test file; the wiring test asserts the prune runs BEFORE the update. LIVE RE-ASK OWED.

Title: An ambiguous room label resolves to 'exists' with no record that several rooms matched
Description: ReferentResolver._exists runs `CONTAINS(LCASE(STR(?s)), token) ... LIMIT 1`. A token that is a PREFIX of several real ids -- '5.1' against Room5.10, Room5.11, Room5.12 -- returns the first match and the gate reports RESOLVED. Nothing records that the label was ambiguous, so a downstream lane silently selects one of them. Found while building V12-11; NOT the cross-building case that row's A13 names, which is prevented by construction (every resolver query filters STRSTARTS(STR(?s), namespace) -- verified structurally over all four).
Root_Cause: LIMIT 1 cannot count, and CONTAINS is a substring match over ids that share prefixes.
Fix_Approach: Not attempted. The shape would be: gather up to N matching subjects, extract their DISTINCT dotted ids (the way _suggest already does -- counting subjects would overcount, since every sensor in Room5.01 contains '5.01'), and return a new AMBIGUOUS status when more than one id matches and none equals the token exactly. That needs a handler at BOTH gate consumers in _orchestrator.py or the status is computed and ignored, which is the V6-T10 failure -- so it is a row, not a tail-end patch.
Verification: MEASUREMENT OWED: confirm on the live graph that a prefix token matches several rooms.

Title: 24 settings in .env.example are read by nothing, so configuring them does nothing
Description: Measured over orchestrator/, shared/, scripts/, frontend/src/, every compose file, every Dockerfile and every database_registry*.yaml: 24 names in .env.example are read by no reader at all. MOCK_LLM, DEV_MODE, SKIP_MODEL_DOWNLOAD, ALLOWED_AUDIO_FORMATS and MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB were never implemented; the four QDRANT_*_COLLECTION names are superseded by per-building derivation; RAG_TOP_K and SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD moved into code; the DEMO_EXTERNAL_* and WIZTEST_* sets are entered through the admin FORM, not the environment. A newcomer sets one, observes no change, and concludes the system ignores its own configuration.
Root_Cause: A template that only ever grew. Nothing checked the reverse direction.
Fix_Approach: Not deleted -- 'nothing in this repo reads it' is not 'nobody needs it', and a deployment script outside this tree might. Listed in _READ_BY_NOTHING in tests/test_every_setting_is_discoverable.py with a written reason each, and the list is CLOSED: the test fails if it grows, so the next dead setting has to be argued for.
Verification: tests/test_every_setting_is_discoverable.py -- 9 tests. Deletion deferred deliberately.

Title: A concept rule cannot say WHICH floor or space it covers
Description: RuleTrigger has `concept` and now `scope`, but no spatial qualifier. So `humidity_damp_floor3` cannot express 'floor 3': with scope:all it would notify about humidity on every floor, and with scope:first_reporting it watches one arbitrary point. Both are wrong about the floor; only the second is wrong QUIETLY, which is why it is what ships. The rule's NAME is the only place the intended scope exists, and nothing enforces a name.
Root_Cause: The trigger model was built for a direct uuid and extended with a concept; the spatial half was never added.
Fix_Approach: Add an optional `floor` / `space` to RuleTrigger and narrow _uuids_for_class with a SPARQL clause on the space->floor relation, the same traversal the spatial lane already uses. Then input/rules.yaml can declare `floor: '3'` and `scope: all` together, and the rule means what its name says for the first time.

Title: A stale named graph was the ONLY home of two live lay terms, and every other measure called it redundant
Description: The V12-15 sweep found `urn:ontosage:schema` -- 1,439 triples -- alongside `urn:ontosage:ttl:ontosage_schema.ttl` (2,710), holding the same OCBV schema. 1,325 triples differ between them; 27 exist only in the stale graph and 25 of those are SHACL blank nodes from an older load (blank-node identities change per load, so re-uploading the file created new ones while the old ones persisted). Four shape subjects -- ConceptShape, CapabilityShape, ReportShape and one more -- carry sh:property pointing at BOTH sets, so every constraint is duplicated across the union. That is harmless while the two agree and is BUG-194's exact mechanism the moment they do not: an edit to the file that reports success and does not take effect, because the old constraint still applies from a graph nothing writes to. THE PART THAT MATTERS: the remaining 2 non-blank triples are `ontosage:HandoverRecord ontosage:layTerms 'handover', 'handovers'` -- present in the stale graph and ABSENT from the file. The two shortest and most likely phrasings of that question were being answered by a graph the uploader no longer maintains.
Root_Cause: Two upload paths wrote the same schema under different graph names at different times; ttl_uploader now maintains only the filename-derived one and has no reason to touch the other, so the old graph persists indefinitely and the PDP/resolver query the union.
Fix_Approach: The two missing lay terms added to ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl FIRST, with the reason above the block so nobody re-drops them. Only then is the stale graph provably redundant and safe to drop. This is exactly the 'prove the loss is zero with a subject-level diff before you drop' procedure CLAUDE.md already documents for the fan-out case, and it earned its keep: every aggregate measure said the graph was pure duplication.
Verification: File re-parsed: 2,712 triples, HandoverRecord now carries 12 lay terms including 'handover' and 'handovers'. LIVE RE-ASK OWED: restart so ttl_uploader re-syncs, confirm the lay terms resolve from the FILE graph, then drop urn:ontosage:schema and re-run the sweep.

Title: A naive shadowing sweep reports 11,145 subjects, and every one of them is inference
Description: The obvious query -- subject in a named graph AND matching outside it -- returns 11,145 subjects on bldg1. Restricted to EXPLICIT statements (FROM <http://www.ontotext.com/explicit>) the answer is ZERO: there is not one explicit triple outside a named graph in this repository. The 11,145 are GraphDB materialising inferred triples into the implicit context. A sweep reporting that number would send someone deleting inference.
Root_Cause: GraphDB's default-graph semantics include inferred statements unless the query says otherwise.
Fix_Approach: scripts/audit_default_graph_shadowing.py runs BOTH queries and reports the pair, so the inference figure is visible as inference rather than absent or mistaken for a finding.
Verification: Measured live on the bldg repository 2026-09-12: 11,145 naive, 0 explicit.

Title: 77 sensors carry TWO timeseries references, so one answer merges a synthetic store and a real one
Description: Found by chasing V12-15's graph shadowing. 77 sensors on bldg1 have two `ref:hasExternalReference` nodes resolving to DIFFERENT uuids in DIFFERENT stores. Measured pairs: database1_synth|occupancy_data 26, |equipment_data 12, |submeter_data 10, |iaq_data 7, |water_data 6, |humidity_data 6, |waterflow_data 2, |temperature_data 1, plus database1|equipment_data 1. Example: Entry_Count_Sensor_Main -> uuid 00000000-ac02-...-0001 @ database1_synth AND uuid 97243f56-b7c1-5386-87bd-613093c1698a @ occupancy_data. The generated SPARQL binds ?sensor ?uuid ?storage with no cardinality restriction, so BOTH rows reach the SQL lane, which fetches from both stores and merges -- min/max/avg are computed across a synthetic placeholder series and the real one at once.
Root_Cause: CORRECTED 2026-09-15 — the earlier text ('two provisioning passes each added a reference') was wrong. The cause is scripts/normalise_timeseries_links.py (2026-09-06), which promotes s223:/brick: hasExternalReference links to ref: with a guard checked PER REFERENCE (FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?s ref:hasExternalReference ?r }) instead of per sensor. A sensor already linked by its building file (bldg1_sensor_links.ttl) to its real narrow table, and also carrying a SATURATE-era s223: link to database1_synth, got the synthetic link promoted as a second canonical reference. Measured: 89 of the 126 promoted links landed on already-linked sensors; 66 of the 77 duals are exactly this shape (real table in the file graph, database1_synth in the derived graph); 70 of those sensors have rows in BOTH stores, so the merge is live, not latent. The fix that made 106 invisible sensors reachable is what created the defect. The remaining ~11 duals are a different shape (bldg1_timeseries_extension.ttl vs the energy/occupancy graphs, two uuids in the SAME table) and are untouched by this fix.
Fix_Approach: Script fixed: the guard is now per sensor (_ONLY_UNLINKED, ?anyRef), used by both the dry-run count and the insert; the fixed dry-run finds 0 to promote, where the OLD script would have promoted 19 more duplicates if re-run. Pinned by tests/test_normalisation_never_adds_a_second_series.py. GRAPH CLEANUP PREPARED, NOT APPLIED: drop <urn:ontosage:derived:timeseries_link_normalisation>, re-run the fixed script; predicted result 38 links onto 37 genuinely unlinked sensors (was 126). Held until after the Tuesday regression probe so the probe measures the 2026-09-12 code and the data change can be attributed separately. The ~11 same-table duals remain for V12-34.
Verification: 2026-09-15 GRAPH CLEANUP APPLIED after the probe. Backed up the derived graph (volumes/derived_link_graph_backup_2026-09-15.ttl, 305 lines), CLEAR GRAPH <urn:ontosage:derived:timeseries_link_normalisation>, re-ran the fixed script: 37 links asserted, 0 unreachable. MEASURED: sensors with two distinct timeseries uuids 77 -> 6; derived graph 127 -> 37 triples (predicted 38); 2,764 sensors keep a canonical link. Redis SPARQL + response caches flushed. STILL OPEN for the 6 same-table duals (bldg1_timeseries_extension.ttl vs the energy/occupancy graphs), owned by V12-34. LIVE ANSWER-LEVEL CHECK OWED: one question on a formerly dual sensor, confirming a single store is fetched. || MEASUREMENT ONLY. Note that the project's documented integrity metric CANNOT see this: timeseries fan-out reads exactly 1.00 copies/uuid (2,841 refs / 2,841 distinct uuids) because each reference carries its OWN uuid. A metric that is healthy while 77 sensors answer from two sources at once is measuring the wrong thing for this defect.

Title: Every adapter's safety check crashed on its own first line when handed an unbuilt query
Description: `build_timeseries_query` returns None when it cannot build one -- an unvalidated uuid, an empty list -- and callers hand the result straight to `execute_query`. Every `validate_query` began `sql.upper().strip()`, so a None query raised `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'upper'` INSIDE THE SAFETY CHECK. The lane above saw an unrelated type error three layers from the actual mistake, rather than a refusal naming the cause. Found while writing the V12-13 parity test, whose first run reproduced it exactly by omitting get_columns().
Root_Cause: The validators assumed a string because the happy path always supplies one. Nothing in the adapter contract says build_timeseries_query can return None, and seven adapters each trusted it independently.
Fix_Approach: All seven validators (postgres, cassandra, mysql, sqlite, influx, mongo, redis-timeseries) now refuse None and empty with a ValueError naming the usual cause: get_columns() has not run, so no uuid is yet known to be valid. Whitespace keeps each adapter's own 'Only SELECT queries are allowed' wording -- a malformed query is a different fault from an unbuilt one.
Verification: tests/test_adapter_parity_and_snapshot.py -- parametrised over all seven adapters; sqlite skips where aiosqlite is absent.

Title: Two live adapter tests were pinned to a uuid from one seed run and could pass only once
Description: tests/test_timescale_cassandra_adapters.py hardcoded UUID_A = 'b1aca4d6-715e-5189-aec1-afe52c426813'. seed_timeseries_backends.py chooses its sensors from the LIVE graph, so once the graph changed the constant stopped matching and both live tests failed against perfectly healthy, correctly seeded servers. The failure looked like an adapter fault and was a test-data fault.
Root_Cause: A test pinned to data it does not control.
Fix_Approach: _roundtrip now reads the uuids back from the store via get_columns() and queries one the store actually holds. It also calls get_columns() BEFORE building, which is the adapter contract BUG-532 documents.
Verification: 26 passed against live TimescaleDB and Cassandra (was 24 passed / 2 failed).

Title: A floor comparison silently averaged 5 of floor 1's 13 CO2 sensors
Description: Live, probe case w0 'Compare the average CO2 on floor 1 versus floor 3', 2026-09-14 23:11. SPARQL returned 64 uuids, 61 in database1_floors04. sql_agent caps each storage group at _UUID_CAP = 30 by slicing grouped_uuids[key][:30] and logs one WARNING. Mapped back to sensors: floor 1 has 13 CO2 sensors in that store and floor 3 has 48; the slice KEPT 5 floor-1 and 25 floor-3, and DROPPED 8 floor-1 (62%) and 23 floor-3 (48%). The answer states a floor-1 average computed over 5 of 13 sensors with no disclosure. The probe PASSED, because its marker checks the answer's shape. Which sensors survive is whatever order SPARQL returned, which is not guaranteed — another run could keep zero floor-1 sensors and 'compare' floor 3 against nothing.
Root_Cause: A sensor cap with no record. rows_capped (BUG-479) covers the ROW limit only; this cap never enters skipped_reasons/points_omitted, so nothing downstream can see it. The comment beside it says deterministic SQL handles many uuids correctly — the cap is a leftover from LLM-prompt sizing, applied to a path that no longer needs it.
Fix_Approach: Planned Tue 15 after the probe: (1) record every dropped uuid in skipped_reasons with a reason so the answer states 'N of M sensors'; (2) select the kept set deterministically and spread across the question's scope rather than by result order, or lift the cap for deterministic aggregate SQL. CHECKED AND REFUTED 2026-09-15: row starvation is NOT part of this defect. The floors04 query returned 30,000 rows = 1,000 per uuid x 30 (per-uuid ROW_NUMBER limit works), co2_data 2,000, iaq_data 1,000. The log line '1000 reading(s) excluded as physically impossible across 1 sensor' in the same turn is ONE sensor whose every reading fell outside the plausible range; it was correctly kept out of the average (CAVEAT-410 class), not merged in. The defect is the sensor cap alone.
Verification: Live 2026-09-15 after restart: the comparison turn logged 'Fetching data for 61 UUIDs from storage: database1_floors04' (was 30); w0 group 7/7. tests/test_a_sensor_cap_is_stated_and_sized_for_a_floor.py (AST: cap >= 61, <= MAX_FETCH_UUIDS, sorted before slicing, points_capped recorded and said). COST FOUND: the turn now takes 251 s — BUG-537.

Title: The census overlap probe I added on 2026-09-12 took GraphDB down for 14 minutes and failed 7 probe cases
Description: Full regression probe 2026-09-15: 50/59 against a 57/59 baseline. 8 of the 9 failures were transport TIMEOUT. Log timeline: every case 10-25 s until 23:19:10 'How many CO2 sensors are there?' -> census -> overlap_notes() -> 'overlap probe failed: ReadTimeout' at 23:19:46; 23:19:48 'How many sensors are there?' (a second census) -> 'GraphDB retrieval failed: ReadTimeout'; then one request EXACTLY every 120 s (the client timeout) for 7 consecutive cases — DEP-13 stakeholders, Room 9.99, swimming pool, two circulation, lab recovery — until recovery ~23:34. None of those 7 questions touches the census; they failed because GraphDB was busy.
Root_Cause: overlap_notes() (V12-09, CAVEAT-523) ran a self-join `?s a ?a, ?b` with BIND(REPLACE(STR(?a)...)) and FILTER(?an IN (...)) — a string function over every type pair in the repository, which no index can serve. Its httpx client gave up after 25 s, but a client timeout does NOT cancel the query in GraphDB, so each census question left a runaway query behind. CAVEAT-523 logged 'one extra round trip, latency unmeasured' — it was never measured, and the unmeasured cost was an outage.
Fix_Approach: Disabled: OVERLAP_PROBE_ENABLED = False in ontology_inventory.py; the census renders exactly as before V12-09. An index-driven rewrite (VALUES on class IRIs) was measured at 3.1 s for 6 classes with ?timeout=5 server-side, still too slow per question, and its answer is almost entirely inferred subclass nesting that the static Brick TBox gives for free. After the demo: compute containment from the TBox. GENERAL FINDING: no GraphDB call in this codebase passes a server-side ?timeout=, so any slow query can outlive its client and cascade the same way (CAVEAT-536).
Verification: Targeted re-run of the failed probe groups owed after restart.

Title: No GraphDB query sets a server-side timeout, so a slow query outlives its client and stalls every later one
Description: BUG-535 showed the mechanism: httpx timed out at 25 s, GraphDB kept executing, and the next 7 unrelated questions timed out behind it. RDF4J/GraphDB honours a `timeout` request parameter (seconds) that aborts the query server-side; nothing in orchestrator/ passes it.
Fix_Approach: After the demo: pass ?timeout= on every SPARQL POST, derived from the same budget as the client timeout, in one helper rather than 40 call sites. Not before Friday — it touches every graph call.

Title: A floor comparison is aggregated by the LLM from per-sensor lines, and took 251 s once every sensor was read
Description: After BUG-534 raised the sensor cap, 'Compare the average CO2 on floor 1 versus floor 3' read all 61 sensors — and took 251 s end to end, against ~72 s with 30. Node timeline: SQL 1 s (61,000 rows), analytics sandbox 3 s, then ~210 s in ONE narration call: a 13,342-char prompt with the analysis output for 64 sensors plus 64 sensor descriptions. The template computes PER-SENSOR averages; the question asks for PER-FLOOR ones, so the model is left to aggregate 64 lines into two numbers itself — arithmetic by LLM on the most quotable figure in the answer.
Root_Cause: Floor membership is known inside the SPARQL floor-scoped template (sensor -> space -> floor) and dropped before the analytics lane: sensor_metadata carries label, sensor_uri, uuid, kind and unit, no floor. With nothing to group by, the only aggregation available is in the prose.
Fix_Approach: Planned Wed-16 as the floor-comparison slice of V12-28: bind ?floor in the floor-scoped template, carry it in sensor_metadata, compute per-floor mean/min/max/sensor-count deterministically, and give the narrator only that summary. Expected effect: prompt shrinks from 64 lines to 2, the figures stop being model arithmetic. Until then the question is kept OUT of the demo script; the 120-sensor cap stays, because a fast average over 5 of 13 sensors is not a better answer.
Verification: sensor_metadata carries floorNum; series_summary.summarise_groups computes per-floor sensor count, readings, mean/range (energy also totalled) behind units.aggregation_decision; analytics narration gets those lines and a 1,500-char cap on sandbox output instead of 64 per-sensor lines. tests/test_a_floor_comparison_is_computed_not_narrated.py (13). Live latency re-measure owed (RUN-06).

Title: One database, two clocks: the real wide table is local time and the synthetic narrow tables are UTC
Description: Measured 2026-09-15 at 00:23:42 UTC / 01:23:42 BST: newest sensor_data (wide) row 01:23:17 — LOCAL; newest co2_data, occupancy_data and sensor_data_synth (narrow) rows 00:22 — UTC. Host MySQL NOW() is local (time_zone SYSTEM); the data-publisher container runs UTC with no TZ set and writes its own clock into the narrow tables. So every time window and every freshness age in this system is correct for one kind of table and an hour wrong for the other during BST. The 2026-09-12 V12-08 work (BUG-517/518/519) moved several clock reads from utcnow() to building-local time on the documented premise 'the stores hold local stamps' — true for the wide table, FALSE for the narrow tables. Those fixes corrected floor-5 (real, wide) answers and shifted narrow-table windows and ages by an hour the other way. Remaining utcnow() readers (event_query_service:388, dialogue_agent._resolve_relative_dt, anomaly diagnosis/scanner, compliance_register_service) are each right or wrong depending on which table the question lands on. Found while diagnosing 'Is Room 1.06 free for the next two hours?' (events lane on utcnow(); separately, 'next N hours' is not parsed and falls back to the whole day).
Root_Cause: No declared timestamp convention per datasource. database_registry.yaml records `nature` per store but not its clock, so every reader has to assume one, and two generators assumed differently.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED — needs a design decision, not a one-line swap. Options: (a) source fix — set the building timezone on the data-publisher service so new narrow rows are local; existing narrow history stays UTC, leaving a one-hour seam at the switch; (b) principled — declare `timestamps: local|utc` per store in database_registry.yaml and convert each window to the store's clock in the adapter, so no reader assumes; (c) for the demo only — build the script on floor-5 rooms (real data, wide table, local stamps), where the 2026-09-12 fixes are correct, and avoid time-sensitive questions on floors 0-4. Decide Wednesday morning.
Verification: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-15: the premise was a measurement error. The stores are UTC (BUG-403): mysql_adapter pins every session to +00:00; sensor_data is a TIMESTAMP column, which MySQL converts to the SESSION zone on read, so a measurement through a SYSTEM-zone (BST) session made it LOOK local. Read on a +00:00 session at 00:34 UTC the newest rows were sensor_data 00:34, co2_data/occupancy_data 00:33, sensor_data_synth 00:32; events are generated from utcnow(). There is one clock, not two. Option (a) (TZ on data-publisher) was NOT applied: the publisher forces a +00:00 session regardless of TZ, and changing that would have reintroduced BUG-403.

Title: 'Is Room 1.06 free for the next two hours?' is answered about the whole day
Description: Live 01:20 BST: answer '**Room1.06 is booked today**: 08:20-18:00' — true, but the next two hours are free and the answer implies they are not. event_query_service.parse_window recognises 'at 2pm', named days, parts of day, 'right now', but not 'next N hours', so it falls back to the whole day. CORRECTION 2026-09-15: event_query_service's utcnow() is CORRECT for the store; what is wrong is (1) 'today' taken as the UTC day and (2) booking times SHOWN in UTC — '08:20-18:00' is 09:20-19:00 in the building. Both belong with the display fix (RUN-07/08).
Fix_Approach: parse_window: 'next/coming N hours|minutes' (digits or words) -> [now, now+N], labelled 'for the next N hours'. EventQueryService parses on the building's clock (to_local(store now)) and converts the window back with to_store, so 'today' and 'at 3pm' are the building's.
Verification: tests/test_event_times_are_local_to_people_and_utc_to_stores.py (12). Live re-ask owed: 'Is Room1.06 free for the next two hours?' (RUN-11).

Title: Stored UTC times are shown to people as if they were building-local
Description: Every store is UTC (BUG-403). Where an answer prints a stored time — booking intervals ('Room1.06 is booked today: 08:20-18:00' is 09:20-19:00 in the building under BST), a reading's 'latest at', a recheck line — it prints the UTC wall clock with no zone. A person reads it as local and is an hour out.
Fix_Approach: EventQueryService._fmt_dt converts stored times (datetime or string) to the building zone; RecheckAdvice.describe(tz_name=) shows 'measured at' and 'recheck by' locally while the age stays one-clock UTC; the orchestrator passes building_tz() to both. No zone -> unchanged. Reading timestamps narrated by the LLM already carry an explicit 'UTC' label, which is honest; left as is.
Verification: Same test file (booking 07:20Z shown 08:20; recheck 00:20Z shown 01:20 with a 5-minute age). Live re-ask owed (RUN-11).

Title: seed_timeseries_backends.py re-serialises database_registry.yaml, deleting its documentation and writing a literal password
Description: Running the seeder on 2026-09-12 to register TimescaleDB and Cassandra rewrote bldg1/database_registry.yaml wholesale: 358 insertions, 786 deletions. The deletions are the file's hand-written comments (nature/provenance notes, placeholder syntax docs), lost because yaml.safe_dump cannot round-trip comments. It also wrote `password: ontosage_ts_secret` as a literal instead of a ${TIMESCALE_PASSWORD:-...} placeholder, so the registry would carry a credential in version control.
Root_Cause: The seeder loads, mutates and dumps YAML instead of appending text; the entry it writes uses resolved values.
Fix_Approach: Checkpoint 2026-09-15: file restored from HEAD, the two entries NOT committed (the parity tests build their adapters directly). Fix after the demo: append the entry as TEXT with ${VAR:-default} placeholders, never re-dump the file.

Title: An Open WebUI login whose OntoSage username is not the email's local part chats as readonly
Description: resolve_forwarded_user's comment said 'match on username first, then email'; the code only looked up usernames (the full email, then its local part). The owner's Open WebUI login suhasdevmanemech@gmail.com maps to the OntoSage admin 'Suhas' by nothing, so every chat created a readonly placeholder row and ran at least privilege: metadata only, for the account the demo is given from.
Root_Cause: Prose described a lookup that was never written (lesson #102 shape: the comment was trusted, not the code).
Fix_Approach: postgres_manager.get_users_by_email (case-insensitive); resolver order is exact username -> registered email -> local part, placeholders skipped at every step. The Suhas account's email was set to the Open WebUI login (it was NULL; the account was already admin in both systems).
Verification: tests/test_forwarded_user_rbac.py 11/11 (3 new). Live /v1: log '[forwarded-user] suhasdevmanemech@gmail.com -> Suhas (role=admin)', CO2 answer for 5.01 in 29.4 s.

Title: A chart keyword inside another word draws a chart, and an empty dataset is charted and narrated as a finding
Description: _user_wants_visualization tested `kw in msg`, so 'mapped' matched 'map', 'drawing more power' matched 'drawing', 'reconfigure' matched 'figure', 'solar panels' matched 'panel': 70 of 4,060 stakeholder questions (word-boundary: 0 of those). Stakeholder run #1 Q2 ('Which permission groups ... mapped opening can be evidenced?') was answered with an empty bar chart narrated as 'no bars appear, indicating that either all groups have an assigned owner or the data is missing'. _visualization_node called the viz agent even when the pre-chart fetch returned nothing.
Root_Cause: Substring matching; no empty-data guard before LLM chart code generation.
Fix_Approach: Whole-word regex over the keyword list; 'drawing' removed (building sense: power draw, design drawings). The viz node records viz_result skipped=no_data with no media when there is still nothing to chart, so dispatch falls through to what the other lanes found.
Verification: tests/test_a_chart_is_asked_for_in_words_and_drawn_from_data.py (16) + routing_accuracy / pipeline_ctx / safety_net 100 green. Live re-ask owed (RUN-11).

Title: Checking that an absent word is not in the graph scans every triple and times out; a dead Fuseki fallback hides the timeout
Description: ReferentResolver._exists ran `?s ?p ?o` with STRSTARTS + CONTAINS + an EXISTS label check per subject. A present token hits LIMIT 1 in <1 s; an absent one scans the graph: 27.6 s measured on bldg1, over the 30 s httpx timeout under load. Stakeholder run #1 Q3 ('room moves') declined with 'the existence check didn't complete in time' after 37 s. sparql_agent then tried Fuseki, which is commented out of compose, and its DNS error ('Name or service not known') replaced GraphDB's ReadTimeout, whose message is empty.
Root_Cause: A whole-graph scan used as an existence test; a fallback that overwrites the primary error.
Fix_Approach: Two narrow lookups: rdfs:label CONTAINS (short-circuits), then typed-subject IRI CONTAINS. Measured on 5.01/atrium/kitchen/chiller: same hits as the old query; ~2.5 s per miss lookup. Fuseki failure re-raises the GraphDB error; the error carries its exception type.
Verification: tests/test_an_absent_word_is_checked_without_scanning_the_graph.py (4) + 98 referent tests green. Live re-ask owed (RUN-11).

Title: Approval words used as adjectives send a question to the approvals register, which answers it wrongly and states the absence as fact
Description: ApprovalRecord's layTerms include approved/confirmed/verified/authorised/evidenced (declared deliberately: 53% of unanswered corpus questions use them). Scoring made the adjective use count the same as the predicative one. Stakeholder run #1, as admin via /v1: Q6 'started late against today's APPROVED schedule' -> 'APR-010 ... 1 day late' (an approval date read as a start time); Q14 'lack CONFIRMED fire-warden coverage' -> 'None of the occupied zones have a confirmed fire-warden' (absence in the wrong register, stated about fire safety); Q16 'VERIFIED alternative location'. Separately EventActivity's bare 'activities' pulled Q8/Q15 (continuity, first-aid) into a raw 56-row open-day dump.
Root_Cause: Lay-term scoring is lexical; the TBox had no way to say a term names the class only when used of it.
Fix_Approach: TBox: new ontosage:qualifierTerms property; ApprovalRecord declares seven qualifiers; EventActivity loses bare activity/activities. record_registry reads qualifierTerms and scores a qualifier 0 when the next word is a content word (attributive), full weight when followed by a function word or nothing. Corpus impact measured before landing: 659 of 4,060 questions change register (356 no longer claimed by any register, go to classification); samples: 'approved weekend service or event' -> PublicEvent, 'approved high-contrast display preset' -> AVReadiness.
Verification: tests/test_a_qualifier_names_its_register_only_when_used_of_it.py (14) + 450 register/schema tests green. ROUTING CHANGE: register probe group and stakeholder re-run owed after restart (RUN-10/13).

Title: Register handovers overflow the prompt into raw dumps, and their narration maps fields onto other concepts, certifies, and does not know the date
Description: Stakeholder run #1 via /v1: (a) routes+workspaces passed the 1,300-CELL budget but rendered 55.9k chars (prompt 58,848; every empty completion logged was >=56k at num_ctx 16384): three empty completions, then _format_results returned the raw bindings ('Found 44 result(s): 1. register: …') — Q8, Q15, Q25. (b) the narration prompt is the generic sensor-list one plus 'answer only from these records': Q6 read approval dates as plant start times, Q27 approval statuses as no-shows, Q24 certified that compliance records 'are retained for the correct period, in the authorised system', Q29 said 'events due today (2026-09-05)' on 15 Sep (a retrievedAt stamp).
Root_Cause: Budget in cells not characters; lineage columns repeated on every row; fallback dumps rows; no date and no rule against re-mapping or certifying.
Fix_Approach: _render_rows hoists values every row of a register shares into one header per register (label/id/status never hoisted; padded gaps listed once) — routes+workspaces 55.9k -> 30.0k, workspace+circulation 50.7k -> 27.4k; MAX_RECORD_CHARS=34000 measured with the same renderer on the primary, the scoped re-fetch and the second register; LLM failure on a handover returns a named-records list that states no conclusion; guidance adds building-local date and rules: say plainly when the records do not record it, never map a field onto another concept, never certify/approve/guarantee, never call a record 'yours'.
Verification: tests/test_a_register_handover_fits_the_prompt_and_says_what_it_lacks.py (7) + 422 sparql/register tests green (3 non-unit tests needing live services fail as before). Live re-ask of Q6/Q8/Q14/Q15/Q24/Q25/Q27/Q29 owed after restart.

Title: A count of sensors was reported as a measured quantity ('269 daylight hours in the deepest workstation')
Description: Stakeholder run #1 Q51 'Whats the daylight hour count in the deepest workstation this December?' generated SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sensor) AS ?count) WHERE { ?sensor rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf* brick:Illuminance_Sensor } = 269 and was narrated 'The deepest workstation recorded 269 daylight hours during December'. The numeric guard passed it because 269 is in the result; the meaning was invented.
Root_Cause: The generic SPARQL narration prompt gives rows with no statement of what an aggregate counts.
Fix_Approach: _count_meaning parses COUNT aggregates (and GROUP BY) from the executed query and prefixes the rows with what each alias counts and that a count is not a reading, measurement, duration or amount; the model must say the model does not hold the asked quantity.
Verification: tests in test_a_register_handover_fits_the_prompt_and_says_what_it_lacks.py (4). Live re-ask of Q51 owed.

Title: A question queued an actuation command, and another question filed a maintenance report
Description: Stakeholder run #1 as admin via /v1. Q57 'Which shutters or doors fail open versus fail locked on power loss?': LLM said metadata; routing_contract actuation_control overrode to control because _CONTROL_VERB_TARGET_RE matched 'open ... lock(ed) ... power'; ControlAgent._queue_pending_approval then fell back to writable_caps[0] and value 'as specified' and answered 'Command queued for approval (ID 11a94eda). Target: urn:bldg1:AHU-F5-SP -> ``' — one 'approve' from a sim write of an AHU setpoint. Q56 'Which drains have needed jetting more than twice this year?': classified maintenance ('a maintenance history query'), and _report_intake_node's classify_action defaults to create, so REP-452756 was written to user_reports. Any maintenance-schedule question the contract routes to maintenance does the same.
Root_Cause: Verb/keyword command detection with no notion of a question; unsafe defaults (first point, placeholder value; create).
